 └ ConsentProbe        ← present</pre> </article> </div> <p class="proof-disclosure" data-astro-cid-nj5fsqu5>Edits stay off until you allow them. This build supports a limited set of place operations. It cannot publish, upload assets or run code inside the plugin.</p> </div> </div>  <p class="proof-more" data-astro-cid-nj5fsqu5> <a href="/proof" data-astro-cid-nj5fsqu5>The whole log of one run, and the five defects it left behind &rarr;</a> </p> <p class="micro proof-source" data-astro-cid-nj5fsqu5>One refused op and one granted op is a control pair, not a capability sweep. Record: docs/evidence/plugin-consent-verified-in-studio-2026-09-19.md</p> </div> </section>  <section class="band" id="inside" aria-labelledby="truths-title"> <div class="shell"> <div class="band-head" data-reveal> <h2 id="truths-title" class="section-title">What it will and will not do</h2> <p class="section-sub">Every line here is a rule in the plugin, not a promise in a brochure.</p> </div> <div class="truths"> <article class="truth" data-reveal data-reveal-delay="0"> <p class="micro">Scope</p> <h3>One place, the one you opened</h3> <p>Apple works in the Studio place you pair it to, and nowhere else. It cannot reach your files or your other games.</p> </article><article class="truth" data-reveal data-reveal-delay="70"> <p class="micro">Consent</p> <h3>Edits are off until you allow them</h3> <p>The plugin opens read-only. Turning writes on takes two deliberate clicks, and disconnecting turns them off again.</p> </article><article class="truth" data-reveal data-reveal-delay="140"> <p class="micro">Refusals</p> <h3>It says no, by name</h3> <p>It will not run code it was sent, drive play mode, or insert an asset carrying a script. Each refusal comes back with its reason.</p> </article><article class="truth" data-reveal data-reveal-delay="210"> <p class="micro">Undo</p> <h3>Every change is one waypoint</h3> <p>Writes are wrapped in Studio’s own undo history — one step per change, so a five-step run is five presses of Ctrl+Z. To take a whole run back at once, restore the checkpoint Apple saved before it started.</p> </article> </div> </div> </section> <section class="band" aria-labelledby="sequence-title"> <div class="shell"> <div class="band-head" data-reveal> <h2 id="sequence-title" class="section-title">How a run actually goes</h2> <p class="section-sub">Three steps, in order, with the third one being the point.</p> </div> <div class="sequence"> <figure class="sequence-figure" data-reveal> <figcaption class="figure-head micro">Studio · activity</figcaption> <div class="activity"> <div class="activity-line" style="--i:0">get_project_tree game.Workspace           ok</div><div class="activity-line refused" style="--i:1">create_instances 4 parts                  refused</div><div class="activity-line refused" style="--i:2">  writes require explicit edit consent</div><div class="activity-line" style="--i:3">create_instances 4 parts                  ok</div><div class="activity-line" style="--i:4">edit_script      ServerScriptService.Main ok</div><div class="activity-line" style="--i:5">render_view      eye · 288×180            ok</div><div class="activity-line" style="--i:6">inspect_visually score 6/10 · 3 defects   ok</div> </div> </figure>  <div class="steps"> <article class="step"> <h3>Pair one place</h3> <p>A six-character code links Apple to the Studio place you have open. Nothing else in your account is in scope, and the pairing ends when you disconnect.</p> </article> <article class="step"> <h3>Say what you want</h3> <p>Plain language. Apple reads the tree, plans the change, and takes a checkpoint before it writes — so the state before the run is always recoverable.</p> </article> <article class="step"> <h3>Look at what it did</h3> <p>Every operation is named as it happens, including the ones that were refused. The result is in your place, in Studio, where you can run it.</p> </article> </div> </div> </div> </section> <section class="band" aria-labelledby="statement-title"> <div class="shell" style="text-align:center"> <h2 id="statement-title" class="statement" data-reveal>Apple builds inside Roblox Studio — in your place, with your account, under your approval.</h2> </div> </section> data-sound-dock data-astro-cid-ke3urpsc> <button class="sound-dock__btn" type="button" data-sound-toggle aria-pressed="false" aria-label="Turn interface sound on" data-astro-cid-ke3urpsc> <span data-astro-cid-ke3urpsc></canvas> <span class="sound-dock__label" data-astro-cid-ke3urpsc>Sound</span> </button> </div>  <script>/* =====================================================================================
 * INTERFACE SOUND — ONE IMPLEMENTATION, SHARED BY EVERY LAYOUT.
 *
 * This file is the whole sound system. Base.astro and Landing.astro both inline THIS TEXT
 * through layouts/InterfaceSound.astro, so there is one synth, one listener and one stored
 * preference for the entire site. Before this there was a copy in Base.astro and nothing at all
 * on the front page, which is two states that cannot agree and one page with no control.
 *
 * WHAT THE OWNER ASKED FOR. He played with rosebud.ai and singled out one thing: pressing a button
 * makes a satisfying mechanical keyboard click. Measured on that page the same day (recorded in
 * packages/corpus/data/ui-references/web-landing.json, claim 16): its resource timing list contains
 * no mp3, wav, ogg, m4a or webm anywhere, while AudioContext is available — so their click is
 * SYNTHESISED at interaction time, not downloaded. That is the cheaper technique and the one used
 * here. A synthesised click costs no bytes, has no load state, and cannot be the reason a button
 * feels late.
 *
 * WHAT A KEYSWITCH ACTUALLY SOUNDS LIKE, and why the old `tick()` did not. The retired version was
 * one triangle oscillator sliding down — a soft chisel tick, a single event. A mechanical key press
 * is TWO events layered: the CLICK OF THE STEM, a bright noise transient of a few milliseconds with
 * no pitch of its own, and the THOCK OF THE BOTTOM-OUT, a low short body as the key meets the
 * plate. Both are below, layered with the body starting 4ms after the transient, and the whole
 * envelope is finished inside 58ms at its longest voice.
 *
 * THE INTERFACE HAS A VOICE RATHER THAN A BEEP. Three voices, chosen the way the reference's accent
 * family is chosen — one object, three jobs: a primary action is lower and fuller, a secondary
 * lighter and shorter, a toggle a touch brighter. Every press also carries a ±2.5% wobble, because
 * a sound repeated at exactly one frequency stops reading as a mechanism and starts reading as a
 * notification.
 *
 * THE PROPERTIES THIS FILE MUST KEEP, all of them checked by tests/interface-sound.test.mjs:
 *   - OFF by default. Nothing is armed by loading a page.
 *   - The AudioContext is constructed by a PRESS and never by load — the visitor's press on the
 *     toggle, or, when a previous visit already chose sound, that session's first press. Both are
 *     real user gestures, which is what browsers require; neither is page load.
 *   - Nothing autoplays.
 *   - The choice persists exactly the way the theme choice does, in localStorage under
 *     `apple-sound`, and is read back on the next page.
 *   - Every toggle states its state in aria-pressed and aria-label.
 *   - Never on hover, never on load, never more than once per press: ONE delegated listener owns
 *     both the toggle and the press, so a press on the toggle cannot produce two sounds.
 *
 * NO `document.currentScript`. Astro hoists a component <script> into a module script where
 * currentScript is null by specification; a hero effect shipped that way this morning and never ran
 * at all. Everything here is found with querySelector, and every one of those lookups tolerates a
 * null.
 * ===================================================================================== */
(function () {
  'use strict';

  var STORE_KEY = 'apple-sound';

  /* Everything that reads as a press. Buttons and links-as-buttons across both layouts: the
     landing's `.pill`, the chrome's `.iconbtn` and `.nav__cta`, anything with an explicit
     role, and `[data-sound-press]` for a control that is none of those. A bare prose link is
     deliberately absent — navigation is not a keystroke. */
  var PRESSABLE = [
    'button',
    '[role="button"]',
    'input[type="submit"]',
    'input[type="button"]',
    'summary',
    'a.pill',
    'a.btn',
    'a.cta',
    'a.button',
    'a.nav__cta',
    'a.nav__signin',
    'a[data-cta]',
    '[data-sound-press]'
  ].join(', ');

  /* THE THREE VOICES. clickHz is the band the stem transient sits in, bodyHz the pitch of the
     bottom-out. Gains are deliberately low: this is a texture under a finger, not an alert. */
  var VOICES = {
    primary:   { clickHz: 2400, clickQ: 0.9, clickGain: 0.034, clickDur: 0.010, bodyHz: 132, bodyGain: 0.075, bodyDur: 0.044 },
    secondary: { clickHz: 3200, clickQ: 1.1, clickGain: 0.026, clickDur: 0.008, bodyHz: 196, bodyGain: 0.048, bodyDur: 0.032 },
    toggle:    { clickHz: 4200, clickQ: 1.3, clickGain: 0.036, clickDur: 0.007, bodyHz: 240, bodyGain: 0.052, bodyDur: 0.030 }
  };

  var audio = null;       // constructed by a press, never by load
  var grain = null;       // the noise buffer, built once per context
  var armed = stored();   // the visitor's persisted choice; false on a first visit

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ preference */

  function stored() {
    try {
      return localStorage.getItem(STORE_KEY) === 'on';
    } catch (err) {
      return false; /* private mode — off, which is the default anyway */
    }
  }

  function remember(on) {
    try {
      localStorage.setItem(STORE_KEY, on ? 'on' : 'off');
    } catch (err) {
      /* private mode — the choice still applies for this page view */
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the synth */

  /** Construct the context. Called from the click handler and from nowhere else. */
  function ensureAudio() {
    if (audio) return audio;
    /* The prefixed name is Safari's, and it is still how an older iOS reaches this API. The cast
       is for the type checker only; there is no TypeScript in a file that ships as it is written. */
    var w = /** @type {any} */ (window);
    var Ctx = w.AudioContext || w.webkitAudioContext;
    if (!Ctx) return null;
    audio = new Ctx();
    return audio;
  }

  /** A short burst of decaying white noise, built once and re-triggered per press. */
  function noise(ac) {
    if (grain) return grain;
    var rate = ac.sampleRate || 44100;
    var len = Math.max(64, Math.floor(rate * 0.06));
    var buf = ac.createBuffer(1, len, rate);
    var data = buf.getChannelData(0);
    for (var i = 0; i < len; i++) {
      data[i] = (Math.random() * 2 - 1) * (1 - i / len);
    }
    grain = buf;
    return grain;
  }

  /**
   * ONE PRESS. Two layered events, under 60ms, at a low gain.
   * Silent unless armed, and silent unless a press has already built the context.
   */
  function press(kind) {
    if (!armed || !audio) return false;
    if (audio.state === 'suspended' && audio.resume) audio.resume();

    var v = VOICES[kind] || VOICES.secondary;
    var t = audio.currentTime;
    var wobble = 1 + (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.05;

    /* 1. THE CLICK OF THE STEM — filtered noise, no pitch, gone in a few milliseconds. */
    var src = audio.createBufferSource();
    src.buffer = noise(audio);
    var band = audio.createBiquadFilter();
    band.type = 'bandpass';
    band.frequency.setValueAtTime(v.clickHz * wobble, t);
    band.Q.value = v.clickQ;
    var clickGain = audio.createGain();
    clickGain.gain.setValueAtTime(v.clickGain, t);
    clickGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, t + v.clickDur);
    src.connect(band).connect(clickGain).connect(audio.destination);
    src.start(t);
    src.stop(t + v.clickDur + 0.004);

    /* 2. THE THOCK OF THE BOTTOM-OUT — a low body, pitched down as it dies. */
    var at = t + 0.004;
    var osc = audio.createOscillator();
    osc.type = 'triangle';
    osc.frequency.setValueAtTime(v.bodyHz * wobble, at);
    osc.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(v.bodyHz * 0.55, at + v.bodyDur);
    var bodyGain = audio.createGain();
    bodyGain.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, at);
    bodyGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(v.bodyGain, at + 0.003);
    bodyGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, at + v.bodyDur);
    osc.connect(bodyGain).connect(audio.destination);
    osc.start(at);
    osc.stop(at + v.bodyDur + 0.008);

    hit(v);
    return true;
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the toggles */

  function toggles() {
    return document.querySelectorAll('[data-sound-toggle]');
  }

  function paint() {
    var list = toggles();
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      list[i].setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(armed));
      list[i].setAttribute(
        'aria-label',
        armed ? 'Turn interface sound off' : 'Turn interface sound on'
      );
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the meter */

  /*
   * A CANVAS THAT SHOWS THE SOUND IT IS ABOUT TO MAKE. It is the toggle's own icon: a flat line
   * while sound is off, a live trace while it is on, and a kick on every press whose height is the
   * press's own body gain. It is entirely optional — a layout without one is silent about it and
   * every other line above still runs.
   *
   * IT IS THE ONLY AMBIENT MOTION THIS FILE OWNS, AND IT STOPS THREE WAYS: it never starts while
   * sound is off, it stops on prefers-reduced-motion, and it stops on visibilitychange. A
   * backgrounded tab must not burn a core for a line nobody is looking at.
   */
  var scope = null;
  var scopeCtx = null;
  var frame = 0;
  var energy = 0;
  var phase = 0;
  var reduced = window.matchMedia ? window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') : null;

  function findScope() {
    var el = document.querySelector('[data-sound-scope]');
    if (!el || !el.getContext) return;
    scope = el;
    scopeCtx = el.getContext('2d');
  }

  function stopped() {
    return !armed || document.hidden === true || !!(reduced && reduced.matches);
  }

  function paintScope() {
    if (!scope || !scopeCtx) return;
    var w = scope.width || 0;
    var h = scope.height || 0;
    if (!w || !h) return;
    var mid = h / 2;
    var ink = '';
    if (window.getComputedStyle) {
      ink = window.getComputedStyle(scope).getPropertyValue('color');
    }
    scopeCtx.clearRect(0, 0, w, h);
    scopeCtx.beginPath();
    for (var x = 0; x <= w; x += 2) {
      var k = x / w;
      var taper = Math.sin(Math.PI * k);
      var wave = Math.sin(k * 14 + phase) * 0.55 + Math.sin(k * 31 - phase * 1.7) * 0.45;
      var amp = (0.16 + energy * 0.84) * (mid - 1.5) * taper;
      var y = mid + wave * amp;
      if (x === 0) scopeCtx.moveTo(x, y);
      else scopeCtx.lineTo(x, y);
    }
    scopeCtx.strokeStyle = ink ? ink.trim() : 'currentColor';
    scopeCtx.lineWidth = 2;
    scopeCtx.stroke();
  }

  function tickScope() {
    if (stopped()) { frame = 0; paintScope(); return; }
    phase += 0.06;
    energy *= 0.9;
    if (energy < 0.004) energy = 0;
    paintScope();
    frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tickScope);
  }

  function runScope() {
    /* The CSS half of the same stop. Every ambient rule in InterfaceSound.astro is paused by this
       attribute, so prefers-reduced-motion, a hidden tab and "sound is off" all halt the keyframes
       as well as the canvas — one predicate, not two that can disagree. */
    var still = stopped();
    if (document.documentElement && document.documentElement.setAttribute) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-sound-still', still ? 'true' : 'false');
    }
    if (!scope) return;
    if (frame) { window.cancelAnimationFrame(frame); frame = 0; }
    if (still) { paintScope(); return; }
    frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tickScope);
  }

  /** The visible half of a press: the meter kicks, and the control flashes its ring. */
  function hit(v) {
    energy = Math.min(1, 0.55 + v.bodyGain * 6);
    runScope();
    var list = toggles();
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var el = list[i];
      if (!el.classList) continue;
      el.classList.remove('is-hit');
      /* Reading offsetWidth restarts a CSS animation that is already running; without it a second
         press inside the animation's own duration adds a class that is already there and nothing
         plays. */
      void el.offsetWidth;
      el.classList.add('is-hit');
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the dock's place */

  /*
   * A FLOATING CONTROL MUST NOT COVER A CONTROL, and this one did.
   *
   * MEASURED, on the built landing, at nine viewport sizes: at 740x360 and 667x375 — a phone held
   * sideways — the hero fills the screen, the corner the dock floats in lands ON the composer, and
   * 66x13 of the SEND BUTTON was underneath it. Both corners: moving it left is no fix, because the
   * composer spans the width. At 1440x900, 1280x620, 1280x480, 1024x700, 900x560, 800x560 and
   * 390x844 the corner is clear.
   *
   * A media query cannot express that boundary — 1280x480 is clear and 1024x540 is not, so it is
   * not a height rule or a width rule. The dock therefore MEASURES: if its own rectangle overlaps
   * any control, it stops floating and takes its place at the end of the page, where it cannot
   * steal a press. This is the same rule apps/web states as "decoration yields to the composer",
   * applied by the decoration rather than assumed by it.
   *
   * On load and on resize, never on scroll. The composer sits at the top of the page, so scrolling
   * carries it AWAY from a bottom corner; and a control that jumps around while the page scrolls is
   * worse than one that overlaps.
   */
  var CONTROLS = 'button, [role="button"], a[href], input, textarea, select, summary';

  function rectOf(el) {
    return el && el.getBoundingClientRect ? el.getBoundingClientRect() : null;
  }

  function placeDock() {
    var dock = document.querySelector('[data-sound-dock]');
    if (!dock || !dock.getBoundingClientRect || !dock.setAttribute) return;
    /* Measure the floating position, not the one it was last given. */
    if (dock.removeAttribute) dock.removeAttribute('data-flow');
    var d = rectOf(dock);
    if (!d || !d.width || !d.height) return;
    var list = document.querySelectorAll(CONTROLS);
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var el = list[i];
      if (el.closest && el.closest('[data-sound-dock]')) continue;
      var r = rectOf(el);
      if (!r || !r.width || !r.height) continue;
      if (r.left < d.right && r.right > d.left && r.top < d.bottom && r.bottom > d.top) {
        dock.setAttribute('data-flow', '');
        return;
      }
    }
  }

  var placing = 0;
  function schedulePlace() {
    if (placing) return;
    placing = window.requestAnimationFrame(function () { placing = 0; placeDock(); });
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the one listener */

  function voiceFor(el) {
    var explicit = el.getAttribute ? el.getAttribute('data-sound') : null;
    if (explicit === 'primary' || explicit === 'secondary' || explicit === 'toggle') return explicit;
    if (el.hasAttribute && (el.hasAttribute('aria-pressed') || el.hasAttribute('data-theme-toggle'))) {
      return 'toggle';
    }
    var name = el.className;
    if (name && typeof name !== 'string' && typeof name.baseVal === 'string') name = name.baseVal;
    var cls = ' ' + (typeof name === 'string' ? name : '') + ' ';
    if (/\bpill-quiet\b|\biconbtn\b|\bghost\b|\bquiet\b/.test(cls)) return 'secondary';
    if (/\bprimary\b|\bcta\b|\bpill\b/.test(cls)) return 'primary';
    if (el.getAttribute && el.getAttribute('type') === 'submit') return 'primary';
    return 'secondary';
  }

  /*
   * ONE LISTENER FOR BOTH JOBS, which is what makes "never more than once per press" structural
   * rather than a promise. The toggle is a button too: if arming were handled in one listener and
   * pressing in another, the press that arms the sound would make two sounds.
   */
  document.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
    var target = e.target;
    if (!target || !target.closest) return;

    var toggle = target.closest('[data-sound-toggle]');
    if (toggle) {
      armed = !armed;
      if (armed) {
        ensureAudio();
        if (audio && audio.resume) audio.resume();
      }
      remember(armed);
      paint();
      if (armed) press('toggle');
      runScope();
      return;
    }

    var control = target.closest(PRESSABLE);
    if (!control) return;
    if (control.getAttribute && control.getAttribute('data-sound') === 'none') return;
    if (control.hasAttribute && control.hasAttribute('disabled')) return;
    /* A choice carried over from a previous visit arms on this session's first press — still a
       gesture, still never at load. */
    if (armed && !audio) {
      ensureAudio();
      if (audio && audio.resume) audio.resume();
    }
    press(voiceFor(control));
  });

  document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', runScope);
  window.addEventListener('resize', schedulePlace);
  if (reduced) {
    if (reduced.addEventListener) reduced.addEventListener('change', runScope);
    else if (reduced.addListener) reduced.addListener(runScope);
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ boot */

  findScope();
  placeDock();
  paint();
  paintScope();
  runScope();

  /* The public surface. `appleTick` is the retired name and is kept aimed at the new synth, so
     anything that already called it gets a keyswitch instead of a chisel tick rather than an
     error. */
  window.appleSound = {
    press: press,
    isOn: function () { return armed; },
    voices: VOICES
  };
  window.appleTick = function () { return press('secondary'); };
})();

      // The landing's own theme wiring. It is inline and tiny rather than a module because this
      // route's whole point is that it ships essentially nothing; the alternative was leaving the
      // front page as the only route on the site with no way to change a preference every other
      // route offers.
      (function () {
        var root = document.documentElement;

        /** The address-bar colour is read from the stylesheet, never typed twice. */
        function paintBand() {
          var meta = document.getElementById('theme-color');
          if (!meta) return;
          var v = getComputedStyle(root).getPropertyValue('--theme-color').trim();
          if (v) meta.setAttribute('content', v);
        }

        function theme() {
          var set = root.getAttribute('data-theme');
          return set === 'light' ? 'light' : 'dark';
        }

        function paintToggles() {
          var t = theme();
          var list = document.querySelectorAll('[data-theme-toggle]');
          for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
            list[i].setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(t === 'dark'));
            list[i].setAttribute(
              'aria-label',
              t === 'dark' ? 'Switch to light theme' : 'Switch to dark theme'
            );
          }
        }

        document.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
          var btn = e.target && e.target.closest ? e.target.closest('[data-theme-toggle]') : null;
          if (!btn) return;
          var next = theme() === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark';
          root.setAttribute('data-theme', next);
          try {
            localStorage.setItem('apple-theme', next);
          } catch (err) {
            /* private mode — the choice still applies for this page view */
          }
          paintToggles();
          paintBand();
        });

        paintToggles();
        paintBand();
      })();
    </script> <script>
      /*
       * SCROLL REVEAL — the driver for the [data-reveal] rules in landing.css.
       *
       * Inline and at the end of <body> on purpose, matching the theme script above: this route's
       * whole point is that it ships essentially nothing, and a hoisted module for twenty lines
       * would be a bundle request to do less than this does. It also means the DOM above it is
       * already parsed, so there is no readiness dance and no `document.currentScript` — the
       * spelling that shipped a completely dead hero effect on this very page today, because
       * `currentScript` is null in every module script by specification.
       *
       * EVERY BRANCH ENDS WITH THE CONTENT VISIBLE. That is the only hard requirement here. A front
       * page that hides its own copy waiting for a class that never arrives is far worse than a
       * front page that does not animate, so the failure is made impossible four times over — see
       * the long note above the rules in landing.css. The failsafe below is the fourth: whatever
       * else happens, everything is revealed shortly after load.
       */
      (function () {
        var nodes = [].slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('[data-reveal]'));
        if (!nodes.length) return;

        function show(el) {
          var d = el.getAttribute('data-reveal-delay');
          if (d) el.style.setProperty('--reveal-delay', d + 'ms');
          el.classList.add('is-in');
        }
        function showAll() {
          for (var i = 0; i < nodes.length; i++) show(nodes[i]);
        }

        if (!('IntersectionObserver' in window)) { showAll(); return; }

        var io = new IntersectionObserver(function (entries) {
          for (var i = 0; i < entries.length; i++) {
            if (!entries[i].isIntersecting) continue;
            show(entries[i].target);
            io.unobserve(entries[i].target);
          }
        }, { rootMargin: '0px 0px -8% 0px', threshold: 0.08 });

        for (var i = 0; i < nodes.length; i++) io.observe(nodes[i]);

        /* The failsafe. An observer that never fires — a zero-height parent, a threshold a short
           section can never satisfy, a browser quirk — would leave copy invisible forever. After
           this beat, nothing is hidden regardless of what the observer did or did not do. */
        setTimeout(function () { io.disconnect(); showAll(); }, 2600);
      })();

id="main">  <section class="section clog is-ember" aria-labelledby="cl-title" data-astro-cid-bd6alw26> <div class="sheet-rails" aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-bd6alw26></div> <div class="wrap clog__wrap" data-astro-cid-bd6alw26> <p class="eyebrow" data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>Changelog</p> <h1 id="cl-title" class="carved" data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>Carved in order</h1> <p class="lede lede-wide" data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>
Every release, what it actually does, no adjectives doing heavy lifting.
</p> <ol class="releases" data-astro-cid-bd6alw26> <!-- ------------------------------------------------ v0.2 --> <li class="release slab slab--seam" data-reveal aria-labelledby="rel-0-2" data-astro-cid-bd6alw26> <header class="release__head" data-astro-cid-bd6alw26> <h2 id="rel-0-2" data-astro-cid-bd6alw26> <span class="release__tag mono" data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>v0.2</span> One model, measured
</h2> <p class="release__date mono" data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>2026-08-30</p> </header> <p class="release__lede" data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>
Every mode moved onto a single model, chosen by the eval suite
            rather than by taste — and the migration made Apple both better and
            cheaper at once.
</p> <h3 data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>The engine</h3> <ul data-astro-cid-bd6alw26> <li data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>
One engine now runs planning, building, memory and vision — 1M
              context, native tool calling, multimodal. Which engine that is, is
              an implementation detail Apple chooses per step; you never pick it
              and it can change without you noticing.
</li> <li data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>
Scored <strong data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>98.9</strong> on the Roblox eval suite against
<strong data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>96.8</strong> for the model it replaced.
</li> <li data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>
A full Agent build fell from <strong data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>$0.0139 to $0.0056</strong> —
              2.5× cheaper for the same work, on a model that scores higher.
</li> <li data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>
Multi-model routing was <em data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>removed</em>. It existed to move cheap
              steps onto a smaller model; measurement showed that routing the
              post-inspection step changed the outcome for the worse — the small
              model read the project tree and declared the task finished instead
              of building it.
</li> </ul> <h3 data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>Spend control</h3> <ul data-astro-cid-bd6alw26> <li data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>
The gateway now bills from the engine's own reported figure per call
              rather than from an estimate.
</li> <li data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>
Credits recalibrated: <strong data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>1 Credit = 30 neurons</strong>, so a
              Credit stays a meaningful unit now that the same work costs less.
</li> <li data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>
Four independent gates, each proven against production: a
              per-request ceiling, a daily ceiling, a monthly billable cap and an
              instant kill switch — all adjustable at runtime with no redeploy.
</li> <li data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>
Automatic retries removed entirely. A retry is a second bill for
              the same work.
</li> </ul> <h3 data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>Leaner context</h3> <ul data-astro-cid-bd6alw26> <li data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>Tool results capped at 3,000 characters, agent transcript at 24,000.</li> <li data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>
Tool definitions filtered per mode, so Plan does not pay to be told
              about playtesting tools.
</li> <li data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>Step budgets tightened to 3 / 8 / 14 for Plan / Agent / Super Agent.</li> </ul> </li> <!-- ------------------------------------------------ v0.1 --> <li class="release slab slab--seam" data-reveal data-reveal-delay="90" aria-labelledby="rel-0-1" data-astro-cid-bd6alw26> <header class="release__head" data-astro-cid-bd6alw26> <h2 id="rel-0-1" data-astro-cid-bd6alw26> <span class="release__tag mono" data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>v0.1</span> First public release
</h2> <p class="release__date mono" data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>2026</p> </header> <p class="release__lede" data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>
Apple opens its doors. The full describe-to-build loop: a web
            workspace, a real Studio plugin, and an agent that changes your
            actual place — carefully.
</p> <h3 data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>The workspace</h3> <ul data-astro-cid-bd6alw26> <li data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>
Chat-driven building with live streaming responses and a visible
              tool trace — you see every <code data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>get_project_tree</code>,
<code data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>edit_script</code> and <code data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>run_and_check</code> as it
              happens.
<span class="release__since" data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>

<code data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>run_and_check</code> and the other tools that would need it are not offered
                while it is the plugin you have paired. The trace shows what actually ran. See
<a href="/docs/plugin" data-astro-cid-bd6alw26>the plugin docs</a> for the current refusals.

</p> </div> </div> </footer>   <script>/* =====================================================================================
 * INTERFACE SOUND — ONE IMPLEMENTATION, SHARED BY EVERY LAYOUT.
 *
 * This file is the whole sound system. Base.astro and Landing.astro both inline THIS TEXT
 * through layouts/InterfaceSound.astro, so there is one synth, one listener and one stored
 * preference for the entire site. Before this there was a copy in Base.astro and nothing at all
 * on the front page, which is two states that cannot agree and one page with no control.
 *
 * WHAT THE OWNER ASKED FOR. He played with rosebud.ai and singled out one thing: pressing a button
 * makes a satisfying mechanical keyboard click. Measured on that page the same day (recorded in
 * packages/corpus/data/ui-references/web-landing.json, claim 16): its resource timing list contains
 * no mp3, wav, ogg, m4a or webm anywhere, while AudioContext is available — so their click is
 * SYNTHESISED at interaction time, not downloaded. That is the cheaper technique and the one used
 * here. A synthesised click costs no bytes, has no load state, and cannot be the reason a button
 * feels late.
 *
 * WHAT A KEYSWITCH ACTUALLY SOUNDS LIKE, and why the old `tick()` did not. The retired version was
 * one triangle oscillator sliding down — a soft chisel tick, a single event. A mechanical key press
 * is TWO events layered: the CLICK OF THE STEM, a bright noise transient of a few milliseconds with
 * no pitch of its own, and the THOCK OF THE BOTTOM-OUT, a low short body as the key meets the
 * plate. Both are below, layered with the body starting 4ms after the transient, and the whole
 * envelope is finished inside 58ms at its longest voice.
 *
 * THE INTERFACE HAS A VOICE RATHER THAN A BEEP. Three voices, chosen the way the reference's accent
 * family is chosen — one object, three jobs: a primary action is lower and fuller, a secondary
 * lighter and shorter, a toggle a touch brighter. Every press also carries a ±2.5% wobble, because
 * a sound repeated at exactly one frequency stops reading as a mechanism and starts reading as a
 * notification.
 *
 * THE PROPERTIES THIS FILE MUST KEEP, all of them checked by tests/interface-sound.test.mjs:
 *   - OFF by default. Nothing is armed by loading a page.
 *   - The AudioContext is constructed by a PRESS and never by load — the visitor's press on the
 *     toggle, or, when a previous visit already chose sound, that session's first press. Both are
 *     real user gestures, which is what browsers require; neither is page load.
 *   - Nothing autoplays.
 *   - The choice persists exactly the way the theme choice does, in localStorage under
 *     `apple-sound`, and is read back on the next page.
 *   - Every toggle states its state in aria-pressed and aria-label.
 *   - Never on hover, never on load, never more than once per press: ONE delegated listener owns
 *     both the toggle and the press, so a press on the toggle cannot produce two sounds.
 *
 * NO `document.currentScript`. Astro hoists a component <script> into a module script where
 * currentScript is null by specification; a hero effect shipped that way this morning and never ran
 * at all. Everything here is found with querySelector, and every one of those lookups tolerates a
 * null.
 * ===================================================================================== */
(function () {
  'use strict';

  var STORE_KEY = 'apple-sound';

  /* Everything that reads as a press. Buttons and links-as-buttons across both layouts: the
     landing's `.pill`, the chrome's `.iconbtn` and `.nav__cta`, anything with an explicit
     role, and `[data-sound-press]` for a control that is none of those. A bare prose link is
     deliberately absent — navigation is not a keystroke. */
  var PRESSABLE = [
    'button',
    '[role="button"]',
    'input[type="submit"]',
    'input[type="button"]',
    'summary',
    'a.pill',
    'a.btn',
    'a.cta',
    'a.button',
    'a.nav__cta',
    'a.nav__signin',
    'a[data-cta]',
    '[data-sound-press]'
  ].join(', ');

  /* THE THREE VOICES. clickHz is the band the stem transient sits in, bodyHz the pitch of the
     bottom-out. Gains are deliberately low: this is a texture under a finger, not an alert. */
  var VOICES = {
    primary:   { clickHz: 2400, clickQ: 0.9, clickGain: 0.034, clickDur: 0.010, bodyHz: 132, bodyGain: 0.075, bodyDur: 0.044 },
    secondary: { clickHz: 3200, clickQ: 1.1, clickGain: 0.026, clickDur: 0.008, bodyHz: 196, bodyGain: 0.048, bodyDur: 0.032 },
    toggle:    { clickHz: 4200, clickQ: 1.3, clickGain: 0.036, clickDur: 0.007, bodyHz: 240, bodyGain: 0.052, bodyDur: 0.030 }
  };

  var audio = null;       // constructed by a press, never by load
  var grain = null;       // the noise buffer, built once per context
  var armed = stored();   // the visitor's persisted choice; false on a first visit

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ preference */

  function stored() {
    try {
      return localStorage.getItem(STORE_KEY) === 'on';
    } catch (err) {
      return false; /* private mode — off, which is the default anyway */
    }
  }

  function remember(on) {
    try {
      localStorage.setItem(STORE_KEY, on ? 'on' : 'off');
    } catch (err) {
      /* private mode — the choice still applies for this page view */
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the synth */

  /** Construct the context. Called from the click handler and from nowhere else. */
  function ensureAudio() {
    if (audio) return audio;
    /* The prefixed name is Safari's, and it is still how an older iOS reaches this API. The cast
       is for the type checker only; there is no TypeScript in a file that ships as it is written. */
    var w = /** @type {any} */ (window);
    var Ctx = w.AudioContext || w.webkitAudioContext;
    if (!Ctx) return null;
    audio = new Ctx();
    return audio;
  }

  /** A short burst of decaying white noise, built once and re-triggered per press. */
  function noise(ac) {
    if (grain) return grain;
    var rate = ac.sampleRate || 44100;
    var len = Math.max(64, Math.floor(rate * 0.06));
    var buf = ac.createBuffer(1, len, rate);
    var data = buf.getChannelData(0);
    for (var i = 0; i < len; i++) {
      data[i] = (Math.random() * 2 - 1) * (1 - i / len);
    }
    grain = buf;
    return grain;
  }

  /**
   * ONE PRESS. Two layered events, under 60ms, at a low gain.
   * Silent unless armed, and silent unless a press has already built the context.
   */
  function press(kind) {
    if (!armed || !audio) return false;
    if (audio.state === 'suspended' && audio.resume) audio.resume();

    var v = VOICES[kind] || VOICES.secondary;
    var t = audio.currentTime;
    var wobble = 1 + (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.05;

    /* 1. THE CLICK OF THE STEM — filtered noise, no pitch, gone in a few milliseconds. */
    var src = audio.createBufferSource();
    src.buffer = noise(audio);
    var band = audio.createBiquadFilter();
    band.type = 'bandpass';
    band.frequency.setValueAtTime(v.clickHz * wobble, t);
    band.Q.value = v.clickQ;
    var clickGain = audio.createGain();
    clickGain.gain.setValueAtTime(v.clickGain, t);
    clickGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, t + v.clickDur);
    src.connect(band).connect(clickGain).connect(audio.destination);
    src.start(t);
    src.stop(t + v.clickDur + 0.004);

    /* 2. THE THOCK OF THE BOTTOM-OUT — a low body, pitched down as it dies. */
    var at = t + 0.004;
    var osc = audio.createOscillator();
    osc.type = 'triangle';
    osc.frequency.setValueAtTime(v.bodyHz * wobble, at);
    osc.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(v.bodyHz * 0.55, at + v.bodyDur);
    var bodyGain = audio.createGain();
    bodyGain.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, at);
    bodyGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(v.bodyGain, at + 0.003);
    bodyGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, at + v.bodyDur);
    osc.connect(bodyGain).connect(audio.destination);
    osc.start(at);
    osc.stop(at + v.bodyDur + 0.008);

    hit(v);
    return true;
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the toggles */

  function toggles() {
    return document.querySelectorAll('[data-sound-toggle]');
  }

  function paint() {
    var list = toggles();
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      list[i].setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(armed));
      list[i].setAttribute(
        'aria-label',
        armed ? 'Turn interface sound off' : 'Turn interface sound on'
      );
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the meter */

  /*
   * A CANVAS THAT SHOWS THE SOUND IT IS ABOUT TO MAKE. It is the toggle's own icon: a flat line
   * while sound is off, a live trace while it is on, and a kick on every press whose height is the
   * press's own body gain. It is entirely optional — a layout without one is silent about it and
   * every other line above still runs.
   *
   * IT IS THE ONLY AMBIENT MOTION THIS FILE OWNS, AND IT STOPS THREE WAYS: it never starts while
   * sound is off, it stops on prefers-reduced-motion, and it stops on visibilitychange. A
   * backgrounded tab must not burn a core for a line nobody is looking at.
   */
  var scope = null;
  var scopeCtx = null;
  var frame = 0;
  var energy = 0;
  var phase = 0;
  var reduced = window.matchMedia ? window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') : null;

  function findScope() {
    var el = document.querySelector('[data-sound-scope]');
    if (!el || !el.getContext) return;
    scope = el;
    scopeCtx = el.getContext('2d');
  }

  function stopped() {
    return !armed || document.hidden === true || !!(reduced && reduced.matches);
  }

  function paintScope() {
    if (!scope || !scopeCtx) return;
    var w = scope.width || 0;
    var h = scope.height || 0;
    if (!w || !h) return;
    var mid = h / 2;
    var ink = '';
    if (window.getComputedStyle) {
      ink = window.getComputedStyle(scope).getPropertyValue('color');
    }
    scopeCtx.clearRect(0, 0, w, h);
    scopeCtx.beginPath();
    for (var x = 0; x <= w; x += 2) {
      var k = x / w;
      var taper = Math.sin(Math.PI * k);
      var wave = Math.sin(k * 14 + phase) * 0.55 + Math.sin(k * 31 - phase * 1.7) * 0.45;
      var amp = (0.16 + energy * 0.84) * (mid - 1.5) * taper;
      var y = mid + wave * amp;
      if (x === 0) scopeCtx.moveTo(x, y);
      else scopeCtx.lineTo(x, y);
    }
    scopeCtx.strokeStyle = ink ? ink.trim() : 'currentColor';
    scopeCtx.lineWidth = 2;
    scopeCtx.stroke();
  }

  function tickScope() {
    if (stopped()) { frame = 0; paintScope(); return; }
    phase += 0.06;
    energy *= 0.9;
    if (energy < 0.004) energy = 0;
    paintScope();
    frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tickScope);
  }

  function runScope() {
    /* The CSS half of the same stop. Every ambient rule in InterfaceSound.astro is paused by this
       attribute, so prefers-reduced-motion, a hidden tab and "sound is off" all halt the keyframes
       as well as the canvas — one predicate, not two that can disagree. */
    var still = stopped();
    if (document.documentElement && document.documentElement.setAttribute) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-sound-still', still ? 'true' : 'false');
    }
    if (!scope) return;
    if (frame) { window.cancelAnimationFrame(frame); frame = 0; }
    if (still) { paintScope(); return; }
    frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tickScope);
  }

  /** The visible half of a press: the meter kicks, and the control flashes its ring. */
  function hit(v) {
    energy = Math.min(1, 0.55 + v.bodyGain * 6);
    runScope();
    var list = toggles();
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var el = list[i];
      if (!el.classList) continue;
      el.classList.remove('is-hit');
      /* Reading offsetWidth restarts a CSS animation that is already running; without it a second
         press inside the animation's own duration adds a class that is already there and nothing
         plays. */
      void el.offsetWidth;
      el.classList.add('is-hit');
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the dock's place */

  /*
   * A FLOATING CONTROL MUST NOT COVER A CONTROL, and this one did.
   *
   * MEASURED, on the built landing, at nine viewport sizes: at 740x360 and 667x375 — a phone held
   * sideways — the hero fills the screen, the corner the dock floats in lands ON the composer, and
   * 66x13 of the SEND BUTTON was underneath it. Both corners: moving it left is no fix, because the
   * composer spans the width. At 1440x900, 1280x620, 1280x480, 1024x700, 900x560, 800x560 and
   * 390x844 the corner is clear.
   *
   * A media query cannot express that boundary — 1280x480 is clear and 1024x540 is not, so it is
   * not a height rule or a width rule. The dock therefore MEASURES: if its own rectangle overlaps
   * any control, it stops floating and takes its place at the end of the page, where it cannot
   * steal a press. This is the same rule apps/web states as "decoration yields to the composer",
   * applied by the decoration rather than assumed by it.
   *
   * On load and on resize, never on scroll. The composer sits at the top of the page, so scrolling
   * carries it AWAY from a bottom corner; and a control that jumps around while the page scrolls is
   * worse than one that overlaps.
   */
  var CONTROLS = 'button, [role="button"], a[href], input, textarea, select, summary';

  function rectOf(el) {
    return el && el.getBoundingClientRect ? el.getBoundingClientRect() : null;
  }

  function placeDock() {
    var dock = document.querySelector('[data-sound-dock]');
    if (!dock || !dock.getBoundingClientRect || !dock.setAttribute) return;
    /* Measure the floating position, not the one it was last given. */
    if (dock.removeAttribute) dock.removeAttribute('data-flow');
    var d = rectOf(dock);
    if (!d || !d.width || !d.height) return;
    var list = document.querySelectorAll(CONTROLS);
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var el = list[i];
      if (el.closest && el.closest('[data-sound-dock]')) continue;
      var r = rectOf(el);
      if (!r || !r.width || !r.height) continue;
      if (r.left < d.right && r.right > d.left && r.top < d.bottom && r.bottom > d.top) {
        dock.setAttribute('data-flow', '');
        return;
      }
    }
  }

  var placing = 0;
  function schedulePlace() {
    if (placing) return;
    placing = window.requestAnimationFrame(function () { placing = 0; placeDock(); });
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the one listener */

  function voiceFor(el) {
    var explicit = el.getAttribute ? el.getAttribute('data-sound') : null;
    if (explicit === 'primary' || explicit === 'secondary' || explicit === 'toggle') return explicit;
    if (el.hasAttribute && (el.hasAttribute('aria-pressed') || el.hasAttribute('data-theme-toggle'))) {
      return 'toggle';
    }
    var name = el.className;
    if (name && typeof name !== 'string' && typeof name.baseVal === 'string') name = name.baseVal;
    var cls = ' ' + (typeof name === 'string' ? name : '') + ' ';
    if (/\bpill-quiet\b|\biconbtn\b|\bghost\b|\bquiet\b/.test(cls)) return 'secondary';
    if (/\bprimary\b|\bcta\b|\bpill\b/.test(cls)) return 'primary';
    if (el.getAttribute && el.getAttribute('type') === 'submit') return 'primary';
    return 'secondary';
  }

  /*
   * ONE LISTENER FOR BOTH JOBS, which is what makes "never more than once per press" structural
   * rather than a promise. The toggle is a button too: if arming were handled in one listener and
   * pressing in another, the press that arms the sound would make two sounds.
   */
  document.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
    var target = e.target;
    if (!target || !target.closest) return;

    var toggle = target.closest('[data-sound-toggle]');
    if (toggle) {
      armed = !armed;
      if (armed) {
        ensureAudio();
        if (audio && audio.resume) audio.resume();
      }
      remember(armed);
      paint();
      if (armed) press('toggle');
      runScope();
      return;
    }

    var control = target.closest(PRESSABLE);
    if (!control) return;
    if (control.getAttribute && control.getAttribute('data-sound') === 'none') return;
    if (control.hasAttribute && control.hasAttribute('disabled')) return;
    /* A choice carried over from a previous visit arms on this session's first press — still a
       gesture, still never at load. */
    if (armed && !audio) {
      ensureAudio();
      if (audio && audio.resume) audio.resume();
    }
    press(voiceFor(control));
  });

  document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', runScope);
  window.addEventListener('resize', schedulePlace);
  if (reduced) {
    if (reduced.addEventListener) reduced.addEventListener('change', runScope);
    else if (reduced.addListener) reduced.addListener(runScope);
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ boot */

  findScope();
  placeDock();
  paint();
  paintScope();
  runScope();

  /* The public surface. `appleTick` is the retired name and is kept aimed at the new synth, so
     anything that already called it gets a keyswitch instead of a chisel tick rather than an
     error. */
  window.appleSound = {
    press: press,
    isOn: function () { return armed; },
    voices: VOICES
  };
  window.appleTick = function () { return press('secondary'); };
})();
</script>  <div class="cursor" aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-msvfyisy> <div class="cursor-ring" data-astro-cid-msvfyisy><span class="cursor-label" data-astro-cid-msvfyisy></span></div> <div </p> </div> </div> </footer>   <script>/* =====================================================================================
 * INTERFACE SOUND — ONE IMPLEMENTATION, SHARED BY EVERY LAYOUT.
 *
 * This file is the whole sound system. Base.astro and Landing.astro both inline THIS TEXT
 * through layouts/InterfaceSound.astro, so there is one synth, one listener and one stored
 * preference for the entire site. Before this there was a copy in Base.astro and nothing at all
 * on the front page, which is two states that cannot agree and one page with no control.
 *
 * WHAT THE OWNER ASKED FOR. He played with rosebud.ai and singled out one thing: pressing a button
 * makes a satisfying mechanical keyboard click. Measured on that page the same day (recorded in
 * packages/corpus/data/ui-references/web-landing.json, claim 16): its resource timing list contains
 * no mp3, wav, ogg, m4a or webm anywhere, while AudioContext is available — so their click is
 * SYNTHESISED at interaction time, not downloaded. That is the cheaper technique and the one used
 * here. A synthesised click costs no bytes, has no load state, and cannot be the reason a button
 * feels late.
 *
 * WHAT A KEYSWITCH ACTUALLY SOUNDS LIKE, and why the old `tick()` did not. The retired version was
 * one triangle oscillator sliding down — a soft chisel tick, a single event. A mechanical key press
 * is TWO events layered: the CLICK OF THE STEM, a bright noise transient of a few milliseconds with
 * no pitch of its own, and the THOCK OF THE BOTTOM-OUT, a low short body as the key meets the
 * plate. Both are below, layered with the body starting 4ms after the transient, and the whole
 * envelope is finished inside 58ms at its longest voice.
 *
 * THE INTERFACE HAS A VOICE RATHER THAN A BEEP. Three voices, chosen the way the reference's accent
 * family is chosen — one object, three jobs: a primary action is lower and fuller, a secondary
 * lighter and shorter, a toggle a touch brighter. Every press also carries a ±2.5% wobble, because
 * a sound repeated at exactly one frequency stops reading as a mechanism and starts reading as a
 * notification.
 *
 * THE PROPERTIES THIS FILE MUST KEEP, all of them checked by tests/interface-sound.test.mjs:
 *   - OFF by default. Nothing is armed by loading a page.
 *   - The AudioContext is constructed by a PRESS and never by load — the visitor's press on the
 *     toggle, or, when a previous visit already chose sound, that session's first press. Both are
 *     real user gestures, which is what browsers require; neither is page load.
 *   - Nothing autoplays.
 *   - The choice persists exactly the way the theme choice does, in localStorage under
 *     `apple-sound`, and is read back on the next page.
 *   - Every toggle states its state in aria-pressed and aria-label.
 *   - Never on hover, never on load, never more than once per press: ONE delegated listener owns
 *     both the toggle and the press, so a press on the toggle cannot produce two sounds.
 *
 * NO `document.currentScript`. Astro hoists a component <script> into a module script where
 * currentScript is null by specification; a hero effect shipped that way this morning and never ran
 * at all. Everything here is found with querySelector, and every one of those lookups tolerates a
 * null.
 * ===================================================================================== */
(function () {
  'use strict';

  var STORE_KEY = 'apple-sound';

  /* Everything that reads as a press. Buttons and links-as-buttons across both layouts: the
     landing's `.pill`, the chrome's `.iconbtn` and `.nav__cta`, anything with an explicit
     role, and `[data-sound-press]` for a control that is none of those. A bare prose link is
     deliberately absent — navigation is not a keystroke. */
  var PRESSABLE = [
    'button',
    '[role="button"]',
    'input[type="submit"]',
    'input[type="button"]',
    'summary',
    'a.pill',
    'a.btn',
    'a.cta',
    'a.button',
    'a.nav__cta',
    'a.nav__signin',
    'a[data-cta]',
    '[data-sound-press]'
  ].join(', ');

  /* THE THREE VOICES. clickHz is the band the stem transient sits in, bodyHz the pitch of the
     bottom-out. Gains are deliberately low: this is a texture under a finger, not an alert. */
  var VOICES = {
    primary:   { clickHz: 2400, clickQ: 0.9, clickGain: 0.034, clickDur: 0.010, bodyHz: 132, bodyGain: 0.075, bodyDur: 0.044 },
    secondary: { clickHz: 3200, clickQ: 1.1, clickGain: 0.026, clickDur: 0.008, bodyHz: 196, bodyGain: 0.048, bodyDur: 0.032 },
    toggle:    { clickHz: 4200, clickQ: 1.3, clickGain: 0.036, clickDur: 0.007, bodyHz: 240, bodyGain: 0.052, bodyDur: 0.030 }
  };

  var audio = null;       // constructed by a press, never by load
  var grain = null;       // the noise buffer, built once per context
  var armed = stored();   // the visitor's persisted choice; false on a first visit

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ preference */

  function stored() {
    try {
      return localStorage.getItem(STORE_KEY) === 'on';
    } catch (err) {
      return false; /* private mode — off, which is the default anyway */
    }
  }

  function remember(on) {
    try {
      localStorage.setItem(STORE_KEY, on ? 'on' : 'off');
    } catch (err) {
      /* private mode — the choice still applies for this page view */
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the synth */

  /** Construct the context. Called from the click handler and from nowhere else. */
  function ensureAudio() {
    if (audio) return audio;
    /* The prefixed name is Safari's, and it is still how an older iOS reaches this API. The cast
       is for the type checker only; there is no TypeScript in a file that ships as it is written. */
    var w = /** @type {any} */ (window);
    var Ctx = w.AudioContext || w.webkitAudioContext;
    if (!Ctx) return null;
    audio = new Ctx();
    return audio;
  }

  /** A short burst of decaying white noise, built once and re-triggered per press. */
  function noise(ac) {
    if (grain) return grain;
    var rate = ac.sampleRate || 44100;
    var len = Math.max(64, Math.floor(rate * 0.06));
    var buf = ac.createBuffer(1, len, rate);
    var data = buf.getChannelData(0);
    for (var i = 0; i < len; i++) {
      data[i] = (Math.random() * 2 - 1) * (1 - i / len);
    }
    grain = buf;
    return grain;
  }

  /**
   * ONE PRESS. Two layered events, under 60ms, at a low gain.
   * Silent unless armed, and silent unless a press has already built the context.
   */
  function press(kind) {
    if (!armed || !audio) return false;
    if (audio.state === 'suspended' && audio.resume) audio.resume();

    var v = VOICES[kind] || VOICES.secondary;
    var t = audio.currentTime;
    var wobble = 1 + (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.05;

    /* 1. THE CLICK OF THE STEM — filtered noise, no pitch, gone in a few milliseconds. */
    var src = audio.createBufferSource();
    src.buffer = noise(audio);
    var band = audio.createBiquadFilter();
    band.type = 'bandpass';
    band.frequency.setValueAtTime(v.clickHz * wobble, t);
    band.Q.value = v.clickQ;
    var clickGain = audio.createGain();
    clickGain.gain.setValueAtTime(v.clickGain, t);
    clickGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, t + v.clickDur);
    src.connect(band).connect(clickGain).connect(audio.destination);
    src.start(t);
    src.stop(t + v.clickDur + 0.004);

    /* 2. THE THOCK OF THE BOTTOM-OUT — a low body, pitched down as it dies. */
    var at = t + 0.004;
    var osc = audio.createOscillator();
    osc.type = 'triangle';
    osc.frequency.setValueAtTime(v.bodyHz * wobble, at);
    osc.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(v.bodyHz * 0.55, at + v.bodyDur);
    var bodyGain = audio.createGain();
    bodyGain.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, at);
    bodyGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(v.bodyGain, at + 0.003);
    bodyGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, at + v.bodyDur);
    osc.connect(bodyGain).connect(audio.destination);
    osc.start(at);
    osc.stop(at + v.bodyDur + 0.008);

    hit(v);
    return true;
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the toggles */

  function toggles() {
    return document.querySelectorAll('[data-sound-toggle]');
  }

  function paint() {
    var list = toggles();
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      list[i].setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(armed));
      list[i].setAttribute(
        'aria-label',
        armed ? 'Turn interface sound off' : 'Turn interface sound on'
      );
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the meter */

  /*
   * A CANVAS THAT SHOWS THE SOUND IT IS ABOUT TO MAKE. It is the toggle's own icon: a flat line
   * while sound is off, a live trace while it is on, and a kick on every press whose height is the
   * press's own body gain. It is entirely optional — a layout without one is silent about it and
   * every other line above still runs.
   *
   * IT IS THE ONLY AMBIENT MOTION THIS FILE OWNS, AND IT STOPS THREE WAYS: it never starts while
   * sound is off, it stops on prefers-reduced-motion, and it stops on visibilitychange. A
   * backgrounded tab must not burn a core for a line nobody is looking at.
   */
  var scope = null;
  var scopeCtx = null;
  var frame = 0;
  var energy = 0;
  var phase = 0;
  var reduced = window.matchMedia ? window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') : null;

  function findScope() {
    var el = document.querySelector('[data-sound-scope]');
    if (!el || !el.getContext) return;
    scope = el;
    scopeCtx = el.getContext('2d');
  }

  function stopped() {
    return !armed || document.hidden === true || !!(reduced && reduced.matches);
  }

  function paintScope() {
    if (!scope || !scopeCtx) return;
    var w = scope.width || 0;
    var h = scope.height || 0;
    if (!w || !h) return;
    var mid = h / 2;
    var ink = '';
    if (window.getComputedStyle) {
      ink = window.getComputedStyle(scope).getPropertyValue('color');
    }
    scopeCtx.clearRect(0, 0, w, h);
    scopeCtx.beginPath();
    for (var x = 0; x <= w; x += 2) {
      var k = x / w;
      var taper = Math.sin(Math.PI * k);
      var wave = Math.sin(k * 14 + phase) * 0.55 + Math.sin(k * 31 - phase * 1.7) * 0.45;
      var amp = (0.16 + energy * 0.84) * (mid - 1.5) * taper;
      var y = mid + wave * amp;
      if (x === 0) scopeCtx.moveTo(x, y);
      else scopeCtx.lineTo(x, y);
    }
    scopeCtx.strokeStyle = ink ? ink.trim() : 'currentColor';
    scopeCtx.lineWidth = 2;
    scopeCtx.stroke();
  }

  function tickScope() {
    if (stopped()) { frame = 0; paintScope(); return; }
    phase += 0.06;
    energy *= 0.9;
    if (energy < 0.004) energy = 0;
    paintScope();
    frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tickScope);
  }

  function runScope() {
    /* The CSS half of the same stop. Every ambient rule in InterfaceSound.astro is paused by this
       attribute, so prefers-reduced-motion, a hidden tab and "sound is off" all halt the keyframes
       as well as the canvas — one predicate, not two that can disagree. */
    var still = stopped();
    if (document.documentElement && document.documentElement.setAttribute) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-sound-still', still ? 'true' : 'false');
    }
    if (!scope) return;
    if (frame) { window.cancelAnimationFrame(frame); frame = 0; }
    if (still) { paintScope(); return; }
    frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tickScope);
  }

  /** The visible half of a press: the meter kicks, and the control flashes its ring. */
  function hit(v) {
    energy = Math.min(1, 0.55 + v.bodyGain * 6);
    runScope();
    var list = toggles();
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var el = list[i];
      if (!el.classList) continue;
      el.classList.remove('is-hit');
      /* Reading offsetWidth restarts a CSS animation that is already running; without it a second
         press inside the animation's own duration adds a class that is already there and nothing
         plays. */
      void el.offsetWidth;
      el.classList.add('is-hit');
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the dock's place */

  /*
   * A FLOATING CONTROL MUST NOT COVER A CONTROL, and this one did.
   *
   * MEASURED, on the built landing, at nine viewport sizes: at 740x360 and 667x375 — a phone held
   * sideways — the hero fills the screen, the corner the dock floats in lands ON the composer, and
   * 66x13 of the SEND BUTTON was underneath it. Both corners: moving it left is no fix, because the
   * composer spans the width. At 1440x900, 1280x620, 1280x480, 1024x700, 900x560, 800x560 and
   * 390x844 the corner is clear.
   *
   * A media query cannot express that boundary — 1280x480 is clear and 1024x540 is not, so it is
   * not a height rule or a width rule. The dock therefore MEASURES: if its own rectangle overlaps
   * any control, it stops floating and takes its place at the end of the page, where it cannot
   * steal a press. This is the same rule apps/web states as "decoration yields to the composer",
   * applied by the decoration rather than assumed by it.
   *
   * On load and on resize, never on scroll. The composer sits at the top of the page, so scrolling
   * carries it AWAY from a bottom corner; and a control that jumps around while the page scrolls is
   * worse than one that overlaps.
   */
  var CONTROLS = 'button, [role="button"], a[href], input, textarea, select, summary';

  function rectOf(el) {
    return el && el.getBoundingClientRect ? el.getBoundingClientRect() : null;
  }

  function placeDock() {
    var dock = document.querySelector('[data-sound-dock]');
    if (!dock || !dock.getBoundingClientRect || !dock.setAttribute) return;
    /* Measure the floating position, not the one it was last given. */
    if (dock.removeAttribute) dock.removeAttribute('data-flow');
    var d = rectOf(dock);
    if (!d || !d.width || !d.height) return;
    var list = document.querySelectorAll(CONTROLS);
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var el = list[i];
      if (el.closest && el.closest('[data-sound-dock]')) continue;
      var r = rectOf(el);
      if (!r || !r.width || !r.height) continue;
      if (r.left < d.right && r.right > d.left && r.top < d.bottom && r.bottom > d.top) {
        dock.setAttribute('data-flow', '');
        return;
      }
    }
  }

  var placing = 0;
  function schedulePlace() {
    if (placing) return;
    placing = window.requestAnimationFrame(function () { placing = 0; placeDock(); });
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the one listener */

  function voiceFor(el) {
    var explicit = el.getAttribute ? el.getAttribute('data-sound') : null;
    if (explicit === 'primary' || explicit === 'secondary' || explicit === 'toggle') return explicit;
    if (el.hasAttribute && (el.hasAttribute('aria-pressed') || el.hasAttribute('data-theme-toggle'))) {
      return 'toggle';
    }
    var name = el.className;
    if (name && typeof name !== 'string' && typeof name.baseVal === 'string') name = name.baseVal;
    var cls = ' ' + (typeof name === 'string' ? name : '') + ' ';
    if (/\bpill-quiet\b|\biconbtn\b|\bghost\b|\bquiet\b/.test(cls)) return 'secondary';
    if (/\bprimary\b|\bcta\b|\bpill\b/.test(cls)) return 'primary';
    if (el.getAttribute && el.getAttribute('type') === 'submit') return 'primary';
    return 'secondary';
  }

  /*
   * ONE LISTENER FOR BOTH JOBS, which is what makes "never more than once per press" structural
   * rather than a promise. The toggle is a button too: if arming were handled in one listener and
   * pressing in another, the press that arms the sound would make two sounds.
   */
  document.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
    var target = e.target;
    if (!target || !target.closest) return;

    var toggle = target.closest('[data-sound-toggle]');
    if (toggle) {
      armed = !armed;
      if (armed) {
        ensureAudio();
        if (audio && audio.resume) audio.resume();
      }
      remember(armed);
      paint();
      if (armed) press('toggle');
      runScope();
      return;
    }

    var control = target.closest(PRESSABLE);
    if (!control) return;
    if (control.getAttribute && control.getAttribute('data-sound') === 'none') return;
    if (control.hasAttribute && control.hasAttribute('disabled')) return;
    /* A choice carried over from a previous visit arms on this session's first press — still a
       gesture, still never at load. */
    if (armed && !audio) {
      ensureAudio();
      if (audio && audio.resume) audio.resume();
    }
    press(voiceFor(control));
  });

  document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', runScope);
  window.addEventListener('resize', schedulePlace);
  if (reduced) {
    if (reduced.addEventListener) reduced.addEventListener('change', runScope);
    else if (reduced.addListener) reduced.addListener(runScope);
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ boot */

  findScope();
  placeDock();
  paint();
  paintScope();
  runScope();

id="main">  <div class="wrap docs" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <aside class="docs__side" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <details class="docs__nav" id="docs-nav-details" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <summary data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> Getting started </a> </li><li data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <a href="/docs/plugin" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> Install the plugin </a> </li><li data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <a data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>Docs</p> <h1 class="carved" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>Billing &amp; payments</h1> <div class="prose" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <div class="callout"> <p> <strong>There is no way to become a paying customer yet.</strong> Paid checkout is not open
        in this preview — <a href="/pricing">Pricing</a> marks every paid tier "planned" and
<a href="/terms">Terms</a> says the same. Everything below describes how billing works for a
        paid account and applies to nobody today; it is published so that the rules are readable
        before anyone is subject to them, not because a subscription can be started. Apple is free
        to use, with the daily allowance on <a href="/docs/credits-and-limits">Credits &amp;
        limits</a>.
</p> </div><p>
Everything to do with money — cards, invoices, cancelling — lives in the billing portal, which
    is Stripe's, not ours. You reach it from <strong>Usage</strong> in the app
    (<a href="/app/usage">/app/usage</a>), from the button that reads
<em>Manage billing, invoices and cancellation</em>. It appears once you are on a paid plan.
</p> <h2 id="failed-payment">A payment failed or the card was declined</h2> <p> <strong>Your plan keeps working.</strong> A failed renewal is usually an expired card, and we do
    not cut off a paying customer at the first retry. Stripe retries over the following days, and
    for as long as it is retrying you keep the allowance you are paying for.
</p> <p>
Update the card in the billing portal — that is the whole fix, and it applies immediately. If
    Stripe gives up before you do, the subscription ends and the account drops to Free: your
    projects, checkpoints and conversations are untouched, and the daily allowance becomes the free
    one. Nothing is deleted for&nbsp;non-payment.
</p> <h2 id="invoices">Where invoices and receipts are</h2> <p>
In the billing portal, under your payment history — every invoice, with a PDF, including ones
    from a subscription that has since ended. We do not hold a second copy of your billing history;
    the portal is the record.
</p> <p>
If you need a company name, address or VAT number on them, set it in the portal before the next
    invoice is issued. Stripe puts on an invoice what it knows at the moment it issues it.
</p> <h2 id="cancelling">Cancelling</h2> <p>
Cancel in the billing portal. <strong>You keep the plan until the end of the period you have
    already paid for</strong> — cancelling on day 3 of a month does not take the allowance away on
    day 3. After that date the account is on Free, with everything still in it.
</p> <p>
Extra Credits, if an account has any, are separate from a subscription and do not expire with
    one. They stay on the account, and they are spent only after the day's included allowance is
    gone. <strong>There is no way to buy them today</strong> — no plan has a credit checkout, and
<a href="/pricing">Pricing</a> says the same in its comparison table.
</p> <h2 id="not-applied">I paid, and the plan still shows the old one</h2> <p>
Give it a few seconds and press <em>Check again</em> on the Usage page. Plans are applied from
    Stripe's own webhook rather than from the page you land on after paying — deliberately, because
    a person who pays and closes the tab has still bought the thing, and a person who reaches the
    success page by typing the URL has not. The webhook usually arrives before you get back.
</p> <p>
If it is still wrong after a minute, that is worth reporting rather than paying again. Nothing
    you do on this page can double-charge you — but a second checkout could, so do not start one.
</p> <h2 id="upgrading">Changing plan while already on a paid one</h2> <p>
Moving between paid tiers happens in the portal, not through a new checkout, in both directions.
    A second checkout would <em>add</em> a subscription rather than replace the running one, and you
    would be billed for both. The app already routes you to the portal for this; it is only worth
    knowing if you were about to go looking for a purchase button.
</p> <h2 id="charges">What is charged, and what is not</h2> <ul> <li> <strong>Nothing is charged before checkout completes.</strong> Starting one and closing it
      costs nothing, and the app says so where it happens.
</li> <li> <strong>Running out of Credits is not a charge.</strong> A request refused for lack of
      allowance is refused before it costs anything — see
<a href="/docs/credits-and-limits">Credits &amp; limits</a>.
</li> <li> <strong>A step that failed is not charged.</strong> Credits come from the compute a call
      actually reports, so a call that returned nothing reports nothing —
<a href="/docs/troubleshooting#model-failures">Troubleshooting</a> covers what each failure
      means.
</li> </ul> <div class="callout"> <p>
A billing question a page cannot answer is worth an email:
<a href="mailto:apple.labs.app@gmail.com">apple.labs.app@gmail.com</a>. Include the email address on the
      account and roughly when the payment was — never a card number, which we neither need nor
      want, and which nobody at Apple can see.
</p> </div>  </div> <footer class="docs__foot" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <p data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>
Stuck? Ask in the app, check your Credits before sending, or email
<a href="mailto:apple.labs.app@gmail.com" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>apple.labs.app@gmail.com</a>.
</p> </footer> </article> </div>  </main> <footer class="foot" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <div class="wrap" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <div class="foot__grid" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <div class="foot__brand" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <a href="/" class="brand" aria-label="Apple — home" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <svg width="26" height="26" viewBox="0 0 32 32" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true" class="gm " data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m> <path d="M5 24 12 5 19 14 27 8 21 27 13 18Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".1" data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m></path> <path d="m5 24 7-19 7 9 8-6-6 19-8-9-8 6Z" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linejoin="round" data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m></path> <path d="m12 5 1 13 6-4 2 13" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.2" data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m></path> </svg>  <span class="brand__word" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Apple</span> </a> <p class="foot__tag" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>It works inside the place you already have open.</p>  <p class="mono" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Apple Labs</p> </div> <nav aria-label="Product" class="foot__col" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <h2 data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Product</h2> <ul data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>  <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/docs/getting-started" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>How it works</a></li>  <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/proof" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Proof</a></li> <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/docs/modes" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Modes</a></li> <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/changelog" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Changelog</a></li> <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/pricing" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Pricing</a></li>  <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/status" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Status &amp;
