 * INTERFACE SOUND — ONE IMPLEMENTATION, SHARED BY EVERY LAYOUT.
 *
 * This file is the whole sound system. Base.astro and Landing.astro both inline THIS TEXT
 * through layouts/InterfaceSound.astro, so there is one synth, one listener and one stored
 * preference for the entire site. Before this there was a copy in Base.astro and nothing at all
 * on the front page, which is two states that cannot agree and one page with no control.
 *
 * WHAT THE OWNER ASKED FOR. He played with rosebud.ai and singled out one thing: pressing a button
 * makes a satisfying mechanical keyboard click. Measured on that page the same day (recorded in
 * packages/corpus/data/ui-references/web-landing.json, claim 16): its resource timing list contains
 * no mp3, wav, ogg, m4a or webm anywhere, while AudioContext is available — so their click is
 * SYNTHESISED at interaction time, not downloaded. That is the cheaper technique and the one used
 * here. A synthesised click costs no bytes, has no load state, and cannot be the reason a button
 * feels late.
 *
 * WHAT A KEYSWITCH ACTUALLY SOUNDS LIKE, and why the old `tick()` did not. The retired version was
 * one triangle oscillator sliding down — a soft chisel tick, a single event. A mechanical key press
 * is TWO events layered: the CLICK OF THE STEM, a bright noise transient of a few milliseconds with
 * no pitch of its own, and the THOCK OF THE BOTTOM-OUT, a low short body as the key meets the
 * plate. Both are below, layered with the body starting 4ms after the transient, and the whole
 * envelope is finished inside 58ms at its longest voice.
 *
 * THE INTERFACE HAS A VOICE RATHER THAN A BEEP. Three voices, chosen the way the reference's accent
 * family is chosen — one object, three jobs: a primary action is lower and fuller, a secondary
 * lighter and shorter, a toggle a touch brighter. Every press also carries a ±2.5% wobble, because
 * a sound repeated at exactly one frequency stops reading as a mechanism and starts reading as a
 * notification.
 *
 * THE PROPERTIES THIS FILE MUST KEEP, all of them checked by tests/interface-sound.test.mjs:
 *   - OFF by default. Nothing is armed by loading a page.
 *   - The AudioContext is constructed by a PRESS and never by load — the visitor's press on the
 *     toggle, or, when a previous visit already chose sound, that session's first press. Both are
 *     real user gestures, which is what browsers require; neither is page load.
 *   - Nothing autoplays.
 *   - The choice persists exactly the way the theme choice does, in localStorage under
 *     `apple-sound`, and is read back on the next page.
 *   - Every toggle states its state in aria-pressed and aria-label.
 *   - Never on hover, never on load, never more than once per press: ONE delegated listener owns
 *     both the toggle and the press, so a press on the toggle cannot produce two sounds.
 *
 * NO `document.currentScript`. Astro hoists a component <script> into a module script where
 * currentScript is null by specification; a hero effect shipped that way this morning and never ran
 * at all. Everything here is found with querySelector, and every one of those lookups tolerates a
 * null.
 * ===================================================================================== */
(function () {
  'use strict';

  var STORE_KEY = 'apple-sound';

  /* Everything that reads as a press. Buttons and links-as-buttons across both layouts: the
     landing's `.pill`, the chrome's `.iconbtn` and `.nav__cta`, anything with an explicit
     role, and `[data-sound-press]` for a control that is none of those. A bare prose link is
     deliberately absent — navigation is not a keystroke. */
  var PRESSABLE = [
    'button',
    '[role="button"]',
    'input[type="submit"]',
    'input[type="button"]',
    'summary',
    'a.pill',
    'a.btn',
    'a.cta',
    'a.button',
    'a.nav__cta',
    'a.nav__signin',
    'a[data-cta]',
    '[data-sound-press]'
  ].join(', ');

  /* THE THREE VOICES. clickHz is the band the stem transient sits in, bodyHz the pitch of the
     bottom-out. Gains are deliberately low: this is a texture under a finger, not an alert. */
  var VOICES = {
    primary:   { clickHz: 2400, clickQ: 0.9, clickGain: 0.034, clickDur: 0.010, bodyHz: 132, bodyGain: 0.075, bodyDur: 0.044 },
    secondary: { clickHz: 3200, clickQ: 1.1, clickGain: 0.026, clickDur: 0.008, bodyHz: 196, bodyGain: 0.048, bodyDur: 0.032 },
    toggle:    { clickHz: 4200, clickQ: 1.3, clickGain: 0.036, clickDur: 0.007, bodyHz: 240, bodyGain: 0.052, bodyDur: 0.030 }
  };

  var audio = null;       // constructed by a press, never by load
  var grain = null;       // the noise buffer, built once per context
  var armed = stored();   // the visitor's persisted choice; false on a first visit

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ preference */

  function stored() {
    try {
      return localStorage.getItem(STORE_KEY) === 'on';
    } catch (err) {
      return false; /* private mode — off, which is the default anyway */
    }
  }

  function remember(on) {
    try {
      localStorage.setItem(STORE_KEY, on ? 'on' : 'off');
    } catch (err) {
      /* private mode — the choice still applies for this page view */
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the synth */

  /** Construct the context. Called from the click handler and from nowhere else. */
  function ensureAudio() {
    if (audio) return audio;
    /* The prefixed name is Safari's, and it is still how an older iOS reaches this API. The cast
       is for the type checker only; there is no TypeScript in a file that ships as it is written. */
    var w = /** @type {any} */ (window);
    var Ctx = w.AudioContext || w.webkitAudioContext;
    if (!Ctx) return null;
    audio = new Ctx();
    return audio;
  }

  /** A short burst of decaying white noise, built once and re-triggered per press. */
  function noise(ac) {
    if (grain) return grain;
    var rate = ac.sampleRate || 44100;
    var len = Math.max(64, Math.floor(rate * 0.06));
    var buf = ac.createBuffer(1, len, rate);
    var data = buf.getChannelData(0);
    for (var i = 0; i < len; i++) {
      data[i] = (Math.random() * 2 - 1) * (1 - i / len);
    }
    grain = buf;
    return grain;
  }

  /**
   * ONE PRESS. Two layered events, under 60ms, at a low gain.
   * Silent unless armed, and silent unless a press has already built the context.
   */
  function press(kind) {
    if (!armed || !audio) return false;
    if (audio.state === 'suspended' && audio.resume) audio.resume();

    var v = VOICES[kind] || VOICES.secondary;
    var t = audio.currentTime;
    var wobble = 1 + (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.05;

    /* 1. THE CLICK OF THE STEM — filtered noise, no pitch, gone in a few milliseconds. */
    var src = audio.createBufferSource();
    src.buffer = noise(audio);
    var band = audio.createBiquadFilter();
    band.type = 'bandpass';
    band.frequency.setValueAtTime(v.clickHz * wobble, t);
    band.Q.value = v.clickQ;
    var clickGain = audio.createGain();
    clickGain.gain.setValueAtTime(v.clickGain, t);
    clickGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, t + v.clickDur);
    src.connect(band).connect(clickGain).connect(audio.destination);
    src.start(t);
    src.stop(t + v.clickDur + 0.004);

    /* 2. THE THOCK OF THE BOTTOM-OUT — a low body, pitched down as it dies. */
    var at = t + 0.004;
    var osc = audio.createOscillator();
    osc.type = 'triangle';
    osc.frequency.setValueAtTime(v.bodyHz * wobble, at);
    osc.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(v.bodyHz * 0.55, at + v.bodyDur);
    var bodyGain = audio.createGain();
    bodyGain.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, at);
    bodyGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(v.bodyGain, at + 0.003);
    bodyGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, at + v.bodyDur);
    osc.connect(bodyGain).connect(audio.destination);
    osc.start(at);
    osc.stop(at + v.bodyDur + 0.008);

    hit(v);
    return true;
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the toggles */

  function toggles() {
    return document.querySelectorAll('[data-sound-toggle]');
  }

  function paint() {
    var list = toggles();
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      list[i].setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(armed));
      list[i].setAttribute(
        'aria-label',
        armed ? 'Turn interface sound off' : 'Turn interface sound on'
      );
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the meter */

  /*
   * A CANVAS THAT SHOWS THE SOUND IT IS ABOUT TO MAKE. It is the toggle's own icon: a flat line
   * while sound is off, a live trace while it is on, and a kick on every press whose height is the
   * press's own body gain. It is entirely optional — a layout without one is silent about it and
   * every other line above still runs.
   *
   * IT IS THE ONLY AMBIENT MOTION THIS FILE OWNS, AND IT STOPS THREE WAYS: it never starts while
   * sound is off, it stops on prefers-reduced-motion, and it stops on visibilitychange. A
   * backgrounded tab must not burn a core for a line nobody is looking at.
   */
  var scope = null;
  var scopeCtx = null;
  var frame = 0;
  var energy = 0;
  var phase = 0;
  var reduced = window.matchMedia ? window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') : null;

  function findScope() {
    var el = document.querySelector('[data-sound-scope]');
    if (!el || !el.getContext) return;
    scope = el;
    scopeCtx = el.getContext('2d');
  }

  function stopped() {
    return !armed || document.hidden === true || !!(reduced && reduced.matches);
  }

  function paintScope() {
    if (!scope || !scopeCtx) return;
    var w = scope.width || 0;
    var h = scope.height || 0;
    if (!w || !h) return;
    var mid = h / 2;
    var ink = '';
    if (window.getComputedStyle) {
      ink = window.getComputedStyle(scope).getPropertyValue('color');
    }
    scopeCtx.clearRect(0, 0, w, h);
    scopeCtx.beginPath();
    for (var x = 0; x <= w; x += 2) {
      var k = x / w;
      var taper = Math.sin(Math.PI * k);
      var wave = Math.sin(k * 14 + phase) * 0.55 + Math.sin(k * 31 - phase * 1.7) * 0.45;
      var amp = (0.16 + energy * 0.84) * (mid - 1.5) * taper;
      var y = mid + wave * amp;
      if (x === 0) scopeCtx.moveTo(x, y);
      else scopeCtx.lineTo(x, y);
    }
    scopeCtx.strokeStyle = ink ? ink.trim() : 'currentColor';
    scopeCtx.lineWidth = 2;
    scopeCtx.stroke();
  }

  function tickScope() {
    if (stopped()) { frame = 0; paintScope(); return; }
    phase += 0.06;
    energy *= 0.9;
    if (energy < 0.004) energy = 0;
    paintScope();
    frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tickScope);
  }

  function runScope() {
    /* The CSS half of the same stop. Every ambient rule in InterfaceSound.astro is paused by this
       attribute, so prefers-reduced-motion, a hidden tab and "sound is off" all halt the keyframes
       as well as the canvas — one predicate, not two that can disagree. */
    var still = stopped();
    if (document.documentElement && document.documentElement.setAttribute) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-sound-still', still ? 'true' : 'false');
    }
    if (!scope) return;
    if (frame) { window.cancelAnimationFrame(frame); frame = 0; }
    if (still) { paintScope(); return; }
    frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tickScope);
  }

  /** The visible half of a press: the meter kicks, and the control flashes its ring. */
  function hit(v) {
    energy = Math.min(1, 0.55 + v.bodyGain * 6);
    runScope();
    var list = toggles();
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var el = list[i];
      if (!el.classList) continue;
      el.classList.remove('is-hit');
      /* Reading offsetWidth restarts a CSS animation that is already running; without it a second
         press inside the animation's own duration adds a class that is already there and nothing
         plays. */
      void el.offsetWidth;
      el.classList.add('is-hit');
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the dock's place */

  /*
   * A FLOATING CONTROL MUST NOT COVER A CONTROL, and this one did.
   *
   * MEASURED, on the built landing, at nine viewport sizes: at 740x360 and 667x375 — a phone held
   * sideways — the hero fills the screen, the corner the dock floats in lands ON the composer, and
   * 66x13 of the SEND BUTTON was underneath it. Both corners: moving it left is no fix, because the
   * composer spans the width. At 1440x900, 1280x620, 1280x480, 1024x700, 900x560, 800x560 and
   * 390x844 the corner is clear.
   *
   * A media query cannot express that boundary — 1280x480 is clear and 1024x540 is not, so it is
   * not a height rule or a width rule. The dock therefore MEASURES: if its own rectangle overlaps
   * any control, it stops floating and takes its place at the end of the page, where it cannot
   * steal a press. This is the same rule apps/web states as "decoration yields to the composer",
   * applied by the decoration rather than assumed by it.
   *
   * On load and on resize, never on scroll. The composer sits at the top of the page, so scrolling
   * carries it AWAY from a bottom corner; and a control that jumps around while the page scrolls is
   * worse than one that overlaps.
   */
  var CONTROLS = 'button, [role="button"], a[href], input, textarea, select, summary';

  function rectOf(el) {
    return el && el.getBoundingClientRect ? el.getBoundingClientRect() : null;
  }

  function placeDock() {
    var dock = document.querySelector('[data-sound-dock]');
    if (!dock || !dock.getBoundingClientRect || !dock.setAttribute) return;
    /* Measure the floating position, not the one it was last given. */
    if (dock.removeAttribute) dock.removeAttribute('data-flow');
    var d = rectOf(dock);
    if (!d || !d.width || !d.height) return;
    var list = document.querySelectorAll(CONTROLS);
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var el = list[i];
      if (el.closest && el.closest('[data-sound-dock]')) continue;
      var r = rectOf(el);
      if (!r || !r.width || !r.height) continue;
      if (r.left < d.right && r.right > d.left && r.top < d.bottom && r.bottom > d.top) {
        dock.setAttribute('data-flow', '');
        return;
      }
    }
  }

  var placing = 0;
  function schedulePlace() {
    if (placing) return;
    placing = window.requestAnimationFrame(function () { placing = 0; placeDock(); });
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the one listener */

  function voiceFor(el) {
    var explicit = el.getAttribute ? el.getAttribute('data-sound') : null;
    if (explicit === 'primary' || explicit === 'secondary' || explicit === 'toggle') return explicit;
    if (el.hasAttribute && (el.hasAttribute('aria-pressed') || el.hasAttribute('data-theme-toggle'))) {
      return 'toggle';
    }
    var name = el.className;
    if (name && typeof name !== 'string' && typeof name.baseVal === 'string') name = name.baseVal;
    var cls = ' ' + (typeof name === 'string' ? name : '') + ' ';
    if (/\bpill-quiet\b|\biconbtn\b|\bghost\b|\bquiet\b/.test(cls)) return 'secondary';
    if (/\bprimary\b|\bcta\b|\bpill\b/.test(cls)) return 'primary';
    if (el.getAttribute && el.getAttribute('type') === 'submit') return 'primary';
    return 'secondary';
  }

  /*
   * ONE LISTENER FOR BOTH JOBS, which is what makes "never more than once per press" structural
   * rather than a promise. The toggle is a button too: if arming were handled in one listener and
   * pressing in another, the press that arms the sound would make two sounds.
   */
  document.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
    var target = e.target;
    if (!target || !target.closest) return;

    var toggle = target.closest('[data-sound-toggle]');
    if (toggle) {
      armed = !armed;
      if (armed) {
        ensureAudio();
        if (audio && audio.resume) audio.resume();
      }
      remember(armed);
      paint();
      if (armed) press('toggle');
      runScope();
      return;
    }

    var control = target.closest(PRESSABLE);
    if (!control) return;
    if (control.getAttribute && control.getAttribute('data-sound') === 'none') return;
    if (control.hasAttribute && control.hasAttribute('disabled')) return;
    /* A choice carried over from a previous visit arms on this session's first press — still a
       gesture, still never at load. */
    if (armed && !audio) {
      ensureAudio();
      if (audio && audio.resume) audio.resume();
    }
    press(voiceFor(control));
  });

  document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', runScope);
  window.addEventListener('resize', schedulePlace);
  if (reduced) {
    if (reduced.addEventListener) reduced.addEventListener('change', runScope);
    else if (reduced.addListener) reduced.addListener(runScope);
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ boot */

  findScope();
  placeDock();
  paint();
  paintScope();
  runScope();

  /* The public surface. `appleTick` is the retired name and is kept aimed at the new synth, so
     anything that already called it gets a keyswitch instead of a chisel tick rather than an
     error. */
  window.appleSound = {
    press: press,
    isOn: function () { return armed; },
    voices: VOICES
  };
  window.appleTick = function () { return press('secondary'); };
})();

class="eyebrow" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>Docs</p> <h1 class="carved" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>Build the plugin from source</h1> <div class="prose" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <div class="callout callout--violet"> <p> <strong>This is not how you install Apple.</strong> It is the development and debugging path,
      for people changing the plugin's code. If you want to <em>use</em> Apple, go to
<a href="/docs/plugin">Install Apple for Studio</a> — the Creator Store is the only supported
      install path, and a hand-built plugin is unsupported, unsigned and updated by nobody but you.
</p> <p> <strong>Build <code>apps/apple-plugin</code> and nothing else.</strong> There is a second
      Studio plugin in the repository, <code>apps/plugin</code>. It is the legacy source the removed
      Creator Store asset was built from, it executes Luau it receives over the wire, and it must not
      be loaded into a Studio you care about. Its own README says so in its first line.
</p> </div> <h2>Build it</h2> <p>
The plugin this product ships lives in <code>apps/apple-plugin</code>. Build it with the
    repository's own script, which needs Node, <code>python3</code>,
<a href="https://luau.org/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">luau-analyze</a> and
<a href="https://rojo.space" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Rojo</a> — version
<strong>7.7.0</strong>, the version this repository pins.
</p> <pre><code>node apps/apple-plugin/scripts/build.mjs</code></pre> <p>
It parses every source, refuses a <code>require</code> of a module that is not bundled, runs
    Rojo, and then reads the <em>built</em> artifact back — scanning it for credentials and
    developer paths, and checking that the capabilities the source claims are actually in the bytes.
    That last step exists because the legacy build once shipped with a version string and a feature
    set its own source disagreed with, and every test passed because every test read the
<code>.luau</code>. The result is
<code>apps/apple-plugin/release/apple-studio.rbxm</code>.
</p> <h2>Load it as a local plugin</h2> <p>Drop the <code>.rbxm</code> into Studio's local plugins folder and restart Studio:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Windows:</strong> <code>%LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\Plugins</code></li> <li><strong>macOS:</strong> <code>~/Documents/Roblox/Plugins</code></li> </ul> <p>
Studio's <strong>Plugins</strong> tab has a <strong>Plugins Folder</strong> button that opens
    the same directory, which is the reliable way to find it if the path above does not exist yet.
    Remove a local build by deleting the file and restarting Studio.
</p> <div class="callout"> <p> <strong>Do not run both at once.</strong> A local build and a Creator Store install are two
      separate plugins as far as Studio is concerned. Running both gives you two Apple buttons, two
      panels and two pollers fighting over the same place. Disable or remove one.
</p> </div> <h2>Iterating on the code</h2> <p>
For live editing, Roblox's own workflow beats rebuilding: enable
<strong>Plugin Debugging Enabled</strong> in Studio's settings, use
<strong>Save as Local Plugin</strong> from the <strong>Plugins</strong> menu, and work from the
    copy inside <code>PluginDebugService</code>. Right-click it for
<strong>Save and Reload Plugin</strong> to apply changes without restarting Studio.
</p> <p>
One behavioural difference worth knowing while debugging: our plugin source notes that a
    locally-installed plugin does not go through Studio's per-plugin HTTP permission prompt, while
    a Creator Store install does. That is an observation about our own builds, not a documented
    Roblox guarantee — so test the permission path against a real store install before trusting it,
    and never assume users get the frictionless version you do.
</p> <h2>Publishing an update</h2> <p>
Releases are cut by hand, from Studio: <strong>Plugins</strong> menu →
<strong>Publish as Plugin</strong> → <strong>Overwrite an existing asset</strong>, selecting the
    existing Apple asset so the id stays stable. There is no automated path: Roblox's Open Cloud
    asset API does not support the Plugin asset type at all, and its update endpoint can only
    replace content for models. Budget a human in Studio for every version.
</p> <p>
Users do not receive that update automatically — see <a href="/docs/updating">Updating</a>.
    Assume a long tail of installs running old builds, permanently, and keep the server tolerant of
    them.
</p>  </div> <footer class="docs__foot" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <p data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>

</p> </footer> </article> </div>  </main> <footer class="foot" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <div class="wrap" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <div class="foot__grid" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <div class="foot__brand" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <a href="/" class="brand" aria-label="Apple — home" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <svg width="26" height="26" viewBox="0 0 32 32" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true" class="gm " data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m> <path d="M5 24 12 5 19 14 27 8 21 27 13 18Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".1" data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m></path> <path d="m5 24 7-19 7 9 8-6-6 19-8-9-8 6Z" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linejoin="round" data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m></path> <path d="m12 5 1 13 6-4 2 13" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.2" data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m></path> </svg>  <span class="brand__word" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Apple</span> </a> <p class="foot__tag" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>It works inside the place you already have open.</p>  <p class="mono" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Apple Labs</p> </div> <nav aria-label="Product" class="foot__col" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <h2 data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Product</h2> <ul data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>  <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/docs/getting-started" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>How it works</a></li>  <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/proof" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Proof</a></li> <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/docs/modes" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Modes</a></li> <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/changelog" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Changelog</a></li> <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/pricing" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Pricing</a></li>  <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/status" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Status &amp;  * INTERFACE SOUND — ONE IMPLEMENTATION, SHARED BY EVERY LAYOUT.
 *
 * This file is the whole sound system. Base.astro and Landing.astro both inline THIS TEXT
 * through layouts/InterfaceSound.astro, so there is one synth, one listener and one stored
 * preference for the entire site. Before this there was a copy in Base.astro and nothing at all
 * on the front page, which is two states that cannot agree and one page with no control.
 *
 * WHAT THE OWNER ASKED FOR. He played with rosebud.ai and singled out one thing: pressing a button
 * makes a satisfying mechanical keyboard click. Measured on that page the same day (recorded in
 * packages/corpus/data/ui-references/web-landing.json, claim 16): its resource timing list contains
 * no mp3, wav, ogg, m4a or webm anywhere, while AudioContext is available — so their click is
 * SYNTHESISED at interaction time, not downloaded. That is the cheaper technique and the one used
 * here. A synthesised click costs no bytes, has no load state, and cannot be the reason a button
 * feels late.
 *
 * WHAT A KEYSWITCH ACTUALLY SOUNDS LIKE, and why the old `tick()` did not. The retired version was
 * one triangle oscillator sliding down — a soft chisel tick, a single event. A mechanical key press
 * is TWO events layered: the CLICK OF THE STEM, a bright noise transient of a few milliseconds with
 * no pitch of its own, and the THOCK OF THE BOTTOM-OUT, a low short body as the key meets the
 * plate. Both are below, layered with the body starting 4ms after the transient, and the whole
 * envelope is finished inside 58ms at its longest voice.
 *
 * THE INTERFACE HAS A VOICE RATHER THAN A BEEP. Three voices, chosen the way the reference's accent
 * family is chosen — one object, three jobs: a primary action is lower and fuller, a secondary
 * lighter and shorter, a toggle a touch brighter. Every press also carries a ±2.5% wobble, because
 * a sound repeated at exactly one frequency stops reading as a mechanism and starts reading as a
 * notification.
 *
 * THE PROPERTIES THIS FILE MUST KEEP, all of them checked by tests/interface-sound.test.mjs:
 *   - OFF by default. Nothing is armed by loading a page.
 *   - The AudioContext is constructed by a PRESS and never by load — the visitor's press on the
 *     toggle, or, when a previous visit already chose sound, that session's first press. Both are
 *     real user gestures, which is what browsers require; neither is page load.
 *   - Nothing autoplays.
 *   - The choice persists exactly the way the theme choice does, in localStorage under
 *     `apple-sound`, and is read back on the next page.
 *   - Every toggle states its state in aria-pressed and aria-label.
 *   - Never on hover, never on load, never more than once per press: ONE delegated listener owns
 *     both the toggle and the press, so a press on the toggle cannot produce two sounds.
 *
 * NO `document.currentScript`. Astro hoists a component <script> into a module script where
 * currentScript is null by specification; a hero effect shipped that way this morning and never ran
 * at all. Everything here is found with querySelector, and every one of those lookups tolerates a
 * null.
 * ===================================================================================== */
(function () {
  'use strict';

  var STORE_KEY = 'apple-sound';

  /* Everything that reads as a press. Buttons and links-as-buttons across both layouts: the
     landing's `.pill`, the chrome's `.iconbtn` and `.nav__cta`, anything with an explicit
     role, and `[data-sound-press]` for a control that is none of those. A bare prose link is
     deliberately absent — navigation is not a keystroke. */
  var PRESSABLE = [
    'button',
    '[role="button"]',
    'input[type="submit"]',
    'input[type="button"]',
    'summary',
    'a.pill',
    'a.btn',
    'a.cta',
    'a.button',
    'a.nav__cta',
    'a.nav__signin',
    'a[data-cta]',
    '[data-sound-press]'
  ].join(', ');

  /* THE THREE VOICES. clickHz is the band the stem transient sits in, bodyHz the pitch of the
     bottom-out. Gains are deliberately low: this is a texture under a finger, not an alert. */
  var VOICES = {
    primary:   { clickHz: 2400, clickQ: 0.9, clickGain: 0.034, clickDur: 0.010, bodyHz: 132, bodyGain: 0.075, bodyDur: 0.044 },
    secondary: { clickHz: 3200, clickQ: 1.1, clickGain: 0.026, clickDur: 0.008, bodyHz: 196, bodyGain: 0.048, bodyDur: 0.032 },
    toggle:    { clickHz: 4200, clickQ: 1.3, clickGain: 0.036, clickDur: 0.007, bodyHz: 240, bodyGain: 0.052, bodyDur: 0.030 }
  };

  var audio = null;       // constructed by a press, never by load
  var grain = null;       // the noise buffer, built once per context
  var armed = stored();   // the visitor's persisted choice; false on a first visit

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ preference */

  function stored() {
    try {
      return localStorage.getItem(STORE_KEY) === 'on';
    } catch (err) {
      return false; /* private mode — off, which is the default anyway */
    }
  }

  function remember(on) {
    try {
      localStorage.setItem(STORE_KEY, on ? 'on' : 'off');
    } catch (err) {
      /* private mode — the choice still applies for this page view */
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the synth */

  /** Construct the context. Called from the click handler and from nowhere else. */
  function ensureAudio() {
    if (audio) return audio;
    /* The prefixed name is Safari's, and it is still how an older iOS reaches this API. The cast
       is for the type checker only; there is no TypeScript in a file that ships as it is written. */
    var w = /** @type {any} */ (window);
    var Ctx = w.AudioContext || w.webkitAudioContext;
    if (!Ctx) return null;
    audio = new Ctx();
    return audio;
  }

  /** A short burst of decaying white noise, built once and re-triggered per press. */
  function noise(ac) {
    if (grain) return grain;
    var rate = ac.sampleRate || 44100;
    var len = Math.max(64, Math.floor(rate * 0.06));
    var buf = ac.createBuffer(1, len, rate);
    var data = buf.getChannelData(0);
    for (var i = 0; i < len; i++) {
      data[i] = (Math.random() * 2 - 1) * (1 - i / len);
    }
    grain = buf;
    return grain;
  }

  /**
   * ONE PRESS. Two layered events, under 60ms, at a low gain.
   * Silent unless armed, and silent unless a press has already built the context.
   */
  function press(kind) {
    if (!armed || !audio) return false;
    if (audio.state === 'suspended' && audio.resume) audio.resume();

    var v = VOICES[kind] || VOICES.secondary;
    var t = audio.currentTime;
    var wobble = 1 + (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.05;

    /* 1. THE CLICK OF THE STEM — filtered noise, no pitch, gone in a few milliseconds. */
    var src = audio.createBufferSource();
    src.buffer = noise(audio);
    var band = audio.createBiquadFilter();
    band.type = 'bandpass';
    band.frequency.setValueAtTime(v.clickHz * wobble, t);
    band.Q.value = v.clickQ;
    var clickGain = audio.createGain();
    clickGain.gain.setValueAtTime(v.clickGain, t);
    clickGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, t + v.clickDur);
    src.connect(band).connect(clickGain).connect(audio.destination);
    src.start(t);
    src.stop(t + v.clickDur + 0.004);

    /* 2. THE THOCK OF THE BOTTOM-OUT — a low body, pitched down as it dies. */
    var at = t + 0.004;
    var osc = audio.createOscillator();
    osc.type = 'triangle';
    osc.frequency.setValueAtTime(v.bodyHz * wobble, at);
    osc.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(v.bodyHz * 0.55, at + v.bodyDur);
    var bodyGain = audio.createGain();
    bodyGain.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, at);
    bodyGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(v.bodyGain, at + 0.003);
    bodyGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, at + v.bodyDur);
    osc.connect(bodyGain).connect(audio.destination);
    osc.start(at);
    osc.stop(at + v.bodyDur + 0.008);

    hit(v);
    return true;
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the toggles */

  function toggles() {
    return document.querySelectorAll('[data-sound-toggle]');
  }

  function paint() {
    var list = toggles();
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      list[i].setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(armed));
      list[i].setAttribute(
        'aria-label',
        armed ? 'Turn interface sound off' : 'Turn interface sound on'
      );
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the meter */

  /*
   * A CANVAS THAT SHOWS THE SOUND IT IS ABOUT TO MAKE. It is the toggle's own icon: a flat line
   * while sound is off, a live trace while it is on, and a kick on every press whose height is the
   * press's own body gain. It is entirely optional — a layout without one is silent about it and
   * every other line above still runs.
   *
   * IT IS THE ONLY AMBIENT MOTION THIS FILE OWNS, AND IT STOPS THREE WAYS: it never starts while
   * sound is off, it stops on prefers-reduced-motion, and it stops on visibilitychange. A
   * backgrounded tab must not burn a core for a line nobody is looking at.
   */
  var scope = null;
  var scopeCtx = null;
  var frame = 0;
  var energy = 0;
  var phase = 0;
  var reduced = window.matchMedia ? window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') : null;

  function findScope() {
    var el = document.querySelector('[data-sound-scope]');
    if (!el || !el.getContext) return;
    scope = el;
    scopeCtx = el.getContext('2d');
  }

  function stopped() {
    return !armed || document.hidden === true || !!(reduced && reduced.matches);
  }

  function paintScope() {
    if (!scope || !scopeCtx) return;
    var w = scope.width || 0;
    var h = scope.height || 0;
    if (!w || !h) return;
    var mid = h / 2;
    var ink = '';
    if (window.getComputedStyle) {
      ink = window.getComputedStyle(scope).getPropertyValue('color');
    }
    scopeCtx.clearRect(0, 0, w, h);
    scopeCtx.beginPath();
    for (var x = 0; x <= w; x += 2) {
      var k = x / w;
      var taper = Math.sin(Math.PI * k);
      var wave = Math.sin(k * 14 + phase) * 0.55 + Math.sin(k * 31 - phase * 1.7) * 0.45;
      var amp = (0.16 + energy * 0.84) * (mid - 1.5) * taper;
      var y = mid + wave * amp;
      if (x === 0) scopeCtx.moveTo(x, y);
      else scopeCtx.lineTo(x, y);
    }
    scopeCtx.strokeStyle = ink ? ink.trim() : 'currentColor';
    scopeCtx.lineWidth = 2;
    scopeCtx.stroke();
  }

  function tickScope() {
    if (stopped()) { frame = 0; paintScope(); return; }
    phase += 0.06;
    energy *= 0.9;
    if (energy < 0.004) energy = 0;
    paintScope();
    frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tickScope);
  }

  function runScope() {
    /* The CSS half of the same stop. Every ambient rule in InterfaceSound.astro is paused by this
       attribute, so prefers-reduced-motion, a hidden tab and "sound is off" all halt the keyframes
       as well as the canvas — one predicate, not two that can disagree. */
    var still = stopped();
    if (document.documentElement && document.documentElement.setAttribute) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-sound-still', still ? 'true' : 'false');
    }
    if (!scope) return;
    if (frame) { window.cancelAnimationFrame(frame); frame = 0; }
    if (still) { paintScope(); return; }
    frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tickScope);
  }

  /** The visible half of a press: the meter kicks, and the control flashes its ring. */
  function hit(v) {
    energy = Math.min(1, 0.55 + v.bodyGain * 6);
    runScope();
    var list = toggles();
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var el = list[i];
      if (!el.classList) continue;
      el.classList.remove('is-hit');
      /* Reading offsetWidth restarts a CSS animation that is already running; without it a second
         press inside the animation's own duration adds a class that is already there and nothing
         plays. */
      void el.offsetWidth;
      el.classList.add('is-hit');
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the dock's place */

  /*
   * A FLOATING CONTROL MUST NOT COVER A CONTROL, and this one did.
   *
   * MEASURED, on the built landing, at nine viewport sizes: at 740x360 and 667x375 — a phone held
   * sideways — the hero fills the screen, the corner the dock floats in lands ON the composer, and
   * 66x13 of the SEND BUTTON was underneath it. Both corners: moving it left is no fix, because the
   * composer spans the width. At 1440x900, 1280x620, 1280x480, 1024x700, 900x560, 800x560 and
   * 390x844 the corner is clear.
   *
   * A media query cannot express that boundary — 1280x480 is clear and 1024x540 is not, so it is
   * not a height rule or a width rule. The dock therefore MEASURES: if its own rectangle overlaps
   * any control, it stops floating and takes its place at the end of the page, where it cannot
   * steal a press. This is the same rule apps/web states as "decoration yields to the composer",
   * applied by the decoration rather than assumed by it.
   *
   * On load and on resize, never on scroll. The composer sits at the top of the page, so scrolling
   * carries it AWAY from a bottom corner; and a control that jumps around while the page scrolls is
   * worse than one that overlaps.
   */
  var CONTROLS = 'button, [role="button"], a[href], input, textarea, select, summary';

  function rectOf(el) {
    return el && el.getBoundingClientRect ? el.getBoundingClientRect() : null;
  }

  function placeDock() {
    var dock = document.querySelector('[data-sound-dock]');
    if (!dock || !dock.getBoundingClientRect || !dock.setAttribute) return;
    /* Measure the floating position, not the one it was last given. */
    if (dock.removeAttribute) dock.removeAttribute('data-flow');
    var d = rectOf(dock);
    if (!d || !d.width || !d.height) return;
    var list = document.querySelectorAll(CONTROLS);
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var el = list[i];
      if (el.closest && el.closest('[data-sound-dock]')) continue;
      var r = rectOf(el);
      if (!r || !r.width || !r.height) continue;
      if (r.left < d.right && r.right > d.left && r.top < d.bottom && r.bottom > d.top) {
        dock.setAttribute('data-flow', '');
        return;
      }
    }
  }

  var placing = 0;
  function schedulePlace() {
    if (placing) return;
    placing = window.requestAnimationFrame(function () { placing = 0; placeDock(); });
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the one listener */

  function voiceFor(el) {
    var explicit = el.getAttribute ? el.getAttribute('data-sound') : null;
    if (explicit === 'primary' || explicit === 'secondary' || explicit === 'toggle') return explicit;
    if (el.hasAttribute && (el.hasAttribute('aria-pressed') || el.hasAttribute('data-theme-toggle'))) {
      return 'toggle';
    }
    var name = el.className;
    if (name && typeof name !== 'string' && typeof name.baseVal === 'string') name = name.baseVal;
    var cls = ' ' + (typeof name === 'string' ? name : '') + ' ';
    if (/\bpill-quiet\b|\biconbtn\b|\bghost\b|\bquiet\b/.test(cls)) return 'secondary';
    if (/\bprimary\b|\bcta\b|\bpill\b/.test(cls)) return 'primary';
    if (el.getAttribute && el.getAttribute('type') === 'submit') return 'primary';
    return 'secondary';
  }

  /*
   * ONE LISTENER FOR BOTH JOBS, which is what makes "never more than once per press" structural
   * rather than a promise. The toggle is a button too: if arming were handled in one listener and
   * pressing in another, the press that arms the sound would make two sounds.
   */
  document.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
    var target = e.target;
    if (!target || !target.closest) return;

    var toggle = target.closest('[data-sound-toggle]');
    if (toggle) {
      armed = !armed;
      if (armed) {
        ensureAudio();
        if (audio && audio.resume) audio.resume();
      }
      remember(armed);
      paint();
      if (armed) press('toggle');
      runScope();
      return;
    }

    var control = target.closest(PRESSABLE);
    if (!control) return;
    if (control.getAttribute && control.getAttribute('data-sound') === 'none') return;
    if (control.hasAttribute && control.hasAttribute('disabled')) return;
    /* A choice carried over from a previous visit arms on this session's first press — still a
       gesture, still never at load. */
    if (armed && !audio) {
      ensureAudio();
      if (audio && audio.resume) audio.resume();
    }
    press(voiceFor(control));
  });

  document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', runScope);
  window.addEventListener('resize', schedulePlace);
  if (reduced) {
    if (reduced.addEventListener) reduced.addEventListener('change', runScope);
    else if (reduced.addListener) reduced.addListener(runScope);
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ boot */

  findScope();
  placeDock();
  paint();
  paintScope();
  runScope();

  /* The public surface. `appleTick` is the retired name and is kept aimed at the new synth, so
     anything that already called it gets a keyswitch instead of a chisel tick rather than an
     error. */
  window.appleSound = {
    press: press,
    isOn: function () { return armed; },
    voices: VOICES
  };
  window.appleTick = function () { return press('secondary'); };
})();

class="docs__main" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <p class="eyebrow" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>Docs</p> <h1 class="carved" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>Connect a project</h1> <div class="prose" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <div class="callout"> <p><strong>Public plugin installation is currently unavailable.</strong> These steps are for people who already have a working Apple plugin. New customers can use chat, but cannot build inside Studio yet. See <a href="/docs/plugin">plugin availability</a>; there is no confirmed release date.</p> </div><p>
Connecting links the Apple panel in <em>this</em> Studio window to <em>one</em> Apple project.
    Until you do it, the plugin is inert: the panel reads <strong>Not connected</strong> and Apple
    cannot see or change anything.
</p> <p>
The link uses a short-lived pairing code instead of your password. Treat the code as a
    temporary credential: enter it only in your own Apple plugin and do not share it.
</p> <h2>Connecting</h2> <ol> <li>Open the place you want Apple to work on in Roblox Studio.</li> <li>
In Studio's <strong>Plugins</strong> tab, click <strong>Apple</strong>. The panel docks and
      shows <strong>Not connected</strong>.
</li> <li>
In the Apple web workspace, open the project. Until Studio is linked, the conversation ends
      with a <strong>Connect Roblox Studio</strong> block — press <strong>Enter pairing code</strong>
on its last step. (The <strong>Connect</strong> button in the project's <strong>Studio</strong>
panel opens the same thing.) You get a six-character code — something like <code>K7M3QP</code>
— with a countdown.
</li> <li>
Type that code into the plugin panel and press <strong>Connect</strong>.
</li> </ol> <p>
The panel turns green and reads <strong>Connected</strong> followed by the project name; the
    button becomes <strong>Disconnect</strong>. The web workspace stops saying it is waiting for
    Studio and shows the place you have open. Apple can now act on this place when this project's
    chat asks it to.
</p> <h2>About the code</h2> <ul> <li><strong>It expires after 10 minutes</strong> and works once. Expired or already used, it is dead — generate a new one.</li> <li>
It is six characters drawn from an alphabet with no confusable letters — no O, I, L or 1 —
      so there is nothing to squint at.
</li> <li>
Case does not matter and punctuation is ignored, so <code>k7m3qp</code> and
<code>K7M-3QP</code> both work.
</li> <li>You can have up to five unused codes alive at once, across all your projects.</li> </ul> <h2>What the connection covers</h2> <ul> <li> <strong>One Studio window, one project.</strong> Opening a different place, or a second
      Studio window, does not carry the connection with it — connect that window too.
</li> <li> <strong>It survives restarts.</strong> The plugin remembers the session, so reopening Studio
      reconnects without a new code.
</li> <li> <strong>It expires after 30 days.</strong> When it does, the panel says
<em>Session ended — reconnect with a new code</em>. Generate a fresh code and connect again.
</li> </ul> <h2>Disconnecting</h2> <p>
Press <strong>Disconnect</strong> in the plugin panel, or disconnect from the web workspace.
    Either one stops Apple acting on the place immediately, whether or not the plugin stays
    installed. Nothing Apple already built is undone — use Studio's undo or a checkpoint for that.
</p> <div class="callout"> <p> <strong>Team Create:</strong> the connection belongs to your Studio window, and Apple's edits
      reach your teammates the same way your own edits do. Teammates who want their own Apple chat
      should connect their own Studio window to their own project.
</p> </div> <p>
Something not lining up? <a href="/docs/troubleshooting">Troubleshooting</a> lists the exact
    messages the panel can show and what each one means.
</p>  </div> <footer class="docs__foot" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <p data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>
Stuck? Ask in the app, check your Credits before sending, or email
<a href="mailto:apple.labs.app@gmail.com" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>apple.labs.app@gmail.com</a>.
</p> </footer> </article> </div>  </main> <footer class="foot" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <div class="wrap" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <div class="foot__grid" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <div class="foot__brand" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <a href="/" class="brand" aria-label="Apple — home" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <svg width="26" height="26" viewBox="0 0 32 32" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true" class="gm " data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m> <path d="M5 24 12 5 19 14 27 8 21 27 13 18Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".1" data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m></path> <path d="m5 24 7-19 7 9 8-6-6 19-8-9-8 6Z" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linejoin="round" data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m></path> <path d="m12 5 1 13 6-4 2 13" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.2" data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m></path> </svg>  <span class="brand__word" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Apple</span> </a> <p class="foot__tag" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>It works inside the place you already have open.</p>  <p class="mono" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Apple Labs</p> </div> <nav aria-label="Product" class="foot__col" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <h2 data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Product</h2> <ul data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>  <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/docs/getting-started" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>How it works</a></li>  <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/proof" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Proof</a></li> <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/docs/modes" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Modes</a></li> <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/changelog" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Changelog</a></li> <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/pricing" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Pricing</a></li>  <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/status" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Status &amp;  * INTERFACE SOUND — ONE IMPLEMENTATION, SHARED BY EVERY LAYOUT.
 *
 * This file is the whole sound system. Base.astro and Landing.astro both inline THIS TEXT
 * through layouts/InterfaceSound.astro, so there is one synth, one listener and one stored
 * preference for the entire site. Before this there was a copy in Base.astro and nothing at all
 * on the front page, which is two states that cannot agree and one page with no control.
 *
 * WHAT THE OWNER ASKED FOR. He played with rosebud.ai and singled out one thing: pressing a button
 * makes a satisfying mechanical keyboard click. Measured on that page the same day (recorded in
 * packages/corpus/data/ui-references/web-landing.json, claim 16): its resource timing list contains
 * no mp3, wav, ogg, m4a or webm anywhere, while AudioContext is available — so their click is
 * SYNTHESISED at interaction time, not downloaded. That is the cheaper technique and the one used
 * here. A synthesised click costs no bytes, has no load state, and cannot be the reason a button
 * feels late.
 *
 * WHAT A KEYSWITCH ACTUALLY SOUNDS LIKE, and why the old `tick()` did not. The retired version was
 * one triangle oscillator sliding down — a soft chisel tick, a single event. A mechanical key press
 * is TWO events layered: the CLICK OF THE STEM, a bright noise transient of a few milliseconds with
 * no pitch of its own, and the THOCK OF THE BOTTOM-OUT, a low short body as the key meets the
 * plate. Both are below, layered with the body starting 4ms after the transient, and the whole
 * envelope is finished inside 58ms at its longest voice.
 *
 * THE INTERFACE HAS A VOICE RATHER THAN A BEEP. Three voices, chosen the way the reference's accent
 * family is chosen — one object, three jobs: a primary action is lower and fuller, a secondary
 * lighter and shorter, a toggle a touch brighter. Every press also carries a ±2.5% wobble, because
 * a sound repeated at exactly one frequency stops reading as a mechanism and starts reading as a
 * notification.
 *
 * THE PROPERTIES THIS FILE MUST KEEP, all of them checked by tests/interface-sound.test.mjs:
 *   - OFF by default. Nothing is armed by loading a page.
 *   - The AudioContext is constructed by a PRESS and never by load — the visitor's press on the
 *     toggle, or, when a previous visit already chose sound, that session's first press. Both are
 *     real user gestures, which is what browsers require; neither is page load.
 *   - Nothing autoplays.
 *   - The choice persists exactly the way the theme choice does, in localStorage under
 *     `apple-sound`, and is read back on the next page.
 *   - Every toggle states its state in aria-pressed and aria-label.
 *   - Never on hover, never on load, never more than once per press: ONE delegated listener owns
 *     both the toggle and the press, so a press on the toggle cannot produce two sounds.
 *
 * NO `document.currentScript`. Astro hoists a component <script> into a module script where
 * currentScript is null by specification; a hero effect shipped that way this morning and never ran
 * at all. Everything here is found with querySelector, and every one of those lookups tolerates a
 * null.
 * ===================================================================================== */
(function () {
  'use strict';

  var STORE_KEY = 'apple-sound';

  /* Everything that reads as a press. Buttons and links-as-buttons across both layouts: the
     landing's `.pill`, the chrome's `.iconbtn` and `.nav__cta`, anything with an explicit
     role, and `[data-sound-press]` for a control that is none of those. A bare prose link is
     deliberately absent — navigation is not a keystroke. */
  var PRESSABLE = [
    'button',
    '[role="button"]',
    'input[type="submit"]',
    'input[type="button"]',
    'summary',
    'a.pill',
    'a.btn',
    'a.cta',
    'a.button',
    'a.nav__cta',
    'a.nav__signin',
    'a[data-cta]',
    '[data-sound-press]'
  ].join(', ');

  /* THE THREE VOICES. clickHz is the band the stem transient sits in, bodyHz the pitch of the
     bottom-out. Gains are deliberately low: this is a texture under a finger, not an alert. */
  var VOICES = {
    primary:   { clickHz: 2400, clickQ: 0.9, clickGain: 0.034, clickDur: 0.010, bodyHz: 132, bodyGain: 0.075, bodyDur: 0.044 },
    secondary: { clickHz: 3200, clickQ: 1.1, clickGain: 0.026, clickDur: 0.008, bodyHz: 196, bodyGain: 0.048, bodyDur: 0.032 },
    toggle:    { clickHz: 4200, clickQ: 1.3, clickGain: 0.036, clickDur: 0.007, bodyHz: 240, bodyGain: 0.052, bodyDur: 0.030 }
  };

  var audio = null;       // constructed by a press, never by load
  var grain = null;       // the noise buffer, built once per context
  var armed = stored();   // the visitor's persisted choice; false on a first visit

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ preference */

  function stored() {
    try {
      return localStorage.getItem(STORE_KEY) === 'on';
    } catch (err) {
      return false; /* private mode — off, which is the default anyway */
    }
  }

  function remember(on) {
    try {
      localStorage.setItem(STORE_KEY, on ? 'on' : 'off');
    } catch (err) {
      /* private mode — the choice still applies for this page view */
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the synth */

  /** Construct the context. Called from the click handler and from nowhere else. */
  function ensureAudio() {
    if (audio) return audio;
    /* The prefixed name is Safari's, and it is still how an older iOS reaches this API. The cast
       is for the type checker only; there is no TypeScript in a file that ships as it is written. */
    var w = /** @type {any} */ (window);
    var Ctx = w.AudioContext || w.webkitAudioContext;
    if (!Ctx) return null;
    audio = new Ctx();
    return audio;
  }

  /** A short burst of decaying white noise, built once and re-triggered per press. */
  function noise(ac) {
    if (grain) return grain;
    var rate = ac.sampleRate || 44100;
    var len = Math.max(64, Math.floor(rate * 0.06));
    var buf = ac.createBuffer(1, len, rate);
    var data = buf.getChannelData(0);
    for (var i = 0; i < len; i++) {
      data[i] = (Math.random() * 2 - 1) * (1 - i / len);
    }
    grain = buf;
    return grain;
  }

  /**
   * ONE PRESS. Two layered events, under 60ms, at a low gain.
   * Silent unless armed, and silent unless a press has already built the context.
   */
  function press(kind) {
    if (!armed || !audio) return false;
    if (audio.state === 'suspended' && audio.resume) audio.resume();

    var v = VOICES[kind] || VOICES.secondary;
    var t = audio.currentTime;
    var wobble = 1 + (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.05;

    /* 1. THE CLICK OF THE STEM — filtered noise, no pitch, gone in a few milliseconds. */
    var src = audio.createBufferSource();
    src.buffer = noise(audio);
    var band = audio.createBiquadFilter();
    band.type = 'bandpass';
    band.frequency.setValueAtTime(v.clickHz * wobble, t);
    band.Q.value = v.clickQ;
    var clickGain = audio.createGain();
    clickGain.gain.setValueAtTime(v.clickGain, t);
    clickGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, t + v.clickDur);
    src.connect(band).connect(clickGain).connect(audio.destination);
    src.start(t);
    src.stop(t + v.clickDur + 0.004);

    /* 2. THE THOCK OF THE BOTTOM-OUT — a low body, pitched down as it dies. */
    var at = t + 0.004;
    var osc = audio.createOscillator();
    osc.type = 'triangle';
    osc.frequency.setValueAtTime(v.bodyHz * wobble, at);
    osc.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(v.bodyHz * 0.55, at + v.bodyDur);
    var bodyGain = audio.createGain();
    bodyGain.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, at);
    bodyGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(v.bodyGain, at + 0.003);
    bodyGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, at + v.bodyDur);
    osc.connect(bodyGain).connect(audio.destination);
    osc.start(at);
    osc.stop(at + v.bodyDur + 0.008);

    hit(v);
    return true;
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the toggles */

  function toggles() {
    return document.querySelectorAll('[data-sound-toggle]');
  }

  function paint() {
    var list = toggles();
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      list[i].setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(armed));
      list[i].setAttribute(
        'aria-label',
        armed ? 'Turn interface sound off' : 'Turn interface sound on'
      );
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the meter */

  /*
   * A CANVAS THAT SHOWS THE SOUND IT IS ABOUT TO MAKE. It is the toggle's own icon: a flat line
   * while sound is off, a live trace while it is on, and a kick on every press whose height is the
   * press's own body gain. It is entirely optional — a layout without one is silent about it and
   * every other line above still runs.
   *
   * IT IS THE ONLY AMBIENT MOTION THIS FILE OWNS, AND IT STOPS THREE WAYS: it never starts while
   * sound is off, it stops on prefers-reduced-motion, and it stops on visibilitychange. A
   * backgrounded tab must not burn a core for a line nobody is looking at.
   */
  var scope = null;
  var scopeCtx = null;
  var frame = 0;
  var energy = 0;
  var phase = 0;
  var reduced = window.matchMedia ? window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') : null;

  function findScope() {
    var el = document.querySelector('[data-sound-scope]');
    if (!el || !el.getContext) return;
    scope = el;
    scopeCtx = el.getContext('2d');
  }

  function stopped() {
    return !armed || document.hidden === true || !!(reduced && reduced.matches);
  }

  function paintScope() {
    if (!scope || !scopeCtx) return;
    var w = scope.width || 0;
    var h = scope.height || 0;
    if (!w || !h) return;
    var mid = h / 2;
    var ink = '';
    if (window.getComputedStyle) {
      ink = window.getComputedStyle(scope).getPropertyValue('color');
    }
    scopeCtx.clearRect(0, 0, w, h);
    scopeCtx.beginPath();
    for (var x = 0; x <= w; x += 2) {
      var k = x / w;
      var taper = Math.sin(Math.PI * k);
      var wave = Math.sin(k * 14 + phase) * 0.55 + Math.sin(k * 31 - phase * 1.7) * 0.45;
      var amp = (0.16 + energy * 0.84) * (mid - 1.5) * taper;
      var y = mid + wave * amp;
      if (x === 0) scopeCtx.moveTo(x, y);
      else scopeCtx.lineTo(x, y);
    }
    scopeCtx.strokeStyle = ink ? ink.trim() : 'currentColor';
    scopeCtx.lineWidth = 2;
    scopeCtx.stroke();
  }

  function tickScope() {
    if (stopped()) { frame = 0; paintScope(); return; }
    phase += 0.06;
    energy *= 0.9;
    if (energy < 0.004) energy = 0;
    paintScope();
    frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tickScope);
  }

  function runScope() {
    /* The CSS half of the same stop. Every ambient rule in InterfaceSound.astro is paused by this
       attribute, so prefers-reduced-motion, a hidden tab and "sound is off" all halt the keyframes
       as well as the canvas — one predicate, not two that can disagree. */
    var still = stopped();
    if (document.documentElement && document.documentElement.setAttribute) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-sound-still', still ? 'true' : 'false');
    }
    if (!scope) return;
    if (frame) { window.cancelAnimationFrame(frame); frame = 0; }
    if (still) { paintScope(); return; }
    frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tickScope);
  }

  /** The visible half of a press: the meter kicks, and the control flashes its ring. */
  function hit(v) {
    energy = Math.min(1, 0.55 + v.bodyGain * 6);
    runScope();
    var list = toggles();
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var el = list[i];
      if (!el.classList) continue;
      el.classList.remove('is-hit');
      /* Reading offsetWidth restarts a CSS animation that is already running; without it a second
         press inside the animation's own duration adds a class that is already there and nothing
         plays. */
      void el.offsetWidth;
      el.classList.add('is-hit');
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the dock's place */

  /*
   * A FLOATING CONTROL MUST NOT COVER A CONTROL, and this one did.
   *
   * MEASURED, on the built landing, at nine viewport sizes: at 740x360 and 667x375 — a phone held
   * sideways — the hero fills the screen, the corner the dock floats in lands ON the composer, and
   * 66x13 of the SEND BUTTON was underneath it. Both corners: moving it left is no fix, because the
   * composer spans the width. At 1440x900, 1280x620, 1280x480, 1024x700, 900x560, 800x560 and
   * 390x844 the corner is clear.
   *
   * A media query cannot express that boundary — 1280x480 is clear and 1024x540 is not, so it is
   * not a height rule or a width rule. The dock therefore MEASURES: if its own rectangle overlaps
   * any control, it stops floating and takes its place at the end of the page, where it cannot
   * steal a press. This is the same rule apps/web states as "decoration yields to the composer",
   * applied by the decoration rather than assumed by it.
   *
   * On load and on resize, never on scroll. The composer sits at the top of the page, so scrolling
   * carries it AWAY from a bottom corner; and a control that jumps around while the page scrolls is
   * worse than one that overlaps.
   */
  var CONTROLS = 'button, [role="button"], a[href], input, textarea, select, summary';

  function rectOf(el) {
    return el && el.getBoundingClientRect ? el.getBoundingClientRect() : null;
  }

  function placeDock() {
    var dock = document.querySelector('[data-sound-dock]');
    if (!dock || !dock.getBoundingClientRect || !dock.setAttribute) return;
    /* Measure the floating position, not the one it was last given. */
    if (dock.removeAttribute) dock.removeAttribute('data-flow');
    var d = rectOf(dock);
    if (!d || !d.width || !d.height) return;
    var list = document.querySelectorAll(CONTROLS);
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var el = list[i];
      if (el.closest && el.closest('[data-sound-dock]')) continue;
      var r = rectOf(el);
      if (!r || !r.width || !r.height) continue;
      if (r.left < d.right && r.right > d.left && r.top < d.bottom && r.bottom > d.top) {
        dock.setAttribute('data-flow', '');
        return;
      }
    }
  }

  var placing = 0;
  function schedulePlace() {
    if (placing) return;
    placing = window.requestAnimationFrame(function () { placing = 0; placeDock(); });
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the one listener */

  function voiceFor(el) {
    var explicit = el.getAttribute ? el.getAttribute('data-sound') : null;
    if (explicit === 'primary' || explicit === 'secondary' || explicit === 'toggle') return explicit;
    if (el.hasAttribute && (el.hasAttribute('aria-pressed') || el.hasAttribute('data-theme-toggle'))) {
      return 'toggle';
    }
    var name = el.className;
    if (name && typeof name !== 'string' && typeof name.baseVal === 'string') name = name.baseVal;
    var cls = ' ' + (typeof name === 'string' ? name : '') + ' ';
    if (/\bpill-quiet\b|\biconbtn\b|\bghost\b|\bquiet\b/.test(cls)) return 'secondary';
    if (/\bprimary\b|\bcta\b|\bpill\b/.test(cls)) return 'primary';
    if (el.getAttribute && el.getAttribute('type') === 'submit') return 'primary';
    return 'secondary';
  }

  /*
   * ONE LISTENER FOR BOTH JOBS, which is what makes "never more than once per press" structural
   * rather than a promise. The toggle is a button too: if arming were handled in one listener and
   * pressing in another, the press that arms the sound would make two sounds.
   */
  document.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
    var target = e.target;
    if (!target || !target.closest) return;

    var toggle = target.closest('[data-sound-toggle]');
    if (toggle) {
      armed = !armed;
      if (armed) {
        ensureAudio();
        if (audio && audio.resume) audio.resume();
      }
      remember(armed);
      paint();
      if (armed) press('toggle');
      runScope();
      return;
    }

    var control = target.closest(PRESSABLE);
    if (!control) return;
    if (control.getAttribute && control.getAttribute('data-sound') === 'none') return;
    if (control.hasAttribute && control.hasAttribute('disabled')) return;
    /* A choice carried over from a previous visit arms on this session's first press — still a
       gesture, still never at load. */
    if (armed && !audio) {
      ensureAudio();
      if (audio && audio.resume) audio.resume();
    }
    press(voiceFor(control));
  });

  document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', runScope);
  window.addEventListener('resize', schedulePlace);
  if (reduced) {
    if (reduced.addEventListener) reduced.addEventListener('change', runScope);
    else if (reduced.addListener) reduced.addListener(runScope);
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ boot */

  findScope();
  placeDock();
  paint();
  paintScope();
  runScope();

  /* The public surface. `appleTick` is the retired name and is kept aimed at the new synth, so
     anything that already called it gets a keyswitch instead of a chisel tick rather than an
     error. */
  window.appleSound = {
    press: press,
    isOn: function () { return armed; },
    voices: VOICES
  };
  window.appleTick = function () { return press('secondary'); };
})();

data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>Docs</p> <h1 class="carved" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>Credits &amp; limits</h1> <div class="prose" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>  <p>
Credits are Apple's unit of daily energy. Every AI request burns some; your balance refills to
    full once a day, <strong>up to a monthly ceiling</strong>. The system exists for one reason:
    real inference costs real compute, and a hard, transparent quota is what lets the free tier be
    genuinely free — no card, no trial clock, no surprise bill.
</p> <h2>The numbers</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Free plan:</strong> 231 Credits per day · 2,310 a month.</li> <li><strong>Builder plan:</strong> 416 Credits per day · 12,600 a month.</li><li><strong>Studio plan:</strong> 700 Credits per day · 21,000 a month.</li> <li><strong>Plan:</strong> from 2 credits per request.</li><li><strong>Agent:</strong> from 4 credits per request.</li> </ul> <p>
Those are starting prices, not ceilings: a request settles against the compute it actually
    used, so a short question lands on its figure and a long build climbs past it. In practice the
    free allowance is a solid daily session — about 115 Plan requests, or about 57 Agent requests, or, far more usually, a mix.
</p> <h2>How metering works</h2> <p>
Your balance is one click away in the workspace: the dock down the left edge carries a
<strong>Usage and Credits</strong> row, and it opens a page with the figure, the last thirty
    days, and what your next request costs in each mode. The left navigation is closed when the
    workspace loads, so the meter itself is not on screen until you open it — once you do, it sits
    in the footer of the left rail beside your account, reading what is left, what your allowance is
    and when it resets. Either surface is read when the page loads and does not refresh itself while
    you build — reload for the current figure. What does move as it happens is the run you are
    watching: the thinking panel counts the Credits this run has spent, step by step. One Credit is taken when a request starts, and the
    rest settles against the compute the run actually consumed, so a long build's cost arrives as
    it is incurred rather than as a total you could not see coming.
</p> <p>
A step that fails on our side is not charged: Credits are settled from the compute a call
    actually reported, and a call that returned nothing reports nothing. Beyond that, a run that
    ends in failure having left you nothing to keep gives its Credits back on its own — the reply
    tells you how many and you do not have to ask. A run that changed your place keeps its Credits
    whatever went wrong afterwards, because the work is still there; and stopping a run yourself is
    not a failure, so it is not refunded.
</p> <h2>The daily reset — and the monthly ceiling behind it</h2> <p>
Quotas reset at midnight UTC — one fixed instant for every account, not a rolling window
    that starts when you do. That is worth knowing if you build late in the UTC day: credits
    spent at 23:00 UTC are refilled an hour later. The workspace shows your exact
    reset time. Unused Credits do not roll over — every day starts at your full allowance.
</p> <p> <strong>There are two limits, and you have whichever is smaller.</strong> The daily figure is a
    rate; the monthly figure is a ceiling, and a day's refill cannot take you past it.
 On the Free plan the ceiling is the one that bites: 231 a day against 2,310 a month is <strong>10 full days</strong>.
        Spend the whole daily allowance every day and the eleventh is where it stops until the month
        turns. Pace it and the same total stretches across the month instead.
  The usage meter names which of the two you are up against rather than showing one number for
    both.
</p> <h2>Running out</h2> <p>When your balance hits zero:</p> <ul> <li>New AI requests are declined with a clear message and your reset time — never a silent failure.</li> <li>Everything that does not burn inference keeps working: reading chat history, browsing your project, creating and restoring checkpoints, pairing Studio.</li> <li>Nothing is deleted, downgraded or lost. You are just out of energy until the reset.</li> </ul> <h2>The limit that is not yours</h2> <p>
Your allowance is not the only ceiling. Apple also caps what the <em>whole service</em> spends
    on inference in a day, shared by everyone using it, and that cap can be reached while your own
    balance still has Credits in it. A run stopped by it says so in its own words — “Apple has
    reached today's shared building capacity” — and it resets at midnight UTC like everything else
    here. It exists so that one runaway build cannot take the free tier down for the rest of the
    day. <a href="/docs/troubleshooting">Troubleshooting</a> covers what a run that hits it costs
    you and what it leaves behind.
</p> <h2>Project files</h2> <p>
Apple keeps notes, plans and generated data in a workspace beside each project — Apple's own
    storage, not your Roblox place — and you can open, add, rename and download those files from the
    Files drawer in the workspace. It holds <strong>text files only</strong>: .md, .txt, .json,
    .csv, .luau, .lua, .ts, .js, .yml and .yaml. Generated images are separate: download them
    from their result in the conversation. Roblox models live in your place.
</p> <ul> <li><strong>48 KB per file.</strong> A file past that is refused rather than truncated, so a
      half-saved document is never what you find later. Long material belongs in several files.</li> <li><strong>20 earlier versions of each file are kept.</strong> Every write archives the one
      before it, and any kept version can be read and put back — putting one back is itself a new
      version, so nothing in between is lost.</li> <li><strong>Deleted files are recoverable for 30 days.</strong> Delete moves a file to the
      project's trash with a real deadline on it, and the drawer says how long each one has left.</li> </ul> <p>
None of this counts against your Credits. Credits pay for inference; files are storage, and the
    storage has the limits described here.
</p> <h2>Generated images</h2> <p>
New generated images stay with their project until it is deleted. Each image can be up to
1 MiB, with at most 64 images
    and 16 MiB of encoded image data per project
    (encoding uses about a third more space than the downloaded file).
    Download a copy to keep outside Apple. Older temporary images that have expired cannot be recovered.
</p> <p>
Generation is refused before starting when project or service storage is full. Existing images
    are not removed to make room. Concurrent runs can still fill the space while an image is being
    generated; if saving fails, Apple reports that failure instead of claiming delivery.
</p> <h2>Other limits worth knowing</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Rate limiting:</strong> requests are queued per account, and under heavy load a request may briefly wait. No plan buys a place further up that queue — paying changes your allowance, not your turn.</li> <li><strong>Checkpoints:</strong> Apple keeps your 25 most recent checkpoints per project. Taking the twenty-sixth deletes the oldest in the same write — by age, whether you took it yourself or Apple took it before a change. Restore the one you want before it falls off the end.</li> <li><strong>One account per person:</strong> multiplying free accounts to farm quota is against the <a href="/terms">terms</a> and gets caught.</li> </ul> <div class="callout"> <p> <strong>Making Credits go further:</strong> design the build in Plan before you run it — a question costs a fraction of a wrong build; give Agent specific requests (“the door in Workspace.Lobby”) rather than vague ones. Nothing else moves the number much —
      the expensive request is almost always the one that had to be sent twice.
</p> </div>  </div> <footer class="docs__foot" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <p data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>
