</p> </div> </div> </footer>   <script>/* =====================================================================================
 * INTERFACE SOUND — ONE IMPLEMENTATION, SHARED BY EVERY LAYOUT.
 *
 * This file is the whole sound system. Base.astro and Landing.astro both inline THIS TEXT
 * through layouts/InterfaceSound.astro, so there is one synth, one listener and one stored
 * preference for the entire site. Before this there was a copy in Base.astro and nothing at all
 * on the front page, which is two states that cannot agree and one page with no control.
 *
 * WHAT THE OWNER ASKED FOR. He played with rosebud.ai and singled out one thing: pressing a button
 * makes a satisfying mechanical keyboard click. Measured on that page the same day (recorded in
 * packages/corpus/data/ui-references/web-landing.json, claim 16): its resource timing list contains
 * no mp3, wav, ogg, m4a or webm anywhere, while AudioContext is available — so their click is
 * SYNTHESISED at interaction time, not downloaded. That is the cheaper technique and the one used
 * here. A synthesised click costs no bytes, has no load state, and cannot be the reason a button
 * feels late.
 *
 * WHAT A KEYSWITCH ACTUALLY SOUNDS LIKE, and why the old `tick()` did not. The retired version was
 * one triangle oscillator sliding down — a soft chisel tick, a single event. A mechanical key press
 * is TWO events layered: the CLICK OF THE STEM, a bright noise transient of a few milliseconds with
 * no pitch of its own, and the THOCK OF THE BOTTOM-OUT, a low short body as the key meets the
 * plate. Both are below, layered with the body starting 4ms after the transient, and the whole
 * envelope is finished inside 58ms at its longest voice.
 *
 * THE INTERFACE HAS A VOICE RATHER THAN A BEEP. Three voices, chosen the way the reference's accent
 * family is chosen — one object, three jobs: a primary action is lower and fuller, a secondary
 * lighter and shorter, a toggle a touch brighter. Every press also carries a ±2.5% wobble, because
 * a sound repeated at exactly one frequency stops reading as a mechanism and starts reading as a
 * notification.
 *
 * THE PROPERTIES THIS FILE MUST KEEP, all of them checked by tests/interface-sound.test.mjs:
 *   - OFF by default. Nothing is armed by loading a page.
 *   - The AudioContext is constructed by a PRESS and never by load — the visitor's press on the
 *     toggle, or, when a previous visit already chose sound, that session's first press. Both are
 *     real user gestures, which is what browsers require; neither is page load.
 *   - Nothing autoplays.
 *   - The choice persists exactly the way the theme choice does, in localStorage under
 *     `apple-sound`, and is read back on the next page.
 *   - Every toggle states its state in aria-pressed and aria-label.
 *   - Never on hover, never on load, never more than once per press: ONE delegated listener owns
 *     both the toggle and the press, so a press on the toggle cannot produce two sounds.
 *
 * NO `document.currentScript`. Astro hoists a component <script> into a module script where
 * currentScript is null by specification; a hero effect shipped that way this morning and never ran
 * at all. Everything here is found with querySelector, and every one of those lookups tolerates a
 * null.
 * ===================================================================================== */
(function () {
  'use strict';

  var STORE_KEY = 'apple-sound';

  /* Everything that reads as a press. Buttons and links-as-buttons across both layouts: the
     landing's `.pill`, the chrome's `.iconbtn` and `.nav__cta`, anything with an explicit
     role, and `[data-sound-press]` for a control that is none of those. A bare prose link is
     deliberately absent — navigation is not a keystroke. */
  var PRESSABLE = [
    'button',
    '[role="button"]',
    'input[type="submit"]',
    'input[type="button"]',
    'summary',
    'a.pill',
    'a.btn',
    'a.cta',
    'a.button',
    'a.nav__cta',
    'a.nav__signin',
    'a[data-cta]',
    '[data-sound-press]'
  ].join(', ');

  /* THE THREE VOICES. clickHz is the band the stem transient sits in, bodyHz the pitch of the
     bottom-out. Gains are deliberately low: this is a texture under a finger, not an alert. */
  var VOICES = {
    primary:   { clickHz: 2400, clickQ: 0.9, clickGain: 0.034, clickDur: 0.010, bodyHz: 132, bodyGain: 0.075, bodyDur: 0.044 },
    secondary: { clickHz: 3200, clickQ: 1.1, clickGain: 0.026, clickDur: 0.008, bodyHz: 196, bodyGain: 0.048, bodyDur: 0.032 },
    toggle:    { clickHz: 4200, clickQ: 1.3, clickGain: 0.036, clickDur: 0.007, bodyHz: 240, bodyGain: 0.052, bodyDur: 0.030 }
  };

  var audio = null;       // constructed by a press, never by load
  var grain = null;       // the noise buffer, built once per context
  var armed = stored();   // the visitor's persisted choice; false on a first visit

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ preference */

  function stored() {
    try {
      return localStorage.getItem(STORE_KEY) === 'on';
    } catch (err) {
      return false; /* private mode — off, which is the default anyway */
    }
  }

  function remember(on) {
    try {
      localStorage.setItem(STORE_KEY, on ? 'on' : 'off');
    } catch (err) {
      /* private mode — the choice still applies for this page view */
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the synth */

  /** Construct the context. Called from the click handler and from nowhere else. */
  function ensureAudio() {
    if (audio) return audio;
    /* The prefixed name is Safari's, and it is still how an older iOS reaches this API. The cast
       is for the type checker only; there is no TypeScript in a file that ships as it is written. */
    var w = /** @type {any} */ (window);
    var Ctx = w.AudioContext || w.webkitAudioContext;
    if (!Ctx) return null;
    audio = new Ctx();
    return audio;
  }

  /** A short burst of decaying white noise, built once and re-triggered per press. */
  function noise(ac) {
    if (grain) return grain;
    var rate = ac.sampleRate || 44100;
    var len = Math.max(64, Math.floor(rate * 0.06));
    var buf = ac.createBuffer(1, len, rate);
    var data = buf.getChannelData(0);
    for (var i = 0; i < len; i++) {
      data[i] = (Math.random() * 2 - 1) * (1 - i / len);
    }
    grain = buf;
    return grain;
  }

  /**
   * ONE PRESS. Two layered events, under 60ms, at a low gain.
   * Silent unless armed, and silent unless a press has already built the context.
   */
  function press(kind) {
    if (!armed || !audio) return false;
    if (audio.state === 'suspended' && audio.resume) audio.resume();

    var v = VOICES[kind] || VOICES.secondary;
    var t = audio.currentTime;
    var wobble = 1 + (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.05;

    /* 1. THE CLICK OF THE STEM — filtered noise, no pitch, gone in a few milliseconds. */
    var src = audio.createBufferSource();
    src.buffer = noise(audio);
    var band = audio.createBiquadFilter();
    band.type = 'bandpass';
    band.frequency.setValueAtTime(v.clickHz * wobble, t);
    band.Q.value = v.clickQ;
    var clickGain = audio.createGain();
    clickGain.gain.setValueAtTime(v.clickGain, t);
    clickGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, t + v.clickDur);
    src.connect(band).connect(clickGain).connect(audio.destination);
    src.start(t);
    src.stop(t + v.clickDur + 0.004);

    /* 2. THE THOCK OF THE BOTTOM-OUT — a low body, pitched down as it dies. */
    var at = t + 0.004;
    var osc = audio.createOscillator();
    osc.type = 'triangle';
    osc.frequency.setValueAtTime(v.bodyHz * wobble, at);
    osc.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(v.bodyHz * 0.55, at + v.bodyDur);
    var bodyGain = audio.createGain();
    bodyGain.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, at);
    bodyGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(v.bodyGain, at + 0.003);
    bodyGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, at + v.bodyDur);
    osc.connect(bodyGain).connect(audio.destination);
    osc.start(at);
    osc.stop(at + v.bodyDur + 0.008);

    hit(v);
    return true;
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the toggles */

  function toggles() {
    return document.querySelectorAll('[data-sound-toggle]');
  }

  function paint() {
    var list = toggles();
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      list[i].setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(armed));
      list[i].setAttribute(
        'aria-label',
        armed ? 'Turn interface sound off' : 'Turn interface sound on'
      );
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the meter */

  /*
   * A CANVAS THAT SHOWS THE SOUND IT IS ABOUT TO MAKE. It is the toggle's own icon: a flat line
   * while sound is off, a live trace while it is on, and a kick on every press whose height is the
   * press's own body gain. It is entirely optional — a layout without one is silent about it and
   * every other line above still runs.
   *
   * IT IS THE ONLY AMBIENT MOTION THIS FILE OWNS, AND IT STOPS THREE WAYS: it never starts while
   * sound is off, it stops on prefers-reduced-motion, and it stops on visibilitychange. A
   * backgrounded tab must not burn a core for a line nobody is looking at.
   */
  var scope = null;
  var scopeCtx = null;
  var frame = 0;
  var energy = 0;
  var phase = 0;
  var reduced = window.matchMedia ? window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') : null;

  function findScope() {
    var el = document.querySelector('[data-sound-scope]');
    if (!el || !el.getContext) return;
    scope = el;
    scopeCtx = el.getContext('2d');
  }

  function stopped() {
    return !armed || document.hidden === true || !!(reduced && reduced.matches);
  }

  function paintScope() {
    if (!scope || !scopeCtx) return;
    var w = scope.width || 0;
    var h = scope.height || 0;
    if (!w || !h) return;
    var mid = h / 2;
    var ink = '';
    if (window.getComputedStyle) {
      ink = window.getComputedStyle(scope).getPropertyValue('color');
    }
    scopeCtx.clearRect(0, 0, w, h);
    scopeCtx.beginPath();
    for (var x = 0; x <= w; x += 2) {
      var k = x / w;
      var taper = Math.sin(Math.PI * k);
      var wave = Math.sin(k * 14 + phase) * 0.55 + Math.sin(k * 31 - phase * 1.7) * 0.45;
      var amp = (0.16 + energy * 0.84) * (mid - 1.5) * taper;
      var y = mid + wave * amp;
      if (x === 0) scopeCtx.moveTo(x, y);
      else scopeCtx.lineTo(x, y);
    }
    scopeCtx.strokeStyle = ink ? ink.trim() : 'currentColor';
    scopeCtx.lineWidth = 2;
    scopeCtx.stroke();
  }

  function tickScope() {
    if (stopped()) { frame = 0; paintScope(); return; }
    phase += 0.06;
    energy *= 0.9;
    if (energy < 0.004) energy = 0;
    paintScope();
    frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tickScope);
  }

  function runScope() {
    /* The CSS half of the same stop. Every ambient rule in InterfaceSound.astro is paused by this
       attribute, so prefers-reduced-motion, a hidden tab and "sound is off" all halt the keyframes
       as well as the canvas — one predicate, not two that can disagree. */
    var still = stopped();
    if (document.documentElement && document.documentElement.setAttribute) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-sound-still', still ? 'true' : 'false');
    }
    if (!scope) return;
    if (frame) { window.cancelAnimationFrame(frame); frame = 0; }
    if (still) { paintScope(); return; }
    frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tickScope);
  }

  /** The visible half of a press: the meter kicks, and the control flashes its ring. */
  function hit(v) {
    energy = Math.min(1, 0.55 + v.bodyGain * 6);
    runScope();
    var list = toggles();
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var el = list[i];
      if (!el.classList) continue;
      el.classList.remove('is-hit');
      /* Reading offsetWidth restarts a CSS animation that is already running; without it a second
         press inside the animation's own duration adds a class that is already there and nothing
         plays. */
      void el.offsetWidth;
      el.classList.add('is-hit');
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the dock's place */

  /*
   * A FLOATING CONTROL MUST NOT COVER A CONTROL, and this one did.
   *
   * MEASURED, on the built landing, at nine viewport sizes: at 740x360 and 667x375 — a phone held
   * sideways — the hero fills the screen, the corner the dock floats in lands ON the composer, and
   * 66x13 of the SEND BUTTON was underneath it. Both corners: moving it left is no fix, because the
   * composer spans the width. At 1440x900, 1280x620, 1280x480, 1024x700, 900x560, 800x560 and
   * 390x844 the corner is clear.
   *
   * A media query cannot express that boundary — 1280x480 is clear and 1024x540 is not, so it is
   * not a height rule or a width rule. The dock therefore MEASURES: if its own rectangle overlaps
   * any control, it stops floating and takes its place at the end of the page, where it cannot
   * steal a press. This is the same rule apps/web states as "decoration yields to the composer",
   * applied by the decoration rather than assumed by it.
   *
   * On load and on resize, never on scroll. The composer sits at the top of the page, so scrolling
   * carries it AWAY from a bottom corner; and a control that jumps around while the page scrolls is
   * worse than one that overlaps.
   */
  var CONTROLS = 'button, [role="button"], a[href], input, textarea, select, summary';

  function rectOf(el) {
    return el && el.getBoundingClientRect ? el.getBoundingClientRect() : null;
  }

  function placeDock() {
    var dock = document.querySelector('[data-sound-dock]');
    if (!dock || !dock.getBoundingClientRect || !dock.setAttribute) return;
    /* Measure the floating position, not the one it was last given. */
    if (dock.removeAttribute) dock.removeAttribute('data-flow');
    var d = rectOf(dock);
    if (!d || !d.width || !d.height) return;
    var list = document.querySelectorAll(CONTROLS);
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var el = list[i];
      if (el.closest && el.closest('[data-sound-dock]')) continue;
      var r = rectOf(el);
      if (!r || !r.width || !r.height) continue;
      if (r.left < d.right && r.right > d.left && r.top < d.bottom && r.bottom > d.top) {
        dock.setAttribute('data-flow', '');
        return;
      }
    }
  }

  var placing = 0;
  function schedulePlace() {
    if (placing) return;
    placing = window.requestAnimationFrame(function () { placing = 0; placeDock(); });
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the one listener */

  function voiceFor(el) {
    var explicit = el.getAttribute ? el.getAttribute('data-sound') : null;
    if (explicit === 'primary' || explicit === 'secondary' || explicit === 'toggle') return explicit;
    if (el.hasAttribute && (el.hasAttribute('aria-pressed') || el.hasAttribute('data-theme-toggle'))) {
      return 'toggle';
    }
    var name = el.className;
    if (name && typeof name !== 'string' && typeof name.baseVal === 'string') name = name.baseVal;
    var cls = ' ' + (typeof name === 'string' ? name : '') + ' ';
    if (/\bpill-quiet\b|\biconbtn\b|\bghost\b|\bquiet\b/.test(cls)) return 'secondary';
    if (/\bprimary\b|\bcta\b|\bpill\b/.test(cls)) return 'primary';
    if (el.getAttribute && el.getAttribute('type') === 'submit') return 'primary';
    return 'secondary';
  }

  /*
   * ONE LISTENER FOR BOTH JOBS, which is what makes "never more than once per press" structural
   * rather than a promise. The toggle is a button too: if arming were handled in one listener and
   * pressing in another, the press that arms the sound would make two sounds.
   */
  document.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
    var target = e.target;
    if (!target || !target.closest) return;

    var toggle = target.closest('[data-sound-toggle]');
    if (toggle) {
      armed = !armed;
      if (armed) {
        ensureAudio();
        if (audio && audio.resume) audio.resume();
      }
      remember(armed);
      paint();
      if (armed) press('toggle');
      runScope();
      return;
    }

    var control = target.closest(PRESSABLE);
    if (!control) return;
    if (control.getAttribute && control.getAttribute('data-sound') === 'none') return;
    if (control.hasAttribute && control.hasAttribute('disabled')) return;
    /* A choice carried over from a previous visit arms on this session's first press — still a
       gesture, still never at load. */
    if (armed && !audio) {

    voices: VOICES
  };
  window.appleTick = function () { return press('secondary'); };

data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>Docs</p> <h1 class="carved" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>Frequently asked questions</h1> <div class="prose" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>  <p data-astro-cid-fmtq6k42>
Answers to the questions that reach our inbox most. Pricing and quota questions live on the
<a href="/pricing" data-astro-cid-fmtq6k42>pricing page</a>; data questions on
<a href="/docs/privacy-and-data" data-astro-cid-fmtq6k42>privacy &amp; data</a>.
</p> <div class="faq-block" data-astro-cid-fmtq6k42> <div class="faq" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <details class="faq__item" style="--i:0" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <summary data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <span class="faq__q" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr>Where do I get the Apple plugin?</span> <span class="faq__mark" aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr></span> </summary> <div class="faq__a" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr><p>From the Roblox Creator Store, and only from there — see <a href="/docs/plugin">Install the plugin</a>, which also states plainly whether it is published yet. Roblox splits this into two steps: you acquire the plugin on the web, then install it from inside Studio's Toolbox. There is no one-click install from a web page; Roblox provides no such hand-off.</p></div> </details><details class="faq__item" style="--i:1" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <summary data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <span class="faq__q" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr>There used to be a .rbxm download. Where did it go?</span> <span class="faq__mark" aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr></span> </summary> <div class="faq__a" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr><p>Retired. A file you drop into a folder by hand never updates, is not signed by anything, and gets no help from Studio's plugin management window. The Creator Store install is the supported path. Building the plugin yourself is still possible and documented under <a href="/docs/build-from-source">Build the plugin from source</a>, but that is a development path, not an install path.</p></div> </details><details class="faq__item" style="--i:2" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <summary data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <span class="faq__q" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr>Do I need to know how to script?</span> <span class="faq__mark" aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr></span> </summary> <div class="faq__a" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr><p>No, but it helps. Apple writes the Luau for you and explains anything it wrote in plain language (just ask it to explain what it wrote). Creators who can read a little code iterate faster, and plenty of people have learned scripting <em>from</em> Apple's explanations of its own work.</p></div> </details><details class="faq__item" style="--i:3" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <summary data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <span class="faq__q" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr>Which Roblox Studio versions are supported?</span> <span class="faq__mark" aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr></span> </summary> <div class="faq__a" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr><p>Current production Roblox Studio on Windows and macOS. The plugin uses only stable, documented Studio APIs, so ordinary Studio updates don't break it. If Roblox ships a breaking change, the <a href="/changelog">changelog</a> and the plugin panel will both say so.</p></div> </details><details class="faq__item" style="--i:4" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <summary data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <span class="faq__q" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr>Can Apple publish my game?</span> <span class="faq__mark" aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr></span> </summary> <div class="faq__a" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr><p>No, by design. Apple builds inside your open place; publishing to Roblox stays a human decision made by you, in Studio, with your own account. Apple has no publishing permission over your account and does not ask for one.</p>
      <p>There is one credential you can give it, and only if you want to: an Open Cloud API key, connected under Settings &rarr; Connections, which lets Apple upload images and audio it generates into <em>your</em> Roblox account instead of ours. It is stored encrypted, never shown again, used only for the permissions you ticked, and you can disconnect it at any time. <a href="/docs/troubleshooting#roblox-key-refused">What to do if Roblox refuses it</a>.</p></div> </details><details class="faq__item" style="--i:5" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <summary data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <span class="faq__q" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr>Does Apple work with team projects / Team Create?</span> <span class="faq__mark" aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr></span> </summary> <div class="faq__a" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr><p>Apple works on the place open in the paired Studio window. In Team Create sessions its edits appear to teammates like any collaborator's edits. One pairing belongs to one Studio window; teammates who want their own Apple chats should use their own accounts and projects.</p></div> </details><details class="faq__item" style="--i:6" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <summary data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <span class="faq__q" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr>What happens if I close Studio mid-build?</span> <span class="faq__mark" aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr></span> </summary> <div class="faq__a" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr><p>The agent notices it lost its hands and pauses the run with a clear message. Work that never ran is never charged — Credits settle against the compute a call actually reported, and a call that did not happen reports nothing. Reopen the place, reconnect, and ask Apple to continue — the plan and history are still in the project.</p></div> </details><details class="faq__item" style="--i:7" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <summary data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <span class="faq__q" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr>Apple made a change I hate. Now what?</span> <span class="faq__mark" aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr></span> </summary> <div class="faq__a" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr><p>Three exits, in order of size: press <kbd>Ctrl+Z</kbd> in Studio to take back the last change (one undo step per change Apple made, so a multi-step run needs one press per step); restore the automatic checkpoint taken before the run, which undoes the whole run in one action; or just tell Apple what you hate — it can usually fix a wrong turn faster than a rollback.</p></div> </details><details class="faq__item" style="--i:8" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <summary data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <span class="faq__q" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr>Is there an API or a way to script Apple itself?</span> <span class="faq__mark" aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr></span> </summary> <div class="faq__a" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr><p>Yes. There is an HTTP API at <code>/v1</code> on the same host as the app, with scoped keys: chat completions, your projects and their transcripts, starting an agent run, a server-sent event stream of run state, and a Model Context Protocol endpoint for MCP clients.</p>
      <p>Mint a key under <strong>Settings &rarr; Connections &rarr; API keys</strong> in the app — you see the secret once, and you can rotate or revoke it from the same panel. The surface documents itself: <code>GET /v1</code> lists every route and the scope it needs, and <code>GET /v1/openapi.json</code> is the machine-readable description. Both accept any valid key. There is no separate docs page for it yet, and no published client library — the API is the thing that exists.</p></div> </details><details class="faq__item" style="--i:9" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <summary data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <span class="faq__q" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr>How do I report a bug or ask for a feature?</span> <span class="faq__mark" aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr></span> </summary> <div class="faq__a" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr><p>Email <a href="mailto:apple.labs.app@gmail.com">apple.labs.app@gmail.com</a>. Include the project name and roughly when it happened; screenshots welcome. Feedback lands directly with the people who build the product — there is no ticket abyss.</p></div> </details> </div>  </div>  </div> <footer class="docs__foot" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <p data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>
Stuck? Ask in the app, check your Credits before sending, or email
<a href="mailto:apple.labs.app@gmail.com" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>apple.labs.app@gmail.com</a>.

</p> </div> </div> </footer>   <script>/* =====================================================================================
 * INTERFACE SOUND — ONE IMPLEMENTATION, SHARED BY EVERY LAYOUT.
 *
 * This file is the whole sound system. Base.astro and Landing.astro both inline THIS TEXT
 * through layouts/InterfaceSound.astro, so there is one synth, one listener and one stored
 * preference for the entire site. Before this there was a copy in Base.astro and nothing at all
 * on the front page, which is two states that cannot agree and one page with no control.
 *
 * WHAT THE OWNER ASKED FOR. He played with rosebud.ai and singled out one thing: pressing a button
 * makes a satisfying mechanical keyboard click. Measured on that page the same day (recorded in
 * packages/corpus/data/ui-references/web-landing.json, claim 16): its resource timing list contains
 * no mp3, wav, ogg, m4a or webm anywhere, while AudioContext is available — so their click is
 * SYNTHESISED at interaction time, not downloaded. That is the cheaper technique and the one used
 * here. A synthesised click costs no bytes, has no load state, and cannot be the reason a button
 * feels late.
 *
 * WHAT A KEYSWITCH ACTUALLY SOUNDS LIKE, and why the old `tick()` did not. The retired version was
 * one triangle oscillator sliding down — a soft chisel tick, a single event. A mechanical key press
 * is TWO events layered: the CLICK OF THE STEM, a bright noise transient of a few milliseconds with
 * no pitch of its own, and the THOCK OF THE BOTTOM-OUT, a low short body as the key meets the
 * plate. Both are below, layered with the body starting 4ms after the transient, and the whole
 * envelope is finished inside 58ms at its longest voice.
 *
 * THE INTERFACE HAS A VOICE RATHER THAN A BEEP. Three voices, chosen the way the reference's accent
 * family is chosen — one object, three jobs: a primary action is lower and fuller, a secondary
 * lighter and shorter, a toggle a touch brighter. Every press also carries a ±2.5% wobble, because
 * a sound repeated at exactly one frequency stops reading as a mechanism and starts reading as a
 * notification.
 *
 * THE PROPERTIES THIS FILE MUST KEEP, all of them checked by tests/interface-sound.test.mjs:
 *   - OFF by default. Nothing is armed by loading a page.
 *   - The AudioContext is constructed by a PRESS and never by load — the visitor's press on the
 *     toggle, or, when a previous visit already chose sound, that session's first press. Both are
 *     real user gestures, which is what browsers require; neither is page load.
 *   - Nothing autoplays.
 *   - The choice persists exactly the way the theme choice does, in localStorage under
 *     `apple-sound`, and is read back on the next page.
 *   - Every toggle states its state in aria-pressed and aria-label.
 *   - Never on hover, never on load, never more than once per press: ONE delegated listener owns
 *     both the toggle and the press, so a press on the toggle cannot produce two sounds.
 *
 * NO `document.currentScript`. Astro hoists a component <script> into a module script where
 * currentScript is null by specification; a hero effect shipped that way this morning and never ran
 * at all. Everything here is found with querySelector, and every one of those lookups tolerates a
 * null.
 * ===================================================================================== */
(function () {
  'use strict';

  var STORE_KEY = 'apple-sound';

  /* Everything that reads as a press. Buttons and links-as-buttons across both layouts: the
     landing's `.pill`, the chrome's `.iconbtn` and `.nav__cta`, anything with an explicit
     role, and `[data-sound-press]` for a control that is none of those. A bare prose link is
     deliberately absent — navigation is not a keystroke. */
  var PRESSABLE = [
    'button',
    '[role="button"]',
    'input[type="submit"]',
    'input[type="button"]',
    'summary',
    'a.pill',
    'a.btn',
    'a.cta',
    'a.button',
    'a.nav__cta',
    'a.nav__signin',
    'a[data-cta]',
    '[data-sound-press]'
  ].join(', ');

  /* THE THREE VOICES. clickHz is the band the stem transient sits in, bodyHz the pitch of the
     bottom-out. Gains are deliberately low: this is a texture under a finger, not an alert. */
  var VOICES = {
    primary:   { clickHz: 2400, clickQ: 0.9, clickGain: 0.034, clickDur: 0.010, bodyHz: 132, bodyGain: 0.075, bodyDur: 0.044 },
    secondary: { clickHz: 3200, clickQ: 1.1, clickGain: 0.026, clickDur: 0.008, bodyHz: 196, bodyGain: 0.048, bodyDur: 0.032 },
    toggle:    { clickHz: 4200, clickQ: 1.3, clickGain: 0.036, clickDur: 0.007, bodyHz: 240, bodyGain: 0.052, bodyDur: 0.030 }
  };

  var audio = null;       // constructed by a press, never by load
  var grain = null;       // the noise buffer, built once per context
  var armed = stored();   // the visitor's persisted choice; false on a first visit

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ preference */

  function stored() {
    try {
      return localStorage.getItem(STORE_KEY) === 'on';
    } catch (err) {
      return false; /* private mode — off, which is the default anyway */
    }
  }

  function remember(on) {
    try {
      localStorage.setItem(STORE_KEY, on ? 'on' : 'off');
    } catch (err) {
      /* private mode — the choice still applies for this page view */
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the synth */

  /** Construct the context. Called from the click handler and from nowhere else. */
  function ensureAudio() {
    if (audio) return audio;
    /* The prefixed name is Safari's, and it is still how an older iOS reaches this API. The cast
       is for the type checker only; there is no TypeScript in a file that ships as it is written. */
    var w = /** @type {any} */ (window);
    var Ctx = w.AudioContext || w.webkitAudioContext;
    if (!Ctx) return null;
    audio = new Ctx();
    return audio;
  }

  /** A short burst of decaying white noise, built once and re-triggered per press. */
  function noise(ac) {
    if (grain) return grain;
    var rate = ac.sampleRate || 44100;
    var len = Math.max(64, Math.floor(rate * 0.06));
    var buf = ac.createBuffer(1, len, rate);
    var data = buf.getChannelData(0);
    for (var i = 0; i < len; i++) {
      data[i] = (Math.random() * 2 - 1) * (1 - i / len);
    }
    grain = buf;
    return grain;
  }

  /**
   * ONE PRESS. Two layered events, under 60ms, at a low gain.
   * Silent unless armed, and silent unless a press has already built the context.
   */
  function press(kind) {
    if (!armed || !audio) return false;
    if (audio.state === 'suspended' && audio.resume) audio.resume();

    var v = VOICES[kind] || VOICES.secondary;
    var t = audio.currentTime;
    var wobble = 1 + (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.05;

    /* 1. THE CLICK OF THE STEM — filtered noise, no pitch, gone in a few milliseconds. */
    var src = audio.createBufferSource();
    src.buffer = noise(audio);
    var band = audio.createBiquadFilter();
    band.type = 'bandpass';
    band.frequency.setValueAtTime(v.clickHz * wobble, t);
    band.Q.value = v.clickQ;
    var clickGain = audio.createGain();
    clickGain.gain.setValueAtTime(v.clickGain, t);
    clickGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, t + v.clickDur);
    src.connect(band).connect(clickGain).connect(audio.destination);
    src.start(t);
    src.stop(t + v.clickDur + 0.004);

    /* 2. THE THOCK OF THE BOTTOM-OUT — a low body, pitched down as it dies. */
    var at = t + 0.004;
    var osc = audio.createOscillator();
    osc.type = 'triangle';
    osc.frequency.setValueAtTime(v.bodyHz * wobble, at);
    osc.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(v.bodyHz * 0.55, at + v.bodyDur);
    var bodyGain = audio.createGain();
    bodyGain.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, at);
    bodyGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(v.bodyGain, at + 0.003);
    bodyGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, at + v.bodyDur);
    osc.connect(bodyGain).connect(audio.destination);
    osc.start(at);
    osc.stop(at + v.bodyDur + 0.008);

    hit(v);
    return true;
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the toggles */

  function toggles() {
    return document.querySelectorAll('[data-sound-toggle]');
  }

  function paint() {
    var list = toggles();
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      list[i].setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(armed));
      list[i].setAttribute(
        'aria-label',
        armed ? 'Turn interface sound off' : 'Turn interface sound on'
      );
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the meter */

  /*
   * A CANVAS THAT SHOWS THE SOUND IT IS ABOUT TO MAKE. It is the toggle's own icon: a flat line
   * while sound is off, a live trace while it is on, and a kick on every press whose height is the
   * press's own body gain. It is entirely optional — a layout without one is silent about it and
   * every other line above still runs.
   *
   * IT IS THE ONLY AMBIENT MOTION THIS FILE OWNS, AND IT STOPS THREE WAYS: it never starts while
   * sound is off, it stops on prefers-reduced-motion, and it stops on visibilitychange. A
   * backgrounded tab must not burn a core for a line nobody is looking at.
   */
  var scope = null;
  var scopeCtx = null;
  var frame = 0;
  var energy = 0;
  var phase = 0;
  var reduced = window.matchMedia ? window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') : null;

  function findScope() {
    var el = document.querySelector('[data-sound-scope]');
    if (!el || !el.getContext) return;
    scope = el;
    scopeCtx = el.getContext('2d');
  }

  function stopped() {
    return !armed || document.hidden === true || !!(reduced && reduced.matches);
  }

  function paintScope() {
    if (!scope || !scopeCtx) return;
    var w = scope.width || 0;
    var h = scope.height || 0;
    if (!w || !h) return;
    var mid = h / 2;
    var ink = '';
    if (window.getComputedStyle) {
      ink = window.getComputedStyle(scope).getPropertyValue('color');
    }
    scopeCtx.clearRect(0, 0, w, h);
    scopeCtx.beginPath();
    for (var x = 0; x <= w; x += 2) {
      var k = x / w;
      var taper = Math.sin(Math.PI * k);
      var wave = Math.sin(k * 14 + phase) * 0.55 + Math.sin(k * 31 - phase * 1.7) * 0.45;
      var amp = (0.16 + energy * 0.84) * (mid - 1.5) * taper;
      var y = mid + wave * amp;
      if (x === 0) scopeCtx.moveTo(x, y);
      else scopeCtx.lineTo(x, y);
    }
    scopeCtx.strokeStyle = ink ? ink.trim() : 'currentColor';
    scopeCtx.lineWidth = 2;
    scopeCtx.stroke();
  }

  function tickScope() {
    if (stopped()) { frame = 0; paintScope(); return; }
    phase += 0.06;
    energy *= 0.9;
    if (energy < 0.004) energy = 0;
    paintScope();
    frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tickScope);
  }

  function runScope() {
    /* The CSS half of the same stop. Every ambient rule in InterfaceSound.astro is paused by this
       attribute, so prefers-reduced-motion, a hidden tab and "sound is off" all halt the keyframes
       as well as the canvas — one predicate, not two that can disagree. */
    var still = stopped();
    if (document.documentElement && document.documentElement.setAttribute) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-sound-still', still ? 'true' : 'false');
    }
    if (!scope) return;
    if (frame) { window.cancelAnimationFrame(frame); frame = 0; }
    if (still) { paintScope(); return; }
    frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tickScope);
  }

  /** The visible half of a press: the meter kicks, and the control flashes its ring. */
  function hit(v) {
    energy = Math.min(1, 0.55 + v.bodyGain * 6);
    runScope();
    var list = toggles();
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var el = list[i];
      if (!el.classList) continue;
      el.classList.remove('is-hit');
      /* Reading offsetWidth restarts a CSS animation that is already running; without it a second
         press inside the animation's own duration adds a class that is already there and nothing
         plays. */
      void el.offsetWidth;
      el.classList.add('is-hit');
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the dock's place */

  /*
   * A FLOATING CONTROL MUST NOT COVER A CONTROL, and this one did.
   *
   * MEASURED, on the built landing, at nine viewport sizes: at 740x360 and 667x375 — a phone held
   * sideways — the hero fills the screen, the corner the dock floats in lands ON the composer, and
   * 66x13 of the SEND BUTTON was underneath it. Both corners: moving it left is no fix, because the
   * composer spans the width. At 1440x900, 1280x620, 1280x480, 1024x700, 900x560, 800x560 and
   * 390x844 the corner is clear.
   *
   * A media query cannot express that boundary — 1280x480 is clear and 1024x540 is not, so it is
   * not a height rule or a width rule. The dock therefore MEASURES: if its own rectangle overlaps
   * any control, it stops floating and takes its place at the end of the page, where it cannot
   * steal a press. This is the same rule apps/web states as "decoration yields to the composer",
   * applied by the decoration rather than assumed by it.
   *
   * On load and on resize, never on scroll. The composer sits at the top of the page, so scrolling
   * carries it AWAY from a bottom corner; and a control that jumps around while the page scrolls is
   * worse than one that overlaps.
   */
  var CONTROLS = 'button, [role="button"], a[href], input, textarea, select, summary';

  function rectOf(el) {
    return el && el.getBoundingClientRect ? el.getBoundingClientRect() : null;
  }

  function placeDock() {
    var dock = document.querySelector('[data-sound-dock]');
    if (!dock || !dock.getBoundingClientRect || !dock.setAttribute) return;
    /* Measure the floating position, not the one it was last given. */
    if (dock.removeAttribute) dock.removeAttribute('data-flow');
    var d = rectOf(dock);
    if (!d || !d.width || !d.height) return;
    var list = document.querySelectorAll(CONTROLS);
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var el = list[i];
      if (el.closest && el.closest('[data-sound-dock]')) continue;
      var r = rectOf(el);
      if (!r || !r.width || !r.height) continue;
      if (r.left < d.right && r.right > d.left && r.top < d.bottom && r.bottom > d.top) {
        dock.setAttribute('data-flow', '');
        return;
      }
    }
  }

  var placing = 0;
  function schedulePlace() {
    if (placing) return;
    placing = window.requestAnimationFrame(function () { placing = 0; placeDock(); });
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the one listener */

  function voiceFor(el) {
    var explicit = el.getAttribute ? el.getAttribute('data-sound') : null;
    if (explicit === 'primary' || explicit === 'secondary' || explicit === 'toggle') return explicit;
    if (el.hasAttribute && (el.hasAttribute('aria-pressed') || el.hasAttribute('data-theme-toggle'))) {
      return 'toggle';
    }
    var name = el.className;
    if (name && typeof name !== 'string' && typeof name.baseVal === 'string') name = name.baseVal;
    var cls = ' ' + (typeof name === 'string' ? name : '') + ' ';
    if (/\bpill-quiet\b|\biconbtn\b|\bghost\b|\bquiet\b/.test(cls)) return 'secondary';
    if (/\bprimary\b|\bcta\b|\bpill\b/.test(cls)) return 'primary';
    if (el.getAttribute && el.getAttribute('type') === 'submit') return 'primary';
    return 'secondary';
  }

  /*
   * ONE LISTENER FOR BOTH JOBS, which is what makes "never more than once per press" structural
   * rather than a promise. The toggle is a button too: if arming were handled in one listener and
   * pressing in another, the press that arms the sound would make two sounds.
   */
  document.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
    var target = e.target;
    if (!target || !target.closest) return;

    var toggle = target.closest('[data-sound-toggle]');
    if (toggle) {
      armed = !armed;
      if (armed) {
        ensureAudio();
        if (audio && audio.resume) audio.resume();
      }
      remember(armed);
      paint();
      if (armed) press('toggle');
      runScope();
      return;
    }

    var control = target.closest(PRESSABLE);
    if (!control) return;
    if (control.getAttribute && control.getAttribute('data-sound') === 'none') return;
    if (control.hasAttribute && control.hasAttribute('disabled')) return;
    /* A choice carried over from a previous visit arms on this session's first press — still a
       gesture, still never at load. */
    if (armed && !audio) {
      ensureAudio();
      if (audio && audio.resume) audio.resume();
    }
    press(voiceFor(control));
  });

  document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', runScope);
  window.addEventListener('resize', schedulePlace);
  if (reduced) {
    if (reduced.addEventListener) reduced.addEventListener('change', runScope);
    else if (reduced.addListener) reduced.addListener(runScope);
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ boot */

  findScope();
  placeDock();
  paint();
  paintScope();
  runScope();

  /* The public surface. `appleTick` is the retired name and is kept aimed at the new synth, so
     anything that already called it gets a keyswitch instead of a chisel tick rather than an
     error. */
  window.appleSound = {
    press: press,
    isOn: function () { return armed; },
    voices: VOICES
  };
  window.appleTick = function () { return press('secondary'); };
})();

class="docs__main" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <p class="eyebrow" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>Docs</p> <h1 class="carved" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>Getting started</h1> <div class="prose" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>  <p>
Create your workspace, start a conversation, and check Studio availability before building.
</p> <div class="callout"><p><strong>Public Studio installation is unavailable.</strong> Steps 1–2 work now. Continue to the Studio steps only if you already have a working plugin. New users can chat, but must wait for an approved public plugin before Apple can change their place. <a href="/docs/plugin">See installation status</a>.</p></div><h2>1. Create an account</h2> <p>
Go to <a href="/app">the app</a> and sign up with an email address and a password. That is the
    whole form — no card, no phone number. You start with your full daily allowance of
<strong>231 Credits</strong> immediately.
</p> <h2>2. Create a project</h2> <p>
A <strong>project</strong> is Apple's workspace for one Roblox place: its chat history, its
    checkpoints, and its memory of what you have built together. Click
<strong>New project</strong>, give it a name (naming it after the place helps), and you land in
    the chat workspace.
</p> <p>
Projects are unlimited on the free tier, so make one per place rather than reusing a single
    project — the per-project memory works much better that way.
</p> <h2>3. Check Studio availability</h2> <p> There is no working public Creator Store installation path right now. If you do not already have the plugin, stop here and use the chat workspace. Check <a href="/docs/plugin">plugin status</a> for availability; the remaining steps describe connecting an existing working installation. </p> <h2>4. Connect it to your project</h2> <ol> <li>Open your place in Roblox Studio and click <strong>Apple</strong> in the Plugins tab.</li> <li>
In the Apple web workspace, open the project and press <strong>Enter pairing code</strong> in
      the <strong>Connect Roblox Studio</strong> block. You get a six-character code like
<code>K7M3QP</code>.
</li> <li>Type the code into the Apple panel in Studio and press <strong>Connect</strong>.</li> </ol> <p>
The workspace shows your place name and the panel turns green. Codes expire after 10 minutes; if
    yours does, generate another. More detail on <a href="/docs/connect">Connect a project</a>.
</p> <h2>5. Ask for your first build</h2> <p>Choose <strong>Apple</strong> for limited free use, or <strong>Apple MAX</strong> with an eligible paid subscription, and describe what you want:</p> <ul> <li>“make a lobby with a spinning obby door”</li> <li>“add a coin leaderboard that saves between sessions”</li> <li>“the kill brick in Workspace.Stage2 doesn't kill — fix it”</li> </ul> <p>
Watch the compact activity line and open details when needed. A chat response alone is not
    proof that your place changed: check the reported result, then test it in Studio.
</p> <h2>6. Iterate like you mean it</h2> <p>
The first result is a first draft. React to it the way you would with a collaborator: “make
    the door slower”, “the door should only open for players with the key”. Apple keeps the
    context of everything it has done in this project.
</p> <div class="callout"> <p> <strong>Safety net:</strong> every individual change is one native undo step
      (<kbd>Ctrl+Z</kbd> / <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> in Studio), so undoing a whole run means one press per
      step. Apple also checkpoints your place before every agent run, and restoring that checkpoint
      from the workspace sidebar takes the whole run back at once — even days later.
</p> </div> <h2>Where next</h2> <ul> <li><a href="/docs/modes">Models</a> — when to use Apple or Apple MAX.</li> <li><a href="/docs/credits-and-limits">Credits &amp; limits</a> — how far 231 Credits goes.</li> <li><a href="/docs/updating">Updating the plugin</a> — Roblox will not do it for you.</li> <li><a href="/docs/troubleshooting">Troubleshooting</a> — when the panel says something you didn't expect.</li> </ul>  </div> <footer class="docs__foot" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <p data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>
Stuck? Ask in the app, check your Credits before sending, or email
<a href="mailto:apple.labs.app@gmail.com" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>apple.labs.app@gmail.com</a>.
</p> </footer> </article> </div>  </main> <footer class="foot" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <div class="wrap" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <div class="foot__grid" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <div class="foot__brand" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <a href="/" class="brand" aria-label="Apple — home" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <svg width="26" height="26" viewBox="0 0 32 32" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true" class="gm " data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m> <path d="M5 24 12 5 19 14 27 8 21 27 13 18Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".1" data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m></path> <path d="m5 24 7-19 7 9 8-6-6 19-8-9-8 6Z" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linejoin="round" data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m></path> <path d="m12 5 1 13 6-4 2 13" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.2" data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m></path> </svg>  <span class="brand__word" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Apple</span> </a> <p class="foot__tag" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>It works inside the place you already have open.</p>  <p class="mono" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Apple Labs</p> </div> <nav aria-label="Product" class="foot__col" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <h2 data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Product</h2> <ul data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>  <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/docs/getting-started" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>How it works</a></li>  <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/proof" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Proof</a></li> <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/docs/modes" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Modes</a></li> <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/changelog" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Changelog</a></li> <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/pricing" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Pricing</a></li>  <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/status" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Status &amp; </p> </div> </div> </footer>   <script>/* =====================================================================================
 * INTERFACE SOUND — ONE IMPLEMENTATION, SHARED BY EVERY LAYOUT.
 *
 * This file is the whole sound system. Base.astro and Landing.astro both inline THIS TEXT
 * through layouts/InterfaceSound.astro, so there is one synth, one listener and one stored
 * preference for the entire site. Before this there was a copy in Base.astro and nothing at all
 * on the front page, which is two states that cannot agree and one page with no control.
 *
 * WHAT THE OWNER ASKED FOR. He played with rosebud.ai and singled out one thing: pressing a button
 * makes a satisfying mechanical keyboard click. Measured on that page the same day (recorded in
 * packages/corpus/data/ui-references/web-landing.json, claim 16): its resource timing list contains
 * no mp3, wav, ogg, m4a or webm anywhere, while AudioContext is available — so their click is
 * SYNTHESISED at interaction time, not downloaded. That is the cheaper technique and the one used
 * here. A synthesised click costs no bytes, has no load state, and cannot be the reason a button
 * feels late.
 *
 * WHAT A KEYSWITCH ACTUALLY SOUNDS LIKE, and why the old `tick()` did not. The retired version was
 * one triangle oscillator sliding down — a soft chisel tick, a single event. A mechanical key press
 * is TWO events layered: the CLICK OF THE STEM, a bright noise transient of a few milliseconds with
 * no pitch of its own, and the THOCK OF THE BOTTOM-OUT, a low short body as the key meets the
 * plate. Both are below, layered with the body starting 4ms after the transient, and the whole
 * envelope is finished inside 58ms at its longest voice.
 *
 * THE INTERFACE HAS A VOICE RATHER THAN A BEEP. Three voices, chosen the way the reference's accent
 * family is chosen — one object, three jobs: a primary action is lower and fuller, a secondary
 * lighter and shorter, a toggle a touch brighter. Every press also carries a ±2.5% wobble, because
 * a sound repeated at exactly one frequency stops reading as a mechanism and starts reading as a
 * notification.
 *
 * THE PROPERTIES THIS FILE MUST KEEP, all of them checked by tests/interface-sound.test.mjs:
 *   - OFF by default. Nothing is armed by loading a page.
 *   - The AudioContext is constructed by a PRESS and never by load — the visitor's press on the
 *     toggle, or, when a previous visit already chose sound, that session's first press. Both are
 *     real user gestures, which is what browsers require; neither is page load.
 *   - Nothing autoplays.
 *   - The choice persists exactly the way the theme choice does, in localStorage under
 *     `apple-sound`, and is read back on the next page.
 *   - Every toggle states its state in aria-pressed and aria-label.
 *   - Never on hover, never on load, never more than once per press: ONE delegated listener owns
 *     both the toggle and the press, so a press on the toggle cannot produce two sounds.
 *
 * NO `document.currentScript`. Astro hoists a component <script> into a module script where
 * currentScript is null by specification; a hero effect shipped that way this morning and never ran
 * at all. Everything here is found with querySelector, and every one of those lookups tolerates a
 * null.
 * ===================================================================================== */
(function () {
  'use strict';

  var STORE_KEY = 'apple-sound';

  /* Everything that reads as a press. Buttons and links-as-buttons across both layouts: the
     landing's `.pill`, the chrome's `.iconbtn` and `.nav__cta`, anything with an explicit
     role, and `[data-sound-press]` for a control that is none of those. A bare prose link is
     deliberately absent — navigation is not a keystroke. */
  var PRESSABLE = [
    'button',
    '[role="button"]',
    'input[type="submit"]',
    'input[type="button"]',
    'summary',
    'a.pill',
    'a.btn',
    'a.cta',
    'a.button',
    'a.nav__cta',
    'a.nav__signin',
    'a[data-cta]',
    '[data-sound-press]'
  ].join(', ');

  /* THE THREE VOICES. clickHz is the band the stem transient sits in, bodyHz the pitch of the
     bottom-out. Gains are deliberately low: this is a texture under a finger, not an alert. */
  var VOICES = {
    primary:   { clickHz: 2400, clickQ: 0.9, clickGain: 0.034, clickDur: 0.010, bodyHz: 132, bodyGain: 0.075, bodyDur: 0.044 },
    secondary: { clickHz: 3200, clickQ: 1.1, clickGain: 0.026, clickDur: 0.008, bodyHz: 196, bodyGain: 0.048, bodyDur: 0.032 },
    toggle:    { clickHz: 4200, clickQ: 1.3, clickGain: 0.036, clickDur: 0.007, bodyHz: 240, bodyGain: 0.052, bodyDur: 0.030 }
  };

  var audio = null;       // constructed by a press, never by load
  var grain = null;       // the noise buffer, built once per context
  var armed = stored();   // the visitor's persisted choice; false on a first visit

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ preference */

  function stored() {
    try {
      return localStorage.getItem(STORE_KEY) === 'on';
    } catch (err) {
      return false; /* private mode — off, which is the default anyway */
    }
  }

  function remember(on) {
    try {
      localStorage.setItem(STORE_KEY, on ? 'on' : 'off');
    } catch (err) {
      /* private mode — the choice still applies for this page view */
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the synth */

  /** Construct the context. Called from the click handler and from nowhere else. */
  function ensureAudio() {
    if (audio) return audio;
    /* The prefixed name is Safari's, and it is still how an older iOS reaches this API. The cast
       is for the type checker only; there is no TypeScript in a file that ships as it is written. */
    var w = /** @type {any} */ (window);
    var Ctx = w.AudioContext || w.webkitAudioContext;
    if (!Ctx) return null;
    audio = new Ctx();
    return audio;
  }

  /** A short burst of decaying white noise, built once and re-triggered per press. */
  function noise(ac) {
    if (grain) return grain;
    var rate = ac.sampleRate || 44100;
    var len = Math.max(64, Math.floor(rate * 0.06));
    var buf = ac.createBuffer(1, len, rate);
    var data = buf.getChannelData(0);
    for (var i = 0; i < len; i++) {
      data[i] = (Math.random() * 2 - 1) * (1 - i / len);
    }
    grain = buf;
    return grain;
  }

  /**
   * ONE PRESS. Two layered events, under 60ms, at a low gain.
   * Silent unless armed, and silent unless a press has already built the context.
   */
  function press(kind) {
    if (!armed || !audio) return false;
    if (audio.state === 'suspended' && audio.resume) audio.resume();

    var v = VOICES[kind] || VOICES.secondary;
    var t = audio.currentTime;
    var wobble = 1 + (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.05;

    /* 1. THE CLICK OF THE STEM — filtered noise, no pitch, gone in a few milliseconds. */
    var src = audio.createBufferSource();
    src.buffer = noise(audio);
    var band = audio.createBiquadFilter();
    band.type = 'bandpass';
    band.frequency.setValueAtTime(v.clickHz * wobble, t);
    band.Q.value = v.clickQ;
    var clickGain = audio.createGain();
    clickGain.gain.setValueAtTime(v.clickGain, t);
    clickGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, t + v.clickDur);
    src.connect(band).connect(clickGain).connect(audio.destination);
    src.start(t);
    src.stop(t + v.clickDur + 0.004);

    /* 2. THE THOCK OF THE BOTTOM-OUT — a low body, pitched down as it dies. */
    var at = t + 0.004;
    var osc = audio.createOscillator();
    osc.type = 'triangle';
    osc.frequency.setValueAtTime(v.bodyHz * wobble, at);
    osc.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(v.bodyHz * 0.55, at + v.bodyDur);
    var bodyGain = audio.createGain();
    bodyGain.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, at);
    bodyGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(v.bodyGain, at + 0.003);
    bodyGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, at + v.bodyDur);
    osc.connect(bodyGain).connect(audio.destination);
    osc.start(at);
    osc.stop(at + v.bodyDur + 0.008);

    hit(v);
    return true;
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the toggles */

  function toggles() {
    return document.querySelectorAll('[data-sound-toggle]');
  }

  function paint() {
    var list = toggles();
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      list[i].setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(armed));
      list[i].setAttribute(
        'aria-label',
        armed ? 'Turn interface sound off' : 'Turn interface sound on'
      );
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the meter */

  /*
   * A CANVAS THAT SHOWS THE SOUND IT IS ABOUT TO MAKE. It is the toggle's own icon: a flat line
   * while sound is off, a live trace while it is on, and a kick on every press whose height is the
   * press's own body gain. It is entirely optional — a layout without one is silent about it and
   * every other line above still runs.
   *
   * IT IS THE ONLY AMBIENT MOTION THIS FILE OWNS, AND IT STOPS THREE WAYS: it never starts while
   * sound is off, it stops on prefers-reduced-motion, and it stops on visibilitychange. A
   * backgrounded tab must not burn a core for a line nobody is looking at.
   */
  var scope = null;
  var scopeCtx = null;
  var frame = 0;
  var energy = 0;
  var phase = 0;
  var reduced = window.matchMedia ? window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') : null;

  function findScope() {
    var el = document.querySelector('[data-sound-scope]');
    if (!el || !el.getContext) return;
    scope = el;
    scopeCtx = el.getContext('2d');
  }

  function stopped() {
    return !armed || document.hidden === true || !!(reduced && reduced.matches);
  }

  function paintScope() {
    if (!scope || !scopeCtx) return;
    var w = scope.width || 0;
    var h = scope.height || 0;
    if (!w || !h) return;
    var mid = h / 2;
    var ink = '';
    if (window.getComputedStyle) {
      ink = window.getComputedStyle(scope).getPropertyValue('color');
    }
    scopeCtx.clearRect(0, 0, w, h);
    scopeCtx.beginPath();
    for (var x = 0; x <= w; x += 2) {
      var k = x / w;
      var taper = Math.sin(Math.PI * k);
      var wave = Math.sin(k * 14 + phase) * 0.55 + Math.sin(k * 31 - phase * 1.7) * 0.45;
      var amp = (0.16 + energy * 0.84) * (mid - 1.5) * taper;
      var y = mid + wave * amp;
      if (x === 0) scopeCtx.moveTo(x, y);
      else scopeCtx.lineTo(x, y);
    }
    scopeCtx.strokeStyle = ink ? ink.trim() : 'currentColor';
    scopeCtx.lineWidth = 2;
    scopeCtx.stroke();
  }

  function tickScope() {
    if (stopped()) { frame = 0; paintScope(); return; }
    phase += 0.06;
    energy *= 0.9;
    if (energy < 0.004) energy = 0;
    paintScope();
    frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tickScope);
  }

  function runScope() {
    /* The CSS half of the same stop. Every ambient rule in InterfaceSound.astro is paused by this
       attribute, so prefers-reduced-motion, a hidden tab and "sound is off" all halt the keyframes
       as well as the canvas — one predicate, not two that can disagree. */
    var still = stopped();
    if (document.documentElement && document.documentElement.setAttribute) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-sound-still', still ? 'true' : 'false');
    }
    if (!scope) return;
    if (frame) { window.cancelAnimationFrame(frame); frame = 0; }
    if (still) { paintScope(); return; }
    frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tickScope);
  }

  /** The visible half of a press: the meter kicks, and the control flashes its ring. */
  function hit(v) {
    energy = Math.min(1, 0.55 + v.bodyGain * 6);
    runScope();
    var list = toggles();
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var el = list[i];
      if (!el.classList) continue;
      el.classList.remove('is-hit');
      /* Reading offsetWidth restarts a CSS animation that is already running; without it a second
         press inside the animation's own duration adds a class that is already there and nothing
         plays. */
      void el.offsetWidth;
      el.classList.add('is-hit');
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the dock's place */

  /*
   * A FLOATING CONTROL MUST NOT COVER A CONTROL, and this one did.
   *
   * MEASURED, on the built landing, at nine viewport sizes: at 740x360 and 667x375 — a phone held
   * sideways — the hero fills the screen, the corner the dock floats in lands ON the composer, and
   * 66x13 of the SEND BUTTON was underneath it. Both corners: moving it left is no fix, because the
   * composer spans the width. At 1440x900, 1280x620, 1280x480, 1024x700, 900x560, 800x560 and
   * 390x844 the corner is clear.
   *
   * A media query cannot express that boundary — 1280x480 is clear and 1024x540 is not, so it is
   * not a height rule or a width rule. The dock therefore MEASURES: if its own rectangle overlaps
   * any control, it stops floating and takes its place at the end of the page, where it cannot
   * steal a press. This is the same rule apps/web states as "decoration yields to the composer",
   * applied by the decoration rather than assumed by it.
   *
   * On load and on resize, never on scroll. The composer sits at the top of the page, so scrolling
   * carries it AWAY from a bottom corner; and a control that jumps around while the page scrolls is
   * worse than one that overlaps.
   */
  var CONTROLS = 'button, [role="button"], a[href], input, textarea, select, summary';

  function rectOf(el) {
    return el && el.getBoundingClientRect ? el.getBoundingClientRect() : null;
  }

  function placeDock() {
    var dock = document.querySelector('[data-sound-dock]');
    if (!dock || !dock.getBoundingClientRect || !dock.setAttribute) return;
    /* Measure the floating position, not the one it was last given. */
    if (dock.removeAttribute) dock.removeAttribute('data-flow');
    var d = rectOf(dock);
    if (!d || !d.width || !d.height) return;
    var list = document.querySelectorAll(CONTROLS);
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var el = list[i];
      if (el.closest && el.closest('[data-sound-dock]')) continue;
      var r = rectOf(el);
      if (!r || !r.width || !r.height) continue;
      if (r.left < d.right && r.right > d.left && r.top < d.bottom && r.bottom > d.top) {
        dock.setAttribute('data-flow', '');
        return;
      }
    }
  }

  var placing = 0;
  function schedulePlace() {
    if (placing) return;
    placing = window.requestAnimationFrame(function () { placing = 0; placeDock(); });
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the one listener */

  function voiceFor(el) {
    var explicit = el.getAttribute ? el.getAttribute('data-sound') : null;
    if (explicit === 'primary' || explicit === 'secondary' || explicit === 'toggle') return explicit;
    if (el.hasAttribute && (el.hasAttribute('aria-pressed') || el.hasAttribute('data-theme-toggle'))) {
      return 'toggle';
    }
    var name = el.className;
    if (name && typeof name !== 'string' && typeof name.baseVal === 'string') name = name.baseVal;
    var cls = ' ' + (typeof name === 'string' ? name : '') + ' ';
    if (/\bpill-quiet\b|\biconbtn\b|\bghost\b|\bquiet\b/.test(cls)) return 'secondary';
    if (/\bprimary\b|\bcta\b|\bpill\b/.test(cls)) return 'primary';
    if (el.getAttribute && el.getAttribute('type') === 'submit') return 'primary';
    return 'secondary';
  }

  /*
   * ONE LISTENER FOR BOTH JOBS, which is what makes "never more than once per press" structural
   * rather than a promise. The toggle is a button too: if arming were handled in one listener and
   * pressing in another, the press that arms the sound would make two sounds.
   */
  document.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
    var target = e.target;
    if (!target || !target.closest) return;

    var toggle = target.closest('[data-sound-toggle]');
    if (toggle) {
      armed = !armed;
      if (armed) {
        ensureAudio();
        if (audio && audio.resume) audio.resume();
      }
      remember(armed);
      paint();
      if (armed) press('toggle');
      runScope();
      return;
    }

    var control = target.closest(PRESSABLE);
    if (!control) return;
    if (control.getAttribute && control.getAttribute('data-sound') === 'none') return;
    if (control.hasAttribute && control.hasAttribute('disabled')) return;
    /* A choice carried over from a previous visit arms on this session's first press — still a
       gesture, still never at load. */
    if (armed && !audio) {
      ensureAudio();
      if (audio && audio.resume) audio.resume();
    }
    press(voiceFor(control));
  });

  document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', runScope);
  window.addEventListener('resize', schedulePlace);
  if (reduced) {
    if (reduced.addEventListener) reduced.addEventListener('change', runScope);
    else if (reduced.addListener) reduced.addListener(runScope);
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ boot */

  findScope();
  placeDock();
  paint();
  paintScope();
  runScope();

  /* The public surface. `appleTick` is the retired name and is kept aimed at the new synth, so
     anything that already called it gets a keyswitch instead of a chisel tick rather than an
     error. */
  window.appleSound = {
    press: press,
    isOn: function () { return armed; },
    voices: VOICES
  };
  window.appleTick = function () { return press('secondary'); };
})();

data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> Troubleshooting </a> </li> </ul> </div><div class="docs__group" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <p class="docs__grouplabel mono" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>Trust</p> <ul data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <li data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <a href="/docs/privacy-and-data" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> Privacy &amp; data </a> </li><li data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <a href="/docs/faq" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> FAQ </a> </li> </ul> </div><div class="docs__group" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <p class="docs__grouplabel mono" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>Developer</p> <ul data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <li data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <a href="/docs/build-from-source" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> Build from source </a> </li> </ul> </div> </nav> </details> </aside> <article class="docs__main" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <p class="eyebrow" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>Docs</p> <h1 class="carved" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>Apple and Apple MAX</h1> <div class="prose" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>  <p>The selector beside the message box chooses a product model, not a planning mode.</p> <section> <h2>Apple</h2>  <p>Apple is the limited free model. It can answer questions and use building tools when Studio is connected and changes are allowed. It is not a read-only Plan mode. The Free plan includes 231 Credits per day, subject to its monthly allowance. It works in short bursts: <strong>one request runs at most three steps</strong>, then stops and says so with everything it did saved — send another message and it picks up where it left off. A build that needs more than three steps is not refused; it takes more than one message.</p> </section><section> <h2>Apple MAX</h2>  <p>Apple MAX is available to eligible paid subscribers and carries a longer chain of steps in a single request, so an involved build can finish without being handed back to you partway. Choosing it on a free account shows an availability notice and keeps your draft; it does not switch your model or charge you. See <a href="/app/usage">Usage and plan availability</a>.</p> </section><h2>Availability</h2> <p>Paid checkout is not open in the current preview. Check <a href="/app/usage">Usage and plan availability</a> before expecting access to MAX. Extra purchased Credits do not by themselves grant a paid subscription.</p> <h2>What changes in Studio</h2> <p>Model access and edit permission are separate. Neither choice bypasses Studio pairing, change approval, quota, or tool safety checks. Without a connected plugin, a chat response is not a change to your place. Public plugin installation is currently unavailable. See <a href="/docs/plugin">installation status</a>.</p> <h2>How Credits work</h2> <p>There is no guaranteed fixed charge per message. Actual usage and the plan limits determine the charge. See <a href="/docs/credits-and-limits">Credits and limits</a>; review the result in Studio before treating a build as complete.</p> <h2>Training status</h2> <p>Apple and Apple MAX are separate product choices with different access and working limits. They currently run on the same third-party foundation model — neither is a model we trained — so what Apple MAX buys is a longer chain of steps in one request and a larger allowance, not a different or larger model. Custom Roblox training is in development; a completed independently trained frontier model is not available.</p>  </div> <footer class="docs__foot" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <p data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>
