data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>Docs</p> <h1 class="carved" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>Troubleshooting</h1> <div class="prose" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>  <p>
Grouped by what you can actually see. If the panel is showing you a message, start with
<a href="#messages">what the panel says</a>.
</p> <h2 id="messages">What the panel says</h2> <h3>“Invalid or expired pairing code”</h3> <p>
Codes last 10 minutes and work once. Generate a fresh one in the web workspace
    (<a href="/docs/connect">Connect a project</a>) and type it in promptly. Case and dashes do not
    matter, so mistyping those is not the cause — a stale code almost always is.
</p> <h3>“Could not reach Apple — check Studio’s network permission”</h3> <p>
The plugin's HTTPS request never landed. In order of likelihood:
</p> <ul> <li> <strong>Studio's permission prompt was declined.</strong> Roblox asks once, per plugin, per
      web address. Re-allow it in Studio's <strong>Plugin Management</strong> window, where these
      permissions can be accepted, denied and revoked.
</li> <li><strong>The network blocks it.</strong> School and workplace networks often block outbound HTTPS from Studio. Another network settles it in a minute.</li> <li><strong>Apple is actually down.</strong> The <a href="/status">status page</a> checks the live API from your own browser and answers that in a second.</li> </ul> <h3>“Session ended — reconnect with a new code”</h3> <p>
A Studio connection is good for 30 days, then it expires by design.
<a href="/docs/connect">Connect again</a>; nothing in the project is lost.
</p> <h3>“This Apple build is too old for the server”</h3> <p>
Shown in red, and it does block builds. Update the plugin —
<a href="/docs/updating">Updating the plugin</a> has the two-click version. This is rare by
    design: Apple admits every plugin build whose wire protocol it still supports, and today it
    supports all of them, so you should not see this yet.
</p> <h3>An amber line about a newer version</h3> <p>
Advisory only. A newer Apple has been published and you are still on an older one — everything
    keeps working. Update when convenient. It is written to Studio's Output window once, not
    repeatedly.
</p> <h3>“Connection hiccup — retrying…”</h3> <p>
One request failed and the plugin is already retrying. It clears itself. If it never clears,
    treat it as “Could not reach Apple” above.
</p> <h2>The Apple button isn't in the Plugins tab</h2> <ul> <li>
Acquiring the plugin on the web only puts it in your inventory. The install happens inside
      Studio, in the <strong>Toolbox</strong> — see <a href="/docs/plugin">Install</a>.
</li> <li>Check Studio's plugin management window: if Apple is listed but disabled, enable it.</li> <li>Restart Studio once. Plugins are loaded at launch.</li> </ul> <h2>The panel says Connected, the web app says it isn't</h2> <ul> <li> <strong>A connection belongs to one Studio window.</strong> If you opened a second window or
      a different place, that one is not connected — connect it too.
</li> <li> <strong>Check you are looking at the same project.</strong> The panel names the project it is
      connected to, right next to <strong>Connected</strong>. If that is not the project open in
      your browser, that is the whole answer.
</li> </ul> <h2>Apple stopped mid-build</h2> <ul> <li> <strong>Studio was closed or the place was switched.</strong> Apple loses its hands and pauses
      with a message. Reopen the place, reconnect if needed, and ask it to continue — the plan and
      history are still in the project.
</li> <li> <strong>Very large places are slow to read.</strong> The first tree read in a session can take
      noticeably longer than the rest. Give it a moment before retrying.
</li> <li> <strong>Credits ran out.</strong> The chat says so explicitly. See
<a href="/docs/credits-and-limits">Credits &amp; limits</a>.
</li> </ul> <h2 id="model-failures">The model failed part-way</h2> <p>
Three different things are meant by “it stopped on its own”, and they need different responses.
    The chat says which one happened; this is what each means, and what it costs. One rule covers
    all three: a run that ends this way having left you nothing to keep has its Credits put back
    automatically, and the reply tells you how many.
</p> <h3>“The model dropped that step”</h3> <p>
A single inference call failed after Apple had already done real work. Everything up to that
    step is saved in your place, and the dropped step is <strong>not</strong> charged — Credits are
    billed from the compute a call actually reports, and a call that returned nothing reports
    nothing. Send another message and Apple continues from where it stopped; you do not need to
    repeat the whole instruction.
</p> <h3>“Apple is busy” or “too many requests”</h3> <p>
The model provider rate-limited us, not you. Nothing about your account changed and your
    allowance is untouched. Wait a few seconds and continue — this clears on its own, and it clears
    faster than retrying immediately, which joins the same queue.
</p> <h3>“Apple has reached today's shared building capacity”</h3> <p>
Different from running out of your own Credits: this is a ceiling on what the whole service will
    spend in a day, and it protects the free tier from a single runaway build. The message says when
    it resets — midnight UTC, the same instant for everyone. The step that stops here is not
    charged, because the capacity check happens before the call runs and a call that never ran
    reports no compute. What the steps that did finish cost depends on what they left you: if the
    run changed nothing in your place, every Credit it used is put back automatically and the reply
    says how many; if it had already built something, those Credits stay spent, because the work is
    still there. Either way the total is on the message, and your project and
    checkpoints are exactly where you left them. See
<a href="/docs/credits-and-limits">Credits &amp; limits</a> for the difference between the two.
</p> <div class="callout"> <p>
In all three cases the work already done is in your place and the conversation is intact.
      Apple never rolls back finished steps because a later one failed — that is what the checkpoint
      before the run is for, and it is still there if you want it.
</p> </div> <h2 id="roblox-key-refused">“Roblox is refusing this key”</h2> <p>
This is about the Open Cloud key you connected under
<strong>Settings → Connections</strong>, not about your Apple account. Roblox expires API keys,
    and a key can be deleted from create.roblox.com at any time — neither of those tells Apple, so
    the first sign is usually an upload that fails.
</p> <ol> <li>Press <strong>Test connection</strong> in Settings → Connections. It says which of the three it is: accepted, refused, or not checkable right now.</li> <li>If it was refused, make a new key at create.roblox.com → <strong>Open Cloud</strong> → <strong>API Keys</strong>, tick the same permissions, and paste it in. It replaces the old one.</li> <li>Nothing already built is affected, and nothing in your Roblox account changes. Assets Apple created stay where they are.</li> </ol> <p>
If the answer is neither — “Apple could not reach Roblox”, or a 403 — the check did not happen.
    That is not a verdict on the key, and making a new one will not help.
</p> <h2>Apple changed something I didn't want</h2> <p>Three exits, smallest first:</p> <ol>  <li>Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd> (<kbd>⌘Z</kbd> on macOS) in Studio. Each change Apple made is its own undo step, so a run of several steps needs one press per step.</li> <li>Restore the checkpoint Apple took before the run, from the project's sidebar. That takes the whole run back in one action, which <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd> cannot do.</li> <li>Say what is wrong in the chat. Fixing a wrong turn is usually faster than rolling back.</li> </ol> <h2>Stop Apple now</h2> <p>
Press <strong>Disconnect</strong> in the plugin panel, or disconnect from the web workspace.
    Either one ends Apple's access to the place immediately, without uninstalling anything. To
    remove the plugin entirely, uninstall it from Studio's plugin management window.
</p> <div class="callout"> <p>
Before writing in, check <a href="/status">Status</a> — it lists what is currently known to be
      broken or limited, with the workaround for each, and it says when the API last answered.
</p> </div> <div class="callout"> <p>
Still stuck? Email <a href="mailto:apple.labs.app@gmail.com">apple.labs.app@gmail.com</a> with
      the project name, roughly when it happened, and what the panel said. A human reads it.
</p> </div>  </div> <footer class="docs__foot" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <p data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>
Stuck? Ask in the app, check your Credits before sending, or email
<a href="mailto:apple.labs.app@gmail.com" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>apple.labs.app@gmail.com</a>.
</p> </footer> </article> </div>  </main> <footer class="foot" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <div class="wrap" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <div class="foot__grid" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <div class="foot__brand" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <a href="/" class="brand" aria-label="Apple — home" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <svg width="26" height="26" viewBox="0 0 32 32" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true" class="gm " data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m> <path d="M5 24 12 5 19 14 27 8 21 27 13 18Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".1" data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m></path> <path d="m5 24 7-19 7 9 8-6-6 19-8-9-8 6Z" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linejoin="round" data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m></path> <path d="m12 5 1 13 6-4 2 13" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.2" data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m></path> </svg>  <span class="brand__word" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Apple</span> </a> <p class="foot__tag" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>It works inside the place you already have open.</p>  <p class="mono" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Apple Labs</p> </div> <nav aria-label="Product" class="foot__col" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <h2 data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Product</h2> <ul data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>  <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/docs/getting-started" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>How it works</a></li>  <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/proof" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Proof</a></li> <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/docs/modes" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Modes</a></li> <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/changelog" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Changelog</a></li> <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/pricing" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Pricing</a></li>  <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/status" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Status &amp;  * INTERFACE SOUND — ONE IMPLEMENTATION, SHARED BY EVERY LAYOUT.
 *
 * This file is the whole sound system. Base.astro and Landing.astro both inline THIS TEXT
 * through layouts/InterfaceSound.astro, so there is one synth, one listener and one stored
 * preference for the entire site. Before this there was a copy in Base.astro and nothing at all
 * on the front page, which is two states that cannot agree and one page with no control.
 *
 * WHAT THE OWNER ASKED FOR. He played with rosebud.ai and singled out one thing: pressing a button
 * makes a satisfying mechanical keyboard click. Measured on that page the same day (recorded in
 * packages/corpus/data/ui-references/web-landing.json, claim 16): its resource timing list contains
 * no mp3, wav, ogg, m4a or webm anywhere, while AudioContext is available — so their click is
 * SYNTHESISED at interaction time, not downloaded. That is the cheaper technique and the one used
 * here. A synthesised click costs no bytes, has no load state, and cannot be the reason a button
 * feels late.
 *
 * WHAT A KEYSWITCH ACTUALLY SOUNDS LIKE, and why the old `tick()` did not. The retired version was
 * one triangle oscillator sliding down — a soft chisel tick, a single event. A mechanical key press
 * is TWO events layered: the CLICK OF THE STEM, a bright noise transient of a few milliseconds with
 * no pitch of its own, and the THOCK OF THE BOTTOM-OUT, a low short body as the key meets the
 * plate. Both are below, layered with the body starting 4ms after the transient, and the whole
 * envelope is finished inside 58ms at its longest voice.
 *
 * THE INTERFACE HAS A VOICE RATHER THAN A BEEP. Three voices, chosen the way the reference's accent
 * family is chosen — one object, three jobs: a primary action is lower and fuller, a secondary
 * lighter and shorter, a toggle a touch brighter. Every press also carries a ±2.5% wobble, because
 * a sound repeated at exactly one frequency stops reading as a mechanism and starts reading as a
 * notification.
 *
 * THE PROPERTIES THIS FILE MUST KEEP, all of them checked by tests/interface-sound.test.mjs:
 *   - OFF by default. Nothing is armed by loading a page.
 *   - The AudioContext is constructed by a PRESS and never by load — the visitor's press on the
 *     toggle, or, when a previous visit already chose sound, that session's first press. Both are
 *     real user gestures, which is what browsers require; neither is page load.
 *   - Nothing autoplays.
 *   - The choice persists exactly the way the theme choice does, in localStorage under
 *     `apple-sound`, and is read back on the next page.
 *   - Every toggle states its state in aria-pressed and aria-label.
 *   - Never on hover, never on load, never more than once per press: ONE delegated listener owns
 *     both the toggle and the press, so a press on the toggle cannot produce two sounds.
 *
 * NO `document.currentScript`. Astro hoists a component <script> into a module script where
 * currentScript is null by specification; a hero effect shipped that way this morning and never ran
 * at all. Everything here is found with querySelector, and every one of those lookups tolerates a
 * null.
 * ===================================================================================== */
(function () {
  'use strict';

  var STORE_KEY = 'apple-sound';

  /* Everything that reads as a press. Buttons and links-as-buttons across both layouts: the
     landing's `.pill`, the chrome's `.iconbtn` and `.nav__cta`, anything with an explicit
     role, and `[data-sound-press]` for a control that is none of those. A bare prose link is
     deliberately absent — navigation is not a keystroke. */
  var PRESSABLE = [
    'button',
    '[role="button"]',
    'input[type="submit"]',
    'input[type="button"]',
    'summary',
    'a.pill',
    'a.btn',
    'a.cta',
    'a.button',
    'a.nav__cta',
    'a.nav__signin',
    'a[data-cta]',
    '[data-sound-press]'
  ].join(', ');

  /* THE THREE VOICES. clickHz is the band the stem transient sits in, bodyHz the pitch of the
     bottom-out. Gains are deliberately low: this is a texture under a finger, not an alert. */
  var VOICES = {
    primary:   { clickHz: 2400, clickQ: 0.9, clickGain: 0.034, clickDur: 0.010, bodyHz: 132, bodyGain: 0.075, bodyDur: 0.044 },
    secondary: { clickHz: 3200, clickQ: 1.1, clickGain: 0.026, clickDur: 0.008, bodyHz: 196, bodyGain: 0.048, bodyDur: 0.032 },
    toggle:    { clickHz: 4200, clickQ: 1.3, clickGain: 0.036, clickDur: 0.007, bodyHz: 240, bodyGain: 0.052, bodyDur: 0.030 }
  };

  var audio = null;       // constructed by a press, never by load
  var grain = null;       // the noise buffer, built once per context
  var armed = stored();   // the visitor's persisted choice; false on a first visit

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ preference */

  function stored() {
    try {
      return localStorage.getItem(STORE_KEY) === 'on';
    } catch (err) {
      return false; /* private mode — off, which is the default anyway */
    }
  }

  function remember(on) {
    try {
      localStorage.setItem(STORE_KEY, on ? 'on' : 'off');
    } catch (err) {
      /* private mode — the choice still applies for this page view */
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the synth */

  /** Construct the context. Called from the click handler and from nowhere else. */
  function ensureAudio() {
    if (audio) return audio;
    /* The prefixed name is Safari's, and it is still how an older iOS reaches this API. The cast
       is for the type checker only; there is no TypeScript in a file that ships as it is written. */
    var w = /** @type {any} */ (window);
    var Ctx = w.AudioContext || w.webkitAudioContext;
    if (!Ctx) return null;
    audio = new Ctx();
    return audio;
  }

  /** A short burst of decaying white noise, built once and re-triggered per press. */
  function noise(ac) {
    if (grain) return grain;
    var rate = ac.sampleRate || 44100;
    var len = Math.max(64, Math.floor(rate * 0.06));
    var buf = ac.createBuffer(1, len, rate);
    var data = buf.getChannelData(0);
    for (var i = 0; i < len; i++) {
      data[i] = (Math.random() * 2 - 1) * (1 - i / len);
    }
    grain = buf;
    return grain;
  }

  /**
   * ONE PRESS. Two layered events, under 60ms, at a low gain.
   * Silent unless armed, and silent unless a press has already built the context.
   */
  function press(kind) {
    if (!armed || !audio) return false;
    if (audio.state === 'suspended' && audio.resume) audio.resume();

    var v = VOICES[kind] || VOICES.secondary;
    var t = audio.currentTime;
    var wobble = 1 + (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.05;

    /* 1. THE CLICK OF THE STEM — filtered noise, no pitch, gone in a few milliseconds. */
    var src = audio.createBufferSource();
    src.buffer = noise(audio);
    var band = audio.createBiquadFilter();
    band.type = 'bandpass';
    band.frequency.setValueAtTime(v.clickHz * wobble, t);
    band.Q.value = v.clickQ;
    var clickGain = audio.createGain();
    clickGain.gain.setValueAtTime(v.clickGain, t);
    clickGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, t + v.clickDur);
    src.connect(band).connect(clickGain).connect(audio.destination);
    src.start(t);
    src.stop(t + v.clickDur + 0.004);

    /* 2. THE THOCK OF THE BOTTOM-OUT — a low body, pitched down as it dies. */
    var at = t + 0.004;
    var osc = audio.createOscillator();
    osc.type = 'triangle';
    osc.frequency.setValueAtTime(v.bodyHz * wobble, at);
    osc.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(v.bodyHz * 0.55, at + v.bodyDur);
    var bodyGain = audio.createGain();
    bodyGain.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, at);
    bodyGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(v.bodyGain, at + 0.003);
    bodyGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, at + v.bodyDur);
    osc.connect(bodyGain).connect(audio.destination);
    osc.start(at);
    osc.stop(at + v.bodyDur + 0.008);

    hit(v);
    return true;
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the toggles */

  function toggles() {
    return document.querySelectorAll('[data-sound-toggle]');
  }

  function paint() {
    var list = toggles();
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      list[i].setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(armed));
      list[i].setAttribute(
        'aria-label',
        armed ? 'Turn interface sound off' : 'Turn interface sound on'
      );
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the meter */

  /*
   * A CANVAS THAT SHOWS THE SOUND IT IS ABOUT TO MAKE. It is the toggle's own icon: a flat line
   * while sound is off, a live trace while it is on, and a kick on every press whose height is the
   * press's own body gain. It is entirely optional — a layout without one is silent about it and
   * every other line above still runs.
   *
   * IT IS THE ONLY AMBIENT MOTION THIS FILE OWNS, AND IT STOPS THREE WAYS: it never starts while
   * sound is off, it stops on prefers-reduced-motion, and it stops on visibilitychange. A
   * backgrounded tab must not burn a core for a line nobody is looking at.
   */
  var scope = null;
  var scopeCtx = null;
  var frame = 0;
  var energy = 0;
  var phase = 0;
  var reduced = window.matchMedia ? window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') : null;

  function findScope() {
    var el = document.querySelector('[data-sound-scope]');
    if (!el || !el.getContext) return;
    scope = el;
    scopeCtx = el.getContext('2d');
  }

  function stopped() {
    return !armed || document.hidden === true || !!(reduced && reduced.matches);
  }

  function paintScope() {
    if (!scope || !scopeCtx) return;
    var w = scope.width || 0;
    var h = scope.height || 0;
    if (!w || !h) return;
    var mid = h / 2;
    var ink = '';
    if (window.getComputedStyle) {
      ink = window.getComputedStyle(scope).getPropertyValue('color');
    }
    scopeCtx.clearRect(0, 0, w, h);
    scopeCtx.beginPath();
    for (var x = 0; x <= w; x += 2) {
      var k = x / w;
      var taper = Math.sin(Math.PI * k);
      var wave = Math.sin(k * 14 + phase) * 0.55 + Math.sin(k * 31 - phase * 1.7) * 0.45;
      var amp = (0.16 + energy * 0.84) * (mid - 1.5) * taper;
      var y = mid + wave * amp;
      if (x === 0) scopeCtx.moveTo(x, y);
      else scopeCtx.lineTo(x, y);
    }
    scopeCtx.strokeStyle = ink ? ink.trim() : 'currentColor';
    scopeCtx.lineWidth = 2;
    scopeCtx.stroke();
  }

  function tickScope() {
    if (stopped()) { frame = 0; paintScope(); return; }
    phase += 0.06;
    energy *= 0.9;
    if (energy < 0.004) energy = 0;
    paintScope();
    frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tickScope);
  }

  function runScope() {
    /* The CSS half of the same stop. Every ambient rule in InterfaceSound.astro is paused by this
       attribute, so prefers-reduced-motion, a hidden tab and "sound is off" all halt the keyframes
       as well as the canvas — one predicate, not two that can disagree. */
    var still = stopped();
    if (document.documentElement && document.documentElement.setAttribute) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-sound-still', still ? 'true' : 'false');
    }
    if (!scope) return;
    if (frame) { window.cancelAnimationFrame(frame); frame = 0; }
    if (still) { paintScope(); return; }
    frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tickScope);
  }

  /** The visible half of a press: the meter kicks, and the control flashes its ring. */
  function hit(v) {
    energy = Math.min(1, 0.55 + v.bodyGain * 6);
    runScope();
    var list = toggles();
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var el = list[i];
      if (!el.classList) continue;
      el.classList.remove('is-hit');
      /* Reading offsetWidth restarts a CSS animation that is already running; without it a second
         press inside the animation's own duration adds a class that is already there and nothing
         plays. */
      void el.offsetWidth;
      el.classList.add('is-hit');
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the dock's place */

  /*
   * A FLOATING CONTROL MUST NOT COVER A CONTROL, and this one did.
   *
   * MEASURED, on the built landing, at nine viewport sizes: at 740x360 and 667x375 — a phone held
   * sideways — the hero fills the screen, the corner the dock floats in lands ON the composer, and
   * 66x13 of the SEND BUTTON was underneath it. Both corners: moving it left is no fix, because the
   * composer spans the width. At 1440x900, 1280x620, 1280x480, 1024x700, 900x560, 800x560 and
   * 390x844 the corner is clear.
   *
   * A media query cannot express that boundary — 1280x480 is clear and 1024x540 is not, so it is
   * not a height rule or a width rule. The dock therefore MEASURES: if its own rectangle overlaps
   * any control, it stops floating and takes its place at the end of the page, where it cannot
   * steal a press. This is the same rule apps/web states as "decoration yields to the composer",
   * applied by the decoration rather than assumed by it.
   *
   * On load and on resize, never on scroll. The composer sits at the top of the page, so scrolling
   * carries it AWAY from a bottom corner; and a control that jumps around while the page scrolls is
   * worse than one that overlaps.
   */
  var CONTROLS = 'button, [role="button"], a[href], input, textarea, select, summary';

  function rectOf(el) {
    return el && el.getBoundingClientRect ? el.getBoundingClientRect() : null;
  }

  function placeDock() {
    var dock = document.querySelector('[data-sound-dock]');
    if (!dock || !dock.getBoundingClientRect || !dock.setAttribute) return;
    /* Measure the floating position, not the one it was last given. */
    if (dock.removeAttribute) dock.removeAttribute('data-flow');
    var d = rectOf(dock);
    if (!d || !d.width || !d.height) return;
    var list = document.querySelectorAll(CONTROLS);
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var el = list[i];
      if (el.closest && el.closest('[data-sound-dock]')) continue;
      var r = rectOf(el);
      if (!r || !r.width || !r.height) continue;
      if (r.left < d.right && r.right > d.left && r.top < d.bottom && r.bottom > d.top) {
        dock.setAttribute('data-flow', '');
        return;
      }
    }
  }

  var placing = 0;
  function schedulePlace() {
    if (placing) return;
    placing = window.requestAnimationFrame(function () { placing = 0; placeDock(); });
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the one listener */

  function voiceFor(el) {
    var explicit = el.getAttribute ? el.getAttribute('data-sound') : null;
    if (explicit === 'primary' || explicit === 'secondary' || explicit === 'toggle') return explicit;
    if (el.hasAttribute && (el.hasAttribute('aria-pressed') || el.hasAttribute('data-theme-toggle'))) {
      return 'toggle';
    }
    var name = el.className;
    if (name && typeof name !== 'string' && typeof name.baseVal === 'string') name = name.baseVal;
    var cls = ' ' + (typeof name === 'string' ? name : '') + ' ';
    if (/\bpill-quiet\b|\biconbtn\b|\bghost\b|\bquiet\b/.test(cls)) return 'secondary';
    if (/\bprimary\b|\bcta\b|\bpill\b/.test(cls)) return 'primary';
    if (el.getAttribute && el.getAttribute('type') === 'submit') return 'primary';
    return 'secondary';
  }

  /*
   * ONE LISTENER FOR BOTH JOBS, which is what makes "never more than once per press" structural
   * rather than a promise. The toggle is a button too: if arming were handled in one listener and
   * pressing in another, the press that arms the sound would make two sounds.
   */
  document.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
    var target = e.target;
    if (!target || !target.closest) return;

    var toggle = target.closest('[data-sound-toggle]');
    if (toggle) {
      armed = !armed;
      if (armed) {
        ensureAudio();
        if (audio && audio.resume) audio.resume();
      }
      remember(armed);
      paint();
      if (armed) press('toggle');
      runScope();
      return;
    }

    var control = target.closest(PRESSABLE);
    if (!control) return;
    if (control.getAttribute && control.getAttribute('data-sound') === 'none') return;
    if (control.hasAttribute && control.hasAttribute('disabled')) return;
    /* A choice carried over from a previous visit arms on this session's first press — still a
       gesture, still never at load. */
    if (armed && !audio) {
      ensureAudio();
      if (audio && audio.resume) audio.resume();
    }
    press(voiceFor(control));
  });

  document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', runScope);
  window.addEventListener('resize', schedulePlace);
  if (reduced) {
    if (reduced.addEventListener) reduced.addEventListener('change', runScope);
    else if (reduced.addListener) reduced.addListener(runScope);
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ boot */

  findScope();
  placeDock();
  paint();
  paintScope();
  runScope();

  /* The public surface. `appleTick` is the retired name and is kept aimed at the new synth, so
     anything that already called it gets a keyswitch instead of a chisel tick rather than an
     error. */
  window.appleSound = {
    press: press,
    isOn: function () { return armed; },
    voices: VOICES
  };
  window.appleTick = function () { return press('secondary'); };
})();

data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>Docs</p> <h1 class="carved" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>Updating the plugin</h1> <div class="prose" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>  <p>
Roblox does not update Studio plugins automatically. There is no silent background update and
    nothing happens on restart — a person has to press a button. That is platform behaviour, not an
    Apple choice, and it is why this page exists at all.
</p> <h2>How to update</h2> <ol> <li>
In Studio, open the plugin management window — Roblox's documentation calls it
<strong>Plugin Management</strong>; the <strong>Plugins</strong> tab opens it via
<strong>Manage Plugins</strong>.
</li> <li>Find <strong>Apple</strong> and press its <strong>Update</strong> button.</li> </ol> <p>
There is also an <strong>Update all Plugins</strong> button. Roblox staff confirmed in April
    2026 that the bulk button was broken and a fix was coming, and that the individual
<strong>Update</strong> buttons still work. If the bulk button does nothing, use the per-plugin
    one.
</p> <h2>How you'll know</h2> <p>
You do not have to check. The plugin tells the server which build it is on every time it polls,
    and the server answers.
</p> <ul> <li> <strong>An amber line in the panel</strong> when a newer build is published — for example
<em>“Apple 1.1.0 is available. Update it in Studio → Plugins → Manage Plugins → Update.”</em>
It is also written to Studio's Output window <em>once</em> per message, not on every poll.
</li> <li> <strong>A red line</strong> in the rare case where a build is genuinely too old for the server
      to work with. That one blocks builds and is not advisory.
</li> <li> <strong>Silence</strong> the rest of the time, which is the normal state.
</li> </ul> <h2>Which build am I on?</h2> <p>
The Apple panel prints it at the bottom, as <code>Apple Studio · 1.0.0 · independent preview</code>. The web
    workspace shows the same version under <strong>Studio</strong> in the project rail once the
    plugin has reported in. What changed between builds is on the
<a href="/changelog">changelog</a>.
</p> <p>
Two numbers, because they answer different questions. <strong>Version</strong> is the build you
    have, and it moves on every release including cosmetic ones. <strong>Protocol</strong> is the
    contract the plugin and the server speak, and it almost never moves.
</p> <h2>Running an old build is fine</h2> <p>
Apple's server decides whether to talk to a plugin by <em>protocol</em>, never by version. A
    plugin several releases behind is served normally as long as it still speaks a contract the
    server supports — and today the server supports every protocol that has ever shipped, so nothing
    in the wild is refused.
</p> <p>
This is deliberate. Because updates require you to notice a message and click a button in a
    different window, a server that refused old clients would strand people with no self-service way
    out. Version skew is the expected steady state here, not an error to be stamped out. What you
    miss by staying behind is new capability and fixes, not access.
</p> <div class="callout"> <p> <strong>If an update drops the connection.</strong> Your project link lives in the plugin's
      own saved settings rather than in the build, so it normally survives an update. If the panel
      comes back as <strong>Not connected</strong>, nothing is wrong and nothing is lost —
<a href="/docs/connect">connect again</a> with a new code.
</p> </div>  </div> <footer class="docs__foot" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj> <p data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>

<a href="mailto:apple.labs.app@gmail.com" data-astro-cid-mw7aashj>apple.labs.app@gmail.com</a>.
</p> </footer> </article> </div>  </main> <footer class="foot" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <div class="wrap" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <div class="foot__grid" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <div class="foot__brand" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <a href="/" class="brand" aria-label="Apple — home" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <svg width="26" height="26" viewBox="0 0 32 32" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true" class="gm " data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m> <path d="M5 24 12 5 19 14 27 8 21 27 13 18Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".1" data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m></path> <path d="m5 24 7-19 7 9 8-6-6 19-8-9-8 6Z" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linejoin="round" data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m></path> <path d="m12 5 1 13 6-4 2 13" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.2" data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m></path> </svg>  <span class="brand__word" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Apple</span> </a> <p class="foot__tag" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>It works inside the place you already have open.</p>  <p class="mono" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Apple Labs</p> </div> <nav aria-label="Product" class="foot__col" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <h2 data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Product</h2> <ul data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>  <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/docs/getting-started" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>How it works</a></li>  <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/proof" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Proof</a></li> <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/docs/modes" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Modes</a></li> <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/changelog" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Changelog</a></li> <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/pricing" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Pricing</a></li>  <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/status" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Status &amp; </p> </div> </div> </footer>   <script>/* =====================================================================================
 * INTERFACE SOUND — ONE IMPLEMENTATION, SHARED BY EVERY LAYOUT.
 *
 * This file is the whole sound system. Base.astro and Landing.astro both inline THIS TEXT
 * through layouts/InterfaceSound.astro, so there is one synth, one listener and one stored
 * preference for the entire site. Before this there was a copy in Base.astro and nothing at all
 * on the front page, which is two states that cannot agree and one page with no control.
 *
 * WHAT THE OWNER ASKED FOR. He played with rosebud.ai and singled out one thing: pressing a button
 * makes a satisfying mechanical keyboard click. Measured on that page the same day (recorded in
 * packages/corpus/data/ui-references/web-landing.json, claim 16): its resource timing list contains
 * no mp3, wav, ogg, m4a or webm anywhere, while AudioContext is available — so their click is
 * SYNTHESISED at interaction time, not downloaded. That is the cheaper technique and the one used
 * here. A synthesised click costs no bytes, has no load state, and cannot be the reason a button
 * feels late.
 *
 * WHAT A KEYSWITCH ACTUALLY SOUNDS LIKE, and why the old `tick()` did not. The retired version was
 * one triangle oscillator sliding down — a soft chisel tick, a single event. A mechanical key press
 * is TWO events layered: the CLICK OF THE STEM, a bright noise transient of a few milliseconds with
 * no pitch of its own, and the THOCK OF THE BOTTOM-OUT, a low short body as the key meets the
 * plate. Both are below, layered with the body starting 4ms after the transient, and the whole
 * envelope is finished inside 58ms at its longest voice.
 *
 * THE INTERFACE HAS A VOICE RATHER THAN A BEEP. Three voices, chosen the way the reference's accent
 * family is chosen — one object, three jobs: a primary action is lower and fuller, a secondary
 * lighter and shorter, a toggle a touch brighter. Every press also carries a ±2.5% wobble, because
 * a sound repeated at exactly one frequency stops reading as a mechanism and starts reading as a
 * notification.
 *
 * THE PROPERTIES THIS FILE MUST KEEP, all of them checked by tests/interface-sound.test.mjs:
 *   - OFF by default. Nothing is armed by loading a page.
 *   - The AudioContext is constructed by a PRESS and never by load — the visitor's press on the
 *     toggle, or, when a previous visit already chose sound, that session's first press. Both are
 *     real user gestures, which is what browsers require; neither is page load.
 *   - Nothing autoplays.
 *   - The choice persists exactly the way the theme choice does, in localStorage under
 *     `apple-sound`, and is read back on the next page.
 *   - Every toggle states its state in aria-pressed and aria-label.
 *   - Never on hover, never on load, never more than once per press: ONE delegated listener owns
 *     both the toggle and the press, so a press on the toggle cannot produce two sounds.
 *
 * NO `document.currentScript`. Astro hoists a component <script> into a module script where
 * currentScript is null by specification; a hero effect shipped that way this morning and never ran
 * at all. Everything here is found with querySelector, and every one of those lookups tolerates a
 * null.
 * ===================================================================================== */
(function () {
  'use strict';

  var STORE_KEY = 'apple-sound';

  /* Everything that reads as a press. Buttons and links-as-buttons across both layouts: the
     landing's `.pill`, the chrome's `.iconbtn` and `.nav__cta`, anything with an explicit
     role, and `[data-sound-press]` for a control that is none of those. A bare prose link is
     deliberately absent — navigation is not a keystroke. */
  var PRESSABLE = [
    'button',
    '[role="button"]',
    'input[type="submit"]',
    'input[type="button"]',
    'summary',
    'a.pill',
    'a.btn',
    'a.cta',
    'a.button',
    'a.nav__cta',
    'a.nav__signin',
    'a[data-cta]',
    '[data-sound-press]'
  ].join(', ');

  /* THE THREE VOICES. clickHz is the band the stem transient sits in, bodyHz the pitch of the
     bottom-out. Gains are deliberately low: this is a texture under a finger, not an alert. */
  var VOICES = {
    primary:   { clickHz: 2400, clickQ: 0.9, clickGain: 0.034, clickDur: 0.010, bodyHz: 132, bodyGain: 0.075, bodyDur: 0.044 },
    secondary: { clickHz: 3200, clickQ: 1.1, clickGain: 0.026, clickDur: 0.008, bodyHz: 196, bodyGain: 0.048, bodyDur: 0.032 },
    toggle:    { clickHz: 4200, clickQ: 1.3, clickGain: 0.036, clickDur: 0.007, bodyHz: 240, bodyGain: 0.052, bodyDur: 0.030 }
  };

  var audio = null;       // constructed by a press, never by load
  var grain = null;       // the noise buffer, built once per context
  var armed = stored();   // the visitor's persisted choice; false on a first visit

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ preference */

  function stored() {
    try {
      return localStorage.getItem(STORE_KEY) === 'on';
    } catch (err) {
      return false; /* private mode — off, which is the default anyway */
    }
  }

  function remember(on) {
    try {
      localStorage.setItem(STORE_KEY, on ? 'on' : 'off');
    } catch (err) {
      /* private mode — the choice still applies for this page view */
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the synth */

  /** Construct the context. Called from the click handler and from nowhere else. */
  function ensureAudio() {
    if (audio) return audio;
    /* The prefixed name is Safari's, and it is still how an older iOS reaches this API. The cast
       is for the type checker only; there is no TypeScript in a file that ships as it is written. */
    var w = /** @type {any} */ (window);
    var Ctx = w.AudioContext || w.webkitAudioContext;
    if (!Ctx) return null;
    audio = new Ctx();
    return audio;
  }

  /** A short burst of decaying white noise, built once and re-triggered per press. */
  function noise(ac) {
    if (grain) return grain;
    var rate = ac.sampleRate || 44100;
    var len = Math.max(64, Math.floor(rate * 0.06));
    var buf = ac.createBuffer(1, len, rate);
    var data = buf.getChannelData(0);
    for (var i = 0; i < len; i++) {
      data[i] = (Math.random() * 2 - 1) * (1 - i / len);
    }
    grain = buf;
    return grain;
  }

  /**
   * ONE PRESS. Two layered events, under 60ms, at a low gain.
   * Silent unless armed, and silent unless a press has already built the context.
   */
  function press(kind) {
    if (!armed || !audio) return false;
    if (audio.state === 'suspended' && audio.resume) audio.resume();

    var v = VOICES[kind] || VOICES.secondary;
    var t = audio.currentTime;
    var wobble = 1 + (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.05;

    /* 1. THE CLICK OF THE STEM — filtered noise, no pitch, gone in a few milliseconds. */
    var src = audio.createBufferSource();
    src.buffer = noise(audio);
    var band = audio.createBiquadFilter();
    band.type = 'bandpass';
    band.frequency.setValueAtTime(v.clickHz * wobble, t);
    band.Q.value = v.clickQ;
    var clickGain = audio.createGain();
    clickGain.gain.setValueAtTime(v.clickGain, t);
    clickGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, t + v.clickDur);
    src.connect(band).connect(clickGain).connect(audio.destination);
    src.start(t);
    src.stop(t + v.clickDur + 0.004);

    /* 2. THE THOCK OF THE BOTTOM-OUT — a low body, pitched down as it dies. */
    var at = t + 0.004;
    var osc = audio.createOscillator();
    osc.type = 'triangle';
    osc.frequency.setValueAtTime(v.bodyHz * wobble, at);
    osc.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(v.bodyHz * 0.55, at + v.bodyDur);
    var bodyGain = audio.createGain();
    bodyGain.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, at);
    bodyGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(v.bodyGain, at + 0.003);
    bodyGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, at + v.bodyDur);
    osc.connect(bodyGain).connect(audio.destination);
    osc.start(at);
    osc.stop(at + v.bodyDur + 0.008);

    hit(v);
    return true;
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the toggles */

  function toggles() {
    return document.querySelectorAll('[data-sound-toggle]');
  }

  function paint() {
    var list = toggles();
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      list[i].setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(armed));
      list[i].setAttribute(
        'aria-label',
        armed ? 'Turn interface sound off' : 'Turn interface sound on'
      );
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the meter */

  /*
   * A CANVAS THAT SHOWS THE SOUND IT IS ABOUT TO MAKE. It is the toggle's own icon: a flat line
   * while sound is off, a live trace while it is on, and a kick on every press whose height is the
   * press's own body gain. It is entirely optional — a layout without one is silent about it and
   * every other line above still runs.
   *
   * IT IS THE ONLY AMBIENT MOTION THIS FILE OWNS, AND IT STOPS THREE WAYS: it never starts while
   * sound is off, it stops on prefers-reduced-motion, and it stops on visibilitychange. A
   * backgrounded tab must not burn a core for a line nobody is looking at.
   */
  var scope = null;
  var scopeCtx = null;
  var frame = 0;
  var energy = 0;
  var phase = 0;
  var reduced = window.matchMedia ? window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') : null;

  function findScope() {
    var el = document.querySelector('[data-sound-scope]');
    if (!el || !el.getContext) return;
    scope = el;
    scopeCtx = el.getContext('2d');
  }

  function stopped() {
    return !armed || document.hidden === true || !!(reduced && reduced.matches);
  }

  function paintScope() {
    if (!scope || !scopeCtx) return;
    var w = scope.width || 0;
    var h = scope.height || 0;
    if (!w || !h) return;
    var mid = h / 2;
    var ink = '';
    if (window.getComputedStyle) {
      ink = window.getComputedStyle(scope).getPropertyValue('color');
    }
    scopeCtx.clearRect(0, 0, w, h);
    scopeCtx.beginPath();
    for (var x = 0; x <= w; x += 2) {
      var k = x / w;
      var taper = Math.sin(Math.PI * k);
      var wave = Math.sin(k * 14 + phase) * 0.55 + Math.sin(k * 31 - phase * 1.7) * 0.45;
      var amp = (0.16 + energy * 0.84) * (mid - 1.5) * taper;
      var y = mid + wave * amp;
      if (x === 0) scopeCtx.moveTo(x, y);
      else scopeCtx.lineTo(x, y);
    }
    scopeCtx.strokeStyle = ink ? ink.trim() : 'currentColor';
    scopeCtx.lineWidth = 2;
    scopeCtx.stroke();
  }

  function tickScope() {
    if (stopped()) { frame = 0; paintScope(); return; }
    phase += 0.06;
    energy *= 0.9;
    if (energy < 0.004) energy = 0;
    paintScope();
    frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tickScope);
  }

  function runScope() {
    /* The CSS half of the same stop. Every ambient rule in InterfaceSound.astro is paused by this
       attribute, so prefers-reduced-motion, a hidden tab and "sound is off" all halt the keyframes
       as well as the canvas — one predicate, not two that can disagree. */
    var still = stopped();
    if (document.documentElement && document.documentElement.setAttribute) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-sound-still', still ? 'true' : 'false');
    }
    if (!scope) return;
    if (frame) { window.cancelAnimationFrame(frame); frame = 0; }
    if (still) { paintScope(); return; }
    frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tickScope);
  }

  /** The visible half of a press: the meter kicks, and the control flashes its ring. */
  function hit(v) {
    energy = Math.min(1, 0.55 + v.bodyGain * 6);
    runScope();
    var list = toggles();
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var el = list[i];
      if (!el.classList) continue;
      el.classList.remove('is-hit');
      /* Reading offsetWidth restarts a CSS animation that is already running; without it a second
         press inside the animation's own duration adds a class that is already there and nothing
         plays. */
      void el.offsetWidth;
      el.classList.add('is-hit');
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the dock's place */

  /*
   * A FLOATING CONTROL MUST NOT COVER A CONTROL, and this one did.
   *
   * MEASURED, on the built landing, at nine viewport sizes: at 740x360 and 667x375 — a phone held
   * sideways — the hero fills the screen, the corner the dock floats in lands ON the composer, and
   * 66x13 of the SEND BUTTON was underneath it. Both corners: moving it left is no fix, because the
   * composer spans the width. At 1440x900, 1280x620, 1280x480, 1024x700, 900x560, 800x560 and
   * 390x844 the corner is clear.
   *
   * A media query cannot express that boundary — 1280x480 is clear and 1024x540 is not, so it is
   * not a height rule or a width rule. The dock therefore MEASURES: if its own rectangle overlaps
   * any control, it stops floating and takes its place at the end of the page, where it cannot
   * steal a press. This is the same rule apps/web states as "decoration yields to the composer",
   * applied by the decoration rather than assumed by it.
   *
   * On load and on resize, never on scroll. The composer sits at the top of the page, so scrolling
   * carries it AWAY from a bottom corner; and a control that jumps around while the page scrolls is
   * worse than one that overlaps.
   */
  var CONTROLS = 'button, [role="button"], a[href], input, textarea, select, summary';

  function rectOf(el) {
    return el && el.getBoundingClientRect ? el.getBoundingClientRect() : null;
  }

  function placeDock() {
    var dock = document.querySelector('[data-sound-dock]');
    if (!dock || !dock.getBoundingClientRect || !dock.setAttribute) return;
    /* Measure the floating position, not the one it was last given. */
    if (dock.removeAttribute) dock.removeAttribute('data-flow');
    var d = rectOf(dock);
    if (!d || !d.width || !d.height) return;
    var list = document.querySelectorAll(CONTROLS);
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var el = list[i];
      if (el.closest && el.closest('[data-sound-dock]')) continue;
      var r = rectOf(el);
      if (!r || !r.width || !r.height) continue;
      if (r.left < d.right && r.right > d.left && r.top < d.bottom && r.bottom > d.top) {
        dock.setAttribute('data-flow', '');
        return;
      }
    }
  }

  var placing = 0;
  function schedulePlace() {
    if (placing) return;
    placing = window.requestAnimationFrame(function () { placing = 0; placeDock(); });
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the one listener */

  function voiceFor(el) {
    var explicit = el.getAttribute ? el.getAttribute('data-sound') : null;
    if (explicit === 'primary' || explicit === 'secondary' || explicit === 'toggle') return explicit;
    if (el.hasAttribute && (el.hasAttribute('aria-pressed') || el.hasAttribute('data-theme-toggle'))) {
      return 'toggle';
    }
    var name = el.className;
    if (name && typeof name !== 'string' && typeof name.baseVal === 'string') name = name.baseVal;
    var cls = ' ' + (typeof name === 'string' ? name : '') + ' ';
    if (/\bpill-quiet\b|\biconbtn\b|\bghost\b|\bquiet\b/.test(cls)) return 'secondary';
    if (/\bprimary\b|\bcta\b|\bpill\b/.test(cls)) return 'primary';
    if (el.getAttribute && el.getAttribute('type') === 'submit') return 'primary';
    return 'secondary';
  }

  /*
   * ONE LISTENER FOR BOTH JOBS, which is what makes "never more than once per press" structural
   * rather than a promise. The toggle is a button too: if arming were handled in one listener and
   * pressing in another, the press that arms the sound would make two sounds.
   */
  document.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
    var target = e.target;
    if (!target || !target.closest) return;

    var toggle = target.closest('[data-sound-toggle]');
    if (toggle) {
      armed = !armed;
      if (armed) {
        ensureAudio();
        if (audio && audio.resume) audio.resume();
      }
      remember(armed);
      paint();
      if (armed) press('toggle');
      runScope();
      return;
    }

    var control = target.closest(PRESSABLE);
    if (!control) return;
    if (control.getAttribute && control.getAttribute('data-sound') === 'none') return;
    if (control.hasAttribute && control.hasAttribute('disabled')) return;
    /* A choice carried over from a previous visit arms on this session's first press — still a
       gesture, still never at load. */
    if (armed && !audio) {
      ensureAudio();
      if (audio && audio.resume) audio.resume();
    }
    press(voiceFor(control));
  });

  document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', runScope);
  window.addEventListener('resize', schedulePlace);
  if (reduced) {
    if (reduced.addEventListener) reduced.addEventListener('change', runScope);
    else if (reduced.addListener) reduced.addListener(runScope);
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ boot */

  findScope();
  placeDock();
  paint();
  paintScope();
  runScope();

  /* The public surface. `appleTick` is the retired name and is kept aimed at the new synth, so
     anything that already called it gets a keyswitch instead of a chisel tick rather than an
     error. */
  window.appleSound = {
    press: press,
    isOn: function () { return armed; },
    voices: VOICES
  };
  window.appleTick = function () { return press('secondary'); };
})();

          across the whole service, which is roughly  14 accounts building flat out. When
          that day's pool is gone, a run stops with “Apple has reached today's shared building
          capacity” even though your own balance still shows Credits. It resets at midnight UTC, the
          same instant for everyone, and the steps that already finished stay done and stay paid for.  <a href="/docs/credits-and-limits" data-astro-cid-lmkygsfs>How the two limits differ</a>.

These are internal work-mode estimates, not the Apple and Apple MAX model selector.
          Final usage depends on the work performed.

An Agent request settles against the work it actually did, so a long build costs more than
        the entry price above — metered live, so you always see where you stand. Apple&rsquo;s own
        housekeeping does not count against your quota.
</p>  <p class="tfoot" data-reveal data-astro-cid-lmkygsfs> <strong data-astro-cid-lmkygsfs>A request is not a build.</strong> The counts above are requests at the entry price.
        A whole quality-gated build — read the tree, edit the scripts, create the instances, then
        render it and critique the picture — is about 77 Credits, which is  3 of them a free day and 30 a free month. That is
        the figure the plan cards above are counted in.
</p> </div> </section>  <section class="section limitsec" aria-labelledby="limits-title" data-astro-cid-lmkygsfs> <div class="wrap wrap-narrow-ish" data-astro-cid-lmkygsfs> <header class="sechead" data-astro-cid-lmkygsfs> <p class="eyebrow" data-reveal data-astro-cid-lmkygsfs>The honest part</p> <h2 id="limits-title" data-reveal class="carved" data-astro-cid-lmkygsfs>Limits, plainly stated</h2> </header> <div data-reveal data-reveal-delay="90" data-astro-cid-lmkygsfs> <div class="faq" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <details class="faq__item" style="--i:0" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <summary data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <span class="faq__q" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr>What happens when I run out of Credits?</span> <span class="faq__mark" aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr></span> </summary> <div class="faq__a" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr><p>Apple tells you plainly, mid-conversation, and shows when your quota resets (daily, at midnight UTC — the same instant for everyone, not 24 hours after you started). Nothing is lost — your chat, project and checkpoints stay exactly where they are. You can keep reading, browsing your project and restoring checkpoints; only new AI requests wait for the reset. If it is the <em>monthly</em> ceiling you have reached rather than the day's, the next reset that helps you is the start of the month, and the workspace says which of the two you hit.</p></div> </details><details class="faq__item" style="--i:1" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <summary data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <span class="faq__q" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr>Why is there a limit at all?</span> <span class="faq__mark" aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr></span> </summary> <div class="faq__a" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr><p>Apple runs real inference on every request, and inference costs real compute. A hard daily quota is how the free tier stays genuinely free — no card required, no surprise bill, no "free trial" countdown. We would rather give you an honest daily allowance than an unlimited plan with an asterisk.</p></div> </details><details class="faq__item" style="--i:2" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <summary data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <span class="faq__q" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr>Do unused Credits roll over?</span> <span class="faq__mark" aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr></span> </summary> <div class="faq__a" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr><p>No. Credits reset to your full daily amount each day, up to your plan's monthly ceiling. Rollover sounds nice but pushes people to hoard; a fresh daily allowance keeps the math simple and the queue fair.</p><p><strong>On Free the monthly ceiling is the one that bites.</strong> 231 a day against 2,310 a month is <strong>10 full days</strong>; spend the whole daily allowance every day and there is nothing left for the rest of the month. Whichever limit is lower is the one you actually have, and the workspace shows both.</p></div> </details><details class="faq__item" style="--i:3" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <summary data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <span class="faq__q" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr>Can one request cost more than the price in the table?</span> <span class="faq__mark" aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr></span> </summary> <div class="faq__a" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr><p>Yes, and it is metered transparently. The table quotes what a request starts at; an Agent build settles against the compute it actually used, so a long one costs more. You see the running total live in the workspace while it climbs, and if a run reaches the end of your Credits it stops there and says so — everything it finished by then is saved, and the allowance refills at midnight UTC.</p></div> </details><details class="faq__item" style="--i:4" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <summary data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <span class="faq__q" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr>What is a Credit, underneath?</span> <span class="faq__mark" aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr></span> </summary> <div class="faq__a" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr><p>A unit of real compute. One Credit is 30 neurons, and Apple bills from the engine's own reported figure for each call rather than from an estimate. A <strong>quality-gated</strong> build — read the tree, edit scripts, create instances, then render it and critique the picture — measures about 2,300 neurons, which is the 77 Credits the allowances above are counted in. The same build with the critique left out measured 511; we price the one that looked at what it made.</p></div> </details><details class="faq__item" style="--i:5" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <summary data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr> <span class="faq__q" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr>Can I subscribe now?</span> <span class="faq__mark" aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr></span> </summary> <div class="faq__a" data-astro-cid-al2ca2vr><p>Paid checkout is not open yet. Builder and Studio are the planned subscription tiers. Your account’s Plans &amp; Credits page shows live purchase availability; no subscription starts without a confirmed checkout.</p></div> </details> </div>  </div> </div> </section>  </main> <footer class="foot" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <div class="wrap" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <div class="foot__grid" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <div class="foot__brand" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <a href="/" class="brand" aria-label="Apple — home" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <svg width="26" height="26" viewBox="0 0 32 32" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true" class="gm " data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m> <path d="M5 24 12 5 19 14 27 8 21 27 13 18Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".1" data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m></path> <path d="m5 24 7-19 7 9 8-6-6 19-8-9-8 6Z" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linejoin="round" data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m></path> <path d="m12 5 1 13 6-4 2 13" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.2" data-astro-cid-wo2cit4m></path> </svg>  <span class="brand__word" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Apple</span> </a> <p class="foot__tag" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>It works inside the place you already have open.</p>  <p class="mono" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Apple Labs</p> </div> <nav aria-label="Product" class="foot__col" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte> <h2 data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Product</h2> <ul data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>  <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/docs/getting-started" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>How it works</a></li>  <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/proof" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Proof</a></li> <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/docs/modes" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Modes</a></li> <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/changelog" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Changelog</a></li> <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/pricing" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Pricing</a></li>  <li data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte><a href="/status" data-astro-cid-sz7xmlte>Status &amp; </p> </div> </div> </footer>   <script>/* =====================================================================================
 * INTERFACE SOUND — ONE IMPLEMENTATION, SHARED BY EVERY LAYOUT.
 *
 * This file is the whole sound system. Base.astro and Landing.astro both inline THIS TEXT
 * through layouts/InterfaceSound.astro, so there is one synth, one listener and one stored
 * preference for the entire site. Before this there was a copy in Base.astro and nothing at all
 * on the front page, which is two states that cannot agree and one page with no control.
 *
 * WHAT THE OWNER ASKED FOR. He played with rosebud.ai and singled out one thing: pressing a button
 * makes a satisfying mechanical keyboard click. Measured on that page the same day (recorded in
 * packages/corpus/data/ui-references/web-landing.json, claim 16): its resource timing list contains
 * no mp3, wav, ogg, m4a or webm anywhere, while AudioContext is available — so their click is
 * SYNTHESISED at interaction time, not downloaded. That is the cheaper technique and the one used
 * here. A synthesised click costs no bytes, has no load state, and cannot be the reason a button
 * feels late.
 *
 * WHAT A KEYSWITCH ACTUALLY SOUNDS LIKE, and why the old `tick()` did not. The retired version was
 * one triangle oscillator sliding down — a soft chisel tick, a single event. A mechanical key press
 * is TWO events layered: the CLICK OF THE STEM, a bright noise transient of a few milliseconds with
 * no pitch of its own, and the THOCK OF THE BOTTOM-OUT, a low short body as the key meets the
 * plate. Both are below, layered with the body starting 4ms after the transient, and the whole
 * envelope is finished inside 58ms at its longest voice.
 *
 * THE INTERFACE HAS A VOICE RATHER THAN A BEEP. Three voices, chosen the way the reference's accent
 * family is chosen — one object, three jobs: a primary action is lower and fuller, a secondary
 * lighter and shorter, a toggle a touch brighter. Every press also carries a ±2.5% wobble, because
 * a sound repeated at exactly one frequency stops reading as a mechanism and starts reading as a
 * notification.
 *
 * THE PROPERTIES THIS FILE MUST KEEP, all of them checked by tests/interface-sound.test.mjs:
 *   - OFF by default. Nothing is armed by loading a page.
 *   - The AudioContext is constructed by a PRESS and never by load — the visitor's press on the
 *     toggle, or, when a previous visit already chose sound, that session's first press. Both are
 *     real user gestures, which is what browsers require; neither is page load.
 *   - Nothing autoplays.
 *   - The choice persists exactly the way the theme choice does, in localStorage under
 *     `apple-sound`, and is read back on the next page.
 *   - Every toggle states its state in aria-pressed and aria-label.
 *   - Never on hover, never on load, never more than once per press: ONE delegated listener owns
 *     both the toggle and the press, so a press on the toggle cannot produce two sounds.
 *
 * NO `document.currentScript`. Astro hoists a component <script> into a module script where
 * currentScript is null by specification; a hero effect shipped that way this morning and never ran
 * at all. Everything here is found with querySelector, and every one of those lookups tolerates a
 * null.
 * ===================================================================================== */
(function () {
  'use strict';

  var STORE_KEY = 'apple-sound';

  /* Everything that reads as a press. Buttons and links-as-buttons across both layouts: the
     landing's `.pill`, the chrome's `.iconbtn` and `.nav__cta`, anything with an explicit
     role, and `[data-sound-press]` for a control that is none of those. A bare prose link is
     deliberately absent — navigation is not a keystroke. */
  var PRESSABLE = [
    'button',
    '[role="button"]',
    'input[type="submit"]',
    'input[type="button"]',
    'summary',
    'a.pill',
    'a.btn',
    'a.cta',
    'a.button',
    'a.nav__cta',
    'a.nav__signin',
    'a[data-cta]',
    '[data-sound-press]'
  ].join(', ');

  /* THE THREE VOICES. clickHz is the band the stem transient sits in, bodyHz the pitch of the
     bottom-out. Gains are deliberately low: this is a texture under a finger, not an alert. */
  var VOICES = {
    primary:   { clickHz: 2400, clickQ: 0.9, clickGain: 0.034, clickDur: 0.010, bodyHz: 132, bodyGain: 0.075, bodyDur: 0.044 },
    secondary: { clickHz: 3200, clickQ: 1.1, clickGain: 0.026, clickDur: 0.008, bodyHz: 196, bodyGain: 0.048, bodyDur: 0.032 },
    toggle:    { clickHz: 4200, clickQ: 1.3, clickGain: 0.036, clickDur: 0.007, bodyHz: 240, bodyGain: 0.052, bodyDur: 0.030 }
  };

  var audio = null;       // constructed by a press, never by load
  var grain = null;       // the noise buffer, built once per context
  var armed = stored();   // the visitor's persisted choice; false on a first visit

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ preference */

  function stored() {
    try {
      return localStorage.getItem(STORE_KEY) === 'on';
    } catch (err) {
      return false; /* private mode — off, which is the default anyway */
    }
  }

  function remember(on) {
    try {
      localStorage.setItem(STORE_KEY, on ? 'on' : 'off');
    } catch (err) {
      /* private mode — the choice still applies for this page view */
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the synth */

  /** Construct the context. Called from the click handler and from nowhere else. */
  function ensureAudio() {
    if (audio) return audio;
    /* The prefixed name is Safari's, and it is still how an older iOS reaches this API. The cast
       is for the type checker only; there is no TypeScript in a file that ships as it is written. */
    var w = /** @type {any} */ (window);
    var Ctx = w.AudioContext || w.webkitAudioContext;
    if (!Ctx) return null;
    audio = new Ctx();
    return audio;
  }

  /** A short burst of decaying white noise, built once and re-triggered per press. */
  function noise(ac) {
    if (grain) return grain;
    var rate = ac.sampleRate || 44100;
    var len = Math.max(64, Math.floor(rate * 0.06));
    var buf = ac.createBuffer(1, len, rate);
    var data = buf.getChannelData(0);
    for (var i = 0; i < len; i++) {
      data[i] = (Math.random() * 2 - 1) * (1 - i / len);
    }
    grain = buf;
    return grain;
  }

  /**
   * ONE PRESS. Two layered events, under 60ms, at a low gain.
   * Silent unless armed, and silent unless a press has already built the context.
   */
  function press(kind) {
    if (!armed || !audio) return false;
    if (audio.state === 'suspended' && audio.resume) audio.resume();

    var v = VOICES[kind] || VOICES.secondary;
    var t = audio.currentTime;
    var wobble = 1 + (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.05;

    /* 1. THE CLICK OF THE STEM — filtered noise, no pitch, gone in a few milliseconds. */
    var src = audio.createBufferSource();
    src.buffer = noise(audio);
    var band = audio.createBiquadFilter();
    band.type = 'bandpass';
    band.frequency.setValueAtTime(v.clickHz * wobble, t);
    band.Q.value = v.clickQ;
    var clickGain = audio.createGain();
    clickGain.gain.setValueAtTime(v.clickGain, t);
    clickGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, t + v.clickDur);
    src.connect(band).connect(clickGain).connect(audio.destination);
    src.start(t);
    src.stop(t + v.clickDur + 0.004);

    /* 2. THE THOCK OF THE BOTTOM-OUT — a low body, pitched down as it dies. */
    var at = t + 0.004;
    var osc = audio.createOscillator();
    osc.type = 'triangle';
    osc.frequency.setValueAtTime(v.bodyHz * wobble, at);
    osc.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(v.bodyHz * 0.55, at + v.bodyDur);
    var bodyGain = audio.createGain();
    bodyGain.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, at);
    bodyGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(v.bodyGain, at + 0.003);
    bodyGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, at + v.bodyDur);
    osc.connect(bodyGain).connect(audio.destination);
    osc.start(at);
    osc.stop(at + v.bodyDur + 0.008);

    hit(v);
    return true;
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the toggles */

  function toggles() {
    return document.querySelectorAll('[data-sound-toggle]');
  }

  function paint() {
    var list = toggles();
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      list[i].setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(armed));
      list[i].setAttribute(
        'aria-label',
        armed ? 'Turn interface sound off' : 'Turn interface sound on'
      );
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the meter */

  /*
   * A CANVAS THAT SHOWS THE SOUND IT IS ABOUT TO MAKE. It is the toggle's own icon: a flat line
   * while sound is off, a live trace while it is on, and a kick on every press whose height is the
   * press's own body gain. It is entirely optional — a layout without one is silent about it and
   * every other line above still runs.
   *
   * IT IS THE ONLY AMBIENT MOTION THIS FILE OWNS, AND IT STOPS THREE WAYS: it never starts while
   * sound is off, it stops on prefers-reduced-motion, and it stops on visibilitychange. A
   * backgrounded tab must not burn a core for a line nobody is looking at.
   */
  var scope = null;
  var scopeCtx = null;
  var frame = 0;
  var energy = 0;
  var phase = 0;
  var reduced = window.matchMedia ? window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') : null;

  function findScope() {
    var el = document.querySelector('[data-sound-scope]');
    if (!el || !el.getContext) return;
    scope = el;
    scopeCtx = el.getContext('2d');
  }

  function stopped() {
    return !armed || document.hidden === true || !!(reduced && reduced.matches);
  }

  function paintScope() {
    if (!scope || !scopeCtx) return;
    var w = scope.width || 0;
    var h = scope.height || 0;
    if (!w || !h) return;
    var mid = h / 2;
    var ink = '';
    if (window.getComputedStyle) {
      ink = window.getComputedStyle(scope).getPropertyValue('color');
    }
    scopeCtx.clearRect(0, 0, w, h);
    scopeCtx.beginPath();
    for (var x = 0; x <= w; x += 2) {
      var k = x / w;
      var taper = Math.sin(Math.PI * k);
      var wave = Math.sin(k * 14 + phase) * 0.55 + Math.sin(k * 31 - phase * 1.7) * 0.45;
      var amp = (0.16 + energy * 0.84) * (mid - 1.5) * taper;
      var y = mid + wave * amp;
      if (x === 0) scopeCtx.moveTo(x, y);
      else scopeCtx.lineTo(x, y);
    }
    scopeCtx.strokeStyle = ink ? ink.trim() : 'currentColor';
    scopeCtx.lineWidth = 2;
    scopeCtx.stroke();
  }

  function tickScope() {
    if (stopped()) { frame = 0; paintScope(); return; }
    phase += 0.06;
    energy *= 0.9;
    if (energy < 0.004) energy = 0;
    paintScope();
    frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tickScope);
  }

  function runScope() {
    /* The CSS half of the same stop. Every ambient rule in InterfaceSound.astro is paused by this
       attribute, so prefers-reduced-motion, a hidden tab and "sound is off" all halt the keyframes
       as well as the canvas — one predicate, not two that can disagree. */
    var still = stopped();
    if (document.documentElement && document.documentElement.setAttribute) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-sound-still', still ? 'true' : 'false');
    }
    if (!scope) return;
    if (frame) { window.cancelAnimationFrame(frame); frame = 0; }
    if (still) { paintScope(); return; }
    frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tickScope);
  }

  /** The visible half of a press: the meter kicks, and the control flashes its ring. */
  function hit(v) {
    energy = Math.min(1, 0.55 + v.bodyGain * 6);
    runScope();
    var list = toggles();
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var el = list[i];
      if (!el.classList) continue;
      el.classList.remove('is-hit');
      /* Reading offsetWidth restarts a CSS animation that is already running; without it a second
         press inside the animation's own duration adds a class that is already there and nothing
         plays. */
      void el.offsetWidth;
      el.classList.add('is-hit');
    }
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the dock's place */

  /*
   * A FLOATING CONTROL MUST NOT COVER A CONTROL, and this one did.
   *
   * MEASURED, on the built landing, at nine viewport sizes: at 740x360 and 667x375 — a phone held
   * sideways — the hero fills the screen, the corner the dock floats in lands ON the composer, and
   * 66x13 of the SEND BUTTON was underneath it. Both corners: moving it left is no fix, because the
   * composer spans the width. At 1440x900, 1280x620, 1280x480, 1024x700, 900x560, 800x560 and
   * 390x844 the corner is clear.
   *
   * A media query cannot express that boundary — 1280x480 is clear and 1024x540 is not, so it is
   * not a height rule or a width rule. The dock therefore MEASURES: if its own rectangle overlaps
   * any control, it stops floating and takes its place at the end of the page, where it cannot
   * steal a press. This is the same rule apps/web states as "decoration yields to the composer",
   * applied by the decoration rather than assumed by it.
   *
   * On load and on resize, never on scroll. The composer sits at the top of the page, so scrolling
   * carries it AWAY from a bottom corner; and a control that jumps around while the page scrolls is
   * worse than one that overlaps.
   */
  var CONTROLS = 'button, [role="button"], a[href], input, textarea, select, summary';

  function rectOf(el) {
    return el && el.getBoundingClientRect ? el.getBoundingClientRect() : null;
  }

  function placeDock() {
    var dock = document.querySelector('[data-sound-dock]');
    if (!dock || !dock.getBoundingClientRect || !dock.setAttribute) return;
    /* Measure the floating position, not the one it was last given. */
    if (dock.removeAttribute) dock.removeAttribute('data-flow');
    var d = rectOf(dock);
    if (!d || !d.width || !d.height) return;
    var list = document.querySelectorAll(CONTROLS);
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var el = list[i];
      if (el.closest && el.closest('[data-sound-dock]')) continue;
      var r = rectOf(el);
      if (!r || !r.width || !r.height) continue;
      if (r.left < d.right && r.right > d.left && r.top < d.bottom && r.bottom > d.top) {
        dock.setAttribute('data-flow', '');
        return;
      }
    }
  }

  var placing = 0;
  function schedulePlace() {
    if (placing) return;
    placing = window.requestAnimationFrame(function () { placing = 0; placeDock(); });
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the one listener */

  function voiceFor(el) {
    var explicit = el.getAttribute ? el.getAttribute('data-sound') : null;
    if (explicit === 'primary' || explicit === 'secondary' || explicit === 'toggle') return explicit;
    if (el.hasAttribute && (el.hasAttribute('aria-pressed') || el.hasAttribute('data-theme-toggle'))) {
      return 'toggle';
    }
    var name = el.className;
    if (name && typeof name !== 'string' && typeof name.baseVal === 'string') name = name.baseVal;
    var cls = ' ' + (typeof name === 'string' ? name : '') + ' ';
    if (/\bpill-quiet\b|\biconbtn\b|\bghost\b|\bquiet\b/.test(cls)) return 'secondary';
    if (/\bprimary\b|\bcta\b|\bpill\b/.test(cls)) return 'primary';
    if (el.getAttribute && el.getAttribute('type') === 'submit') return 'primary';
    return 'secondary';
  }

  /*
   * ONE LISTENER FOR BOTH JOBS, which is what makes "never more than once per press" structural
   * rather than a promise. The toggle is a button too: if arming were handled in one listener and
   * pressing in another, the press that arms the sound would make two sounds.
   */
  document.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
    var target = e.target;
    if (!target || !target.closest) return;

    var toggle = target.closest('[data-sound-toggle]');
    if (toggle) {
      armed = !armed;
      if (armed) {
        ensureAudio();
        if (audio && audio.resume) audio.resume();
      }
      remember(armed);
      paint();
      if (armed) press('toggle');
      runScope();
      return;
    }

    var control = target.closest(PRESSABLE);
    if (!control) return;
    if (control.getAttribute && control.getAttribute('data-sound') === 'none') return;
    if (control.hasAttribute && control.hasAttribute('disabled')) return;
    /* A choice carried over from a previous visit arms on this session's first press — still a
       gesture, still never at load. */
    if (armed && !audio) {
      ensureAudio();
      if (audio && audio.resume) audio.resume();
    }
    press(voiceFor(control));
  });

  document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', runScope);
  window.addEventListener('resize', schedulePlace);
  if (reduced) {
    if (reduced.addEventListener) reduced.addEventListener('change', runScope);
    else if (reduced.addListener) reduced.addListener(runScope);
  }

  /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ boot */

  findScope();
  placeDock();
  paint();
  paintScope();
  runScope();

  /* The public surface. `appleTick` is the retired name and is kept aimed at the new synth, so
     anything that already called it gets a keyswitch instead of a chisel tick rather than an
     error. */
  window.appleSound = {
    press: press,
    isOn: function () { return armed; },
    voices: VOICES
  };
  window.appleTick = function () { return press('secondary'); };
})();
